### §36.3 Theorem 36.3: Observer-Participant Duality Deepens Wave-Particle Duality


**Theorem 36.3 (Observer-Participant-Duality-Deepens-Wave-Particle-Duality).** The observer-participant duality of Theorems 36.1-36.2 is the deeper structural content underlying the wave-particle duality of Theorem 35.3. The particle-nature IS what the observer (Algebraic Channel) sees; the wave-nature IS what the participant (Geometric Channel) experiences; wave-particle duality emerges as the operational content of the observer-participant duality at every event of $\mathcal{M}$. Neither role is more fundamental; both are simultaneously valid at every event; the bidirectional Wick rotation between them is the operational content of the role transition observed at every measurement event.

**Proof.**

*Step 1 — Assemble the observer-side and participant-side identifications.* From Theorem 36.1, the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel content of $dx_4/dt = ic$ IS the observer-of-$x_4$ reading. From Theorem 35.1, the Algebraic Channel content IS the particle-nature reading. By transitivity, the particle-nature content IS what the observer of $x_4$ sees when watching $x_4$'s invariant expansion pass through. Similarly, from Theorem 36.2, the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel content IS the participant-in-$x_4$ reading; from Theorem 35.2, the Geometric Channel content IS the wave-nature reading; by transitivity, the wave-nature content IS what the participant experiences while riding the expanding McGucken Sphere wavefront.

*Step 2 — Structural depth of observer-participant duality.* The observer-participant duality identifies not merely *what* the two channels present (particle vs. wave, per Theorems 35.1-35.2) but *why* they present these contents structurally: the Algebraic Channel presents localization, discreteness, invariance, and unitary evolution because those are exactly the properties visible from an observer's reference-frame position watching an invariant expansion pass through; the Geometric Channel presents extension, dissipation, probability, and Brownian coupling because those are exactly the properties experienced from a participant's wavefront-riding position on the expanding Sphere. The observer-participant depth explains the two natures rather than merely identifying them.

*Step 3 — Both roles simultaneous at every event.* Any event $q$ of $\mathcal{M}$ admits both roles simultaneously: (a) as observer, matter at $q$ watches $x_4$ pass through with rate $ic$ carrying the invariant substrate-tick content; (b) as participant, matter at $q$ is on the McGucken Sphere expanded from every earlier event $p_0$ (with $q \in \Sigma_+(p_0)$ for all $p_0$ in $q$'s past null cone). The two roles are not mutually exclusive; they are two aspects of matter's presence at event $q$. This is the structural fact that makes wave-particle duality possible: matter has both natures simultaneously because matter plays both roles simultaneously.

*Step 4 — Bidirectional Wick rotation is the role transition.* From Theorem 33.5 (Bidirectional Wick Rotation as Foundational Duality Operation), the forward $W$ and inverse $W^{-1}$ are exact inverse coordinate operations mediating between the two channels. Combined with Theorems 36.1-36.2: forward $W$ takes observer-side content (particle) and converts it to participant-side content (wave) by re-parametrizing $t \to -i\tau$ so that the observer's frame-invariance perspective becomes the participant's wavefront-riding perspective; inverse $W^{-1}$ takes participant-side content (wave) and converts it to observer-side content (particle) by re-parametrizing $\tau \to +it$ so that the participant's wavefront-riding perspective becomes the observer's frame-invariance perspective. The wave-particle transition observed at every measurement event IS the operational content of the observer-participant role transition performed by the apparatus via the physical Wick rotation.

*Step 5 — Refinement of Bohr's complementarity.* From Theorem 35.3 Step 5, Bohr's principle of complementarity was refined into simultaneous dual presence: the two natures are not mutually exclusive; both are present simultaneously. Theorem 36.3 deepens the refinement: the two natures are simultaneously present because the two roles (observer, participant) are simultaneously played by matter at every event. What is mutually exclusive is which role a specific apparatus-arrangement reads out: an apparatus arranged as observer (which-path detector, definite-outcome recorder) reads the Algebraic Channel content of the observer role; an apparatus arranged as participant (double-slit interference screen, wavefront-tracking detector) reads the Geometric Channel content of the participant role. Both readings are possible in principle; a specific apparatus performs one role-reading at a time.

*Step 6 — Structural depth extended to de Broglie relations.* From Theorem 35.3 Step 6, the de Broglie relations $E = \hbar\omega$ and $p = h/\lambda$ connect particle-nature quantities to wave-nature quantities via the substrate-tick invariant $\hbar$. Theorem 36.3 deepens this: the de Broglie relations connect observer-quantities ($E$, $p$ — what the observer measures) to participant-quantities ($\omega$, $\lambda$ — what the participant experiences as wavefront frequency and wavelength) via $\hbar$ — the invariant substrate-tick action-quantum that both roles carry across their $x_4$-expansion content. The de Broglie relations are thus the connecting-substrate content between the two roles, with $\hbar$ playing the load-bearing role.

*Conclusion.* The observer-participant duality of Theorems 36.1-36.2 is the deeper structural content underlying the wave-particle duality of Theorem 35.3. Wave-particle duality emerges as the operational content of the observer-participant duality at every event of $\mathcal{M}$; both roles are simultaneously played by matter at every event; the bidirectional Wick rotation is the operational content of the role transition observed at every measurement event; Bohr's complementarity is refined into simultaneous dual presence of the two roles. QED.

### §36.4 Theorem 36.4: Conservation Laws IS the Invariance of $x_4$-Expansion Passing Through the Observer


**Theorem 36.4 (Conservation-Laws-are-Invariance-of-$x_4$-Passing-Through-Observer).** The three fundamental conservation laws observed in classical and quantum physics — conservation of energy, conservation of linear momentum, and conservation of angular momentum — are the operational manifestation of the invariances that $x_4$'s spherically-symmetric expansion carries as it passes through the observer at every event of $\mathcal{M}$. Under Noether's theorem [86], the three subgroups of the $\mathrm{ISO}(3)$ algebraic-symmetry group of $dx_4/dt = ic$ (Theorem 2) generate the three conservation laws directly: temporal uniformity $\mathbb{R}_t$ → energy conservation; spatial homogeneity $\mathbb{R}^3$ → linear momentum conservation; spatial isotropy $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ → angular momentum conservation.

The observed conservation laws are not additional postulates of physics — they are direct structural consequences of $dx_4/dt = ic$'s invariance at every event of $\mathcal{M}$, converted into observable conservation via Noether's structural machinery applied to the observer's frame invariances.

**Proof.**

*Step 1 — $\mathrm{ISO}(3)$ symmetry content of $dx_4/dt = ic$.* From Theorem 2 of the present paper, the algebraic-symmetry content of $dx_4/dt = ic$ at every event of $\mathcal{M}$ is the $\mathrm{ISO}(3)$ group with three subgroups: $\mathbb{R}_t$ (temporal uniformity), $\mathbb{R}^3$ (spatial homogeneity), $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ (spatial isotropy). Each subgroup encodes one aspect of $x_4$-expansion's invariance: the expansion rate is the same at all times (temporal uniformity); the expansion is the same at all spatial locations (spatial homogeneity); the expansion is spherically symmetric (spatial isotropy).

*Step 2 — Observer's frame invariances.* From Theorem 36.1 Step 3, the observer of $x_4$-expansion measures each of these subgroups as their frame invariances: the observer's frame origin can be shifted temporally without changing the observed physics ($\mathbb{R}_t$-invariance); the observer's spatial position can be shifted without changing the observed physics ($\mathbb{R}^3$-invariance); the observer's spatial orientation can be rotated without changing the observed physics ($\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariance).

*Step 3 — Noether's theorem statement.* From Noether 1918 [86] "Invariante Variationsprobleme": for every continuous symmetry of the action functional of a classical system, there exists a conserved current whose integral over any spacelike hypersurface is a conserved charge. In modern formulation: given a Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}(\phi, \partial\phi)$ invariant under an infinitesimal transformation $\phi \to \phi + \delta\phi$ generated by a continuous parameter $\epsilon$, there exists a Noether current $J^\mu$ such that $\partial_\mu J^\mu = 0$, and the integrated charge $Q = \int J^0 \, d^3x$ is conserved: $dQ/dt = 0$.

*Step 4 — Noether applied to temporal uniformity $\mathbb{R}_t$.* The temporal-uniformity subgroup $\mathbb{R}_t$ generates transformations $t \to t + \epsilon$ for continuous parameter $\epsilon$. Under this transformation, any physical field $\phi(x, t) \to \phi(x, t + \epsilon)$, which is a symmetry of any Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}$ that does not explicitly depend on time. The Noether current associated with this symmetry is the energy-momentum tensor's time-time component $T^{00}$; the conserved charge is the total energy $E = \int T^{00} d^3x$. Consequence: energy is conserved. This is the classical conservation-of-energy law, derived from the temporal-uniformity of $x_4$-expansion.

*Step 5 — Noether applied to spatial homogeneity $\mathbb{R}^3$.* The spatial-homogeneity subgroup $\mathbb{R}^3$ generates translations $\mathbf{x} \to \mathbf{x} + \boldsymbol{\epsilon}$ for continuous parameter vector $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}$. Under this transformation, any physical field $\phi(x, t) \to \phi(x - \boldsymbol{\epsilon}, t)$, which is a symmetry of any Lagrangian that does not explicitly depend on spatial position. The Noether current associated with each of the three spatial-translation directions is the momentum-density $T^{0i}$ ($i = 1, 2, 3$); the conserved charges are the three components of the total momentum $\mathbf{p} = \int T^{0i} d^3x$. Consequence: linear momentum is conserved. This is the classical conservation-of-momentum law, derived from the spatial-homogeneity of $x_4$-expansion.

*Step 6 — Noether applied to spatial isotropy $\mathrm{SO}(3)$.* The spatial-isotropy subgroup $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ generates rotations $\mathbf{x} \to R\mathbf{x}$ for $R \in \mathrm{SO}(3)$. Under this transformation, any physical field $\phi(x, t) \to \phi(R^{-1}\mathbf{x}, t)$, which is a symmetry of any Lagrangian invariant under spatial rotations. The Noether currents associated with the three infinitesimal rotation generators are the three components of the angular-momentum density; the conserved charges are the three components of the total angular momentum $\mathbf{L} = \int \mathbf{x} \times \mathbf{p}\,d^3x$ (for classical mechanics) or the quantum-mechanical angular momentum operator content (for quantum mechanics). Consequence: angular momentum is conserved. This is the classical conservation-of-angular-momentum law, derived from the spatial-isotropy of $x_4$-expansion.

*Step 7 — Structural payoff — conservation laws as invariance content.* Steps 4-6 establish that the three fundamental conservation laws (energy, momentum, angular momentum) are direct structural consequences of the three algebraic-symmetry subgroups of $dx_4/dt = ic$ at every event, converted into observable conservation via Noether's theorem. The observer is subject to these conservation laws because the observer's frame invariances (Step 2) are exactly the invariances of $x_4$-expansion (Step 1), and Noether's theorem generates the conservation laws from those invariances. The conservation laws are not additional physical postulates — they are what the observer sees as the invariant content of $x_4$-expansion passing through their reference frame.

*Step 8 — Extension to further conservation laws.* Other observed conservation laws also descend from $dx_4/dt = ic$'s symmetry content. Electric charge conservation descends from the $\mathrm{U}(1)$ gauge symmetry of the electromagnetic field, which is the $x_4$-expansion's phase-rotation content on the Compton clock (Corollary 32.3.1: $\Delta x_4 = i\lambda_C$ carries the $\mathrm{U}(1)$ phase). Baryon/lepton number conservation descends from the appropriate global symmetries at the corpus-paper level [MGGaugeGroups]. All observed conservation laws are, in the McGucken framework, structural consequences of $dx_4/dt = ic$'s invariance at every event, converted into observable conservation via Noether-type structural arguments.

*Conclusion.* The three fundamental conservation laws — energy, linear momentum, angular momentum — are direct structural consequences of $dx_4/dt = ic$'s invariance at every event of $\mathcal{M}$, as seen by the observer watching $x_4$'s expansion pass through their frame. Noether's theorem is the structural machinery that converts the observer's frame invariances (equivalent to $x_4$-expansion invariances) into the observed conservation laws. Conservation laws IS the invariance of $x_4$-expansion passing through the observer. QED.

### §36.5 Theorem 36.5: Quantum Probability IS the Participant's Coupling to the Expanding Sphere


**Theorem 36.5 (Quantum-Probability-is-Sphere-Coupling-from-Participant).** The quantum probability distribution $|\psi|^2$ observed in the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel reading is the operational manifestation of the participant's coupling to the expanding McGucken Sphere at every event of $\mathcal{M}$. **Proof.**

*Step 1 — Wavefunction on the Sphere is participant's amplitude content.* From Theorem 22.1 (Wavefunction Support and Measurement Projection), the wavefunction $\psi$ has natural support on the actively expanding $x_4$-axis; equivalently (via Theorem 32.1's coordinate identification $\tau = x_4/c$), the wavefunction lives on the McGucken Sphere at every event. The wavefunction's value at the participant's position on the Sphere is the amplitude of the participant's presence at that position.

*Step 2 — Born rule as $W^{-1}$-projection.* From Theorem 22.1 Substep 2c and Theorem 33.4 Part (b), the Sphere-supported wavefunction is $W^{-1}$-projected onto the spatial three-slice via the Born-rule modulus-squared: $\psi \to \psi^*\psi = |\psi|^2$. The projection collapses the null-hypersurface Sphere content onto spatial-slice-local pointwise probability content on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$. Consequence: the Born rule probability $|\psi(\mathbf{x})|^2$ at spatial location $\mathbf{x}$ IS the amplitude-squared content of the participant's position on the Sphere-supported wavefront, projected onto the spatial three-slice.

*Step 3 — Probability distribution shape reflects Sphere-nonlocal null-hypersurface support.* From Theorem 33.2 Part (b), the Sphere-supported wavefunction has Sphere-nonlocal null-hypersurface support extending over the full future null cone from the apex event. The $|\psi(\mathbf{x})|^2$ distribution over the spatial slice is the modulus-squared projection of this extended support, giving a probability distribution that spreads over the spatial region reached by the wavefront. The specific shape of the distribution (Gaussian for free-particle wave packets, atomic-orbital shape for bound states, interference-pattern shape for double-slit experiments) reflects the specific Sphere-history content of the wavefunction's Sphere-supported amplitude.

*Step 4 — Dissipation of probability distributions.* From Theorem 32.7 Part (a) (Sphere Intrinsically Dissipative) and Theorem 32.8 (Compton Content Under Wick Rotation), the amplitude on the participant's wavefront undergoes decay $e^{-\omega_C \tau}$ as the Sphere expands. Consequence: the participant's probability distribution dissipates over time — initially localized probability content spreads over an ever-growing wavefront region, with amplitude density decreasing monotonically. This is the observed dissipation of quantum probability distributions in standard quantum-mechanical evolution: a Gaussian wave packet spreads over time; a particle initially localized becomes progressively delocalized; the probability distribution's variance $\sigma^2(t)$ grows as $\sigma^2(t) \geq \sigma^2(0) + (\hbar t / 2m\sigma(0))^2$ (Heisenberg minimum spread). *Step 5 — Brownian motion from Compton-coupling to expanding Spheres.* From Theorem 4 (Compton coupling per event), the participant Compton-couples to the $x_4$-expansion at every event, receiving substrate-tick advances at rate $\omega_C$. The participant is simultaneously subject to Compton-couplings with expanding Spheres $\Sigma_+(p_i)$ from every surrounding event $p_i$ in the participant's past null cone. Each coupling delivers a stochastic increment of substrate-tick advance (characteristic Compton wavelength $\lambda_C = h/(mc)$). From Theorem 26 (steam-engine thermodynamics with inter-molecular collision rate $\nu_{\rm coll} \sim 10^{10}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ at standard conditions), the participant experiences $\sim 10^{10}$ such stochastic increments per second at the classical thermodynamic scale. The aggregate of these stochastic increments produces observed Brownian motion. Consequence: the participant's Brownian-like stochastic motion IS the aggregate Compton-coupling content to surrounding expanding Spheres.

*Step 6 — Feynman path-integral content as participant surfing-path summation.* The Feynman path integral [252] presents quantum-mechanical evolution as a sum over all possible paths $\gamma$ from initial to final event, weighted by $e^{iS[\gamma]/\hbar}$ where $S[\gamma]$ is the classical action along the path. Feynman's path integral IS the participant's Sphere-history-summation content, with the classical action $S[\gamma]$ per path being the accumulated substrate-tick action of the participant's surfing along that specific Sphere-history.

*Step 7 — Assembling the quantum probability identification.* Steps 1-6 establish that the four load-bearing pieces of the quantum probability content — Born rule modulus-squared, spatial distribution shape reflecting Sphere-nonlocal support, dissipation of probabilities over time, Brownian-like stochastic motion — are each aspects of the participant's coupling to the expanding McGucken Sphere at every event. ### The Hero's-Journey Structural Closure: McGucken Rescuing the Geometric Tradition


We now state the structural-historical closure of the present section in plain terms.

The 1973 MTW abandonment of $x_4 = ict$ (the integrated coordinate shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$) (Theorem 29) was a tragic-irony moment in the history of theoretical physics: the geometrodynamics community, whose foundational program was the recovery of physics as geometry, itself eliminated the geometric content of the imaginary fourth coordinate and adopted the Cartesian-algebraic real time coordinate $x^0 = ct$ as the working convention. The decision was institutional and canonical — from 1973 forward, the standard convention in general-relativity texts is the real time coordinate. The geometric program of physics formally surrendered to the Cartesian-algebraic program at the same page where the geometric content was correctly identified.

The McGucken framework recovers what the geometrodynamics program abandoned. The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ retains the imaginary unit as the algebraic record of $x_4$'s perpendicularity to the spatial three-slice; the McGucken Sphere supplies the active flat-invariant Huygens surface that MTW could not find a way to make work in curved spacetime (the answer is the deformable-spatial-slice / invariant-$x_4$-axis split of Proposition L.1); the dual-channel diagnostic of Theorem 27 separates the Cartesian-algebraic content (which is destroyed by the Wick rotation) from the pre-Cartesian-geometric content (which is preserved). The recovery is not a return to a pre-1973 convention but a structurally deeper reading of the same physical principle that Wheeler and his collaborators were reaching for.

§36 established that the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel is the observer-of-$x_4$ reading (Theorem 36.1) and the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel is the participant-in-$x_4$ reading (Theorem 36.2), with Theorem 36.4 identifying conservation laws as the observer's Noether-shadows of substrate invariance and Theorem 36.5 identifying quantum probability as the participant's Sphere-coupling content. ### §37.1 Theorem 37.1: Dual-Signature Simultaneity — Noether-Conservation and Born-Probability Co-Manifest at Every Quantum Event


**Theorem 37.1 (Dual-Signature-Simultaneity).** Every quantum measurement event exhibits both Noether-shadow conservation content (the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel's empirical signature per Theorem 36.4) and Born-rule probability content (the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel's empirical signature per Theorem 36.5) *simultaneously*, in a single experimental record, with neither signature suppressible without discarding the physical content of the event. The simultaneity is the empirical signature of the dual-channel architecture of $dx_4/dt = ic$: both channels apply to the same substrate at the same event, and every measurement records both channels' outputs at once.

**Proof.**

*Step 1 — Every quantum event admits both roles.* From Theorem 36.3, every event of $\mathcal{M}$ admits simultaneously both the observer role (reference-frame position with $u^4 = c$ per Theorem 4) and the participant role (position on the McGucken Sphere as expanding wavefront). The two roles apply simultaneously as descriptions of the same event, related by the bidirectional Wick rotation (Theorem 33.5). Consequently, every measurement made at the event registers *both* the observer's content (invariants passing through) and the participant's content (Sphere-coupling amplitude).

*Step 2 — Every experimental record contains both signatures.* By direct enumeration of quantum measurements against the dual-signature check:

- *Atomic emission spectroscopy* — the observer measures the discrete spectral line at frequency $\omega$ (Noether-shadow of temporal invariance: energy $E = \hbar\omega$ conserved between initial and final atomic states); the participant simultaneously experiences the Born-rule probability distribution over spectral lines (transition amplitudes $|\langle f | H_{\rm int} | i \rangle|^2$). Discrete spectrum + probability distribution: both signatures in one experimental record.
- *Double-slit interference* — the observer measures conservation of total particle count (Noether-shadow of $\mathrm{U}(1)$ phase invariance of the wavefunction: particle number conserved); the participant simultaneously experiences the interference pattern $|\psi_1 + \psi_2|^2$ (Born-rule probability distribution across the screen). Particle-count conservation + interference pattern: both signatures in one experimental record.
- *EPR-Bell correlation measurements* — the observer measures conservation of total angular momentum between the two entangled particles (Noether-shadow of $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ isotropy: $L_1 + L_2$ conserved across the joint measurement); the participant simultaneously experiences the nonlocal Bell-correlation distribution ($\cos^2(\theta_1 - \theta_2)$ from the shared Sphere content). Angular momentum conservation + nonlocal correlation: both signatures in one experimental record.
- *Compton scattering* — the observer measures conservation of four-momentum in the scattering event (Noether-shadow of spacetime translational invariance: $p^\mu_{\rm in} = p^\mu_{\rm out}$); the participant simultaneously experiences the differential cross-section distribution (Klein-Nishina formula from wavefunction amplitude). *Step 3 — Neither signature is suppressible.* Attempting to discard the Noether-shadow content (retaining only Born probabilities) discards the reproducibility of physical measurement — without conservation laws, the experimenter cannot even identify the same particle before and after the interaction. Attempting to discard the Born-rule content (retaining only Noether-shadow conservation) discards the specific outcome frequencies — without the Born rule, the experimenter cannot predict the distribution of measurement outcomes across repeated trials. *Step 4 — Simultaneity is the empirical signature.* Given (Step 1) that every event admits both roles, (Step 2) that every quantum measurement records both signatures, and (Step 3) that neither is suppressible, the simultaneity of Noether-shadow conservation and Born-rule probability at every quantum event is an empirical fact. Under the McGucken framework, this simultaneity is the expected signature of the dual-channel architecture: both channels apply to the substrate at the same event, and every measurement records both channels' outputs. $\square$


### §37.2 Theorem 37.2: The Five Foundational Puzzles of Quantum Mechanics Dissolve as Channel-Description Signatures


**Theorem 37.2 (Five-Puzzles-Dissolved).** Five specific foundational puzzles of quantum mechanics — (a) wave-particle duality, (b) the coexistence of classical conservation laws with quantum probabilities, (c) the measurement problem, (d) Bell nonlocality, and (e) Brownian motion of quantum particles — are all *channel-description signatures* of the McGucken Duality of $dx_4/dt = ic$. **Proof.** By direct identification of each puzzle with its channel-description signature.

*(a) Wave-particle duality.* Established as Theorem 35.3 of the present chain: wave-particle duality IS the McGucken Duality. The wave-nature is the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel presentation of $dx_4/dt = ic$; the particle-nature is the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel presentation. *(b) Coexistence of conservation laws and quantum probabilities.* Established as Theorem 37.1 above: conservation laws are the Algebraic Channel Noether-shadow signatures; quantum probabilities are the Geometric Channel Sphere-coupling signatures; both simultaneously observed at every quantum measurement because both channels apply to the same substrate. *(c) The measurement problem.* Under the McGucken framework, the "measurement problem" as classically posed — how does unitary evolution (Schrödinger equation applied to the isolated system) reconcile with Born-rule collapse (probabilistic outcome upon measurement)? — resolves as the observer's confusion about which channel description applies at which experimental phase. During closed-system evolution (no measurement interaction), the Algebraic Channel description dominates (unitary Schrödinger evolution as Theorem 32.4). The century-long interpretational programs — Copenhagen (measurement collapses the wavefunction), Bohm (hidden variables carry definite trajectories), Everett (all branches actualize), GRW (spontaneous localization), QBism (probabilities are subjective degrees of belief), Relational Quantum Mechanics (measurement outcomes are relative to observers) — are diagnosed as different attempts to identify *a single channel description* that suffices for both unitary evolution and measurement collapse. The McGucken framework says no single channel suffices because the substrate carries dual-channel content: physics uses both channels simultaneously, and the "measurement problem" is the artifact of demanding a single-channel description of a dual-channel object.

*(d) Bell nonlocality.* Established at the framework level: two events on the past McGucken Sphere of a common source event share substrate content that manifests as Bell correlations. The nonlocality is the geometric-channel signature of Sphere spatial extent at zero $x_4$-separation from the source. No superluminal signaling (the substrate expansion is at rate $c$, not superluminal); the nonlocality is spatial correlation within a common wavefront, not causal signaling between separated events. Bell's inequality violations are the expected empirical signature of Sphere-shared content across spatially-separated measurement events, not a puzzle to be reconciled by "spooky action at a distance" or by rejection of realism.

*(e) Brownian motion of quantum particles.* Established at Theorem 36.5 (last part): the participant on the Sphere at every event is coupled to surrounding Spheres at neighboring events, producing stochastic motion with diffusion coefficient $D = \hbar/(2m) = \omega_C \bar\lambda_C^2/2$. The convergence of Nelson's postulate with the McGucken derivation is a fourth independent derivation of $D = \hbar/(2m)$ (the others being: standard QM via Schrödinger equation, path-integral formulation via Feynman, and Nelson's own stochastic-mechanics derivation).

All five puzzles reduce to the same fact: the substrate carries dual-channel content; every measurement records both channels' outputs; the "puzzles" arise from demanding single-channel descriptions of a dual-channel object. The dissolution is achieved by identifying each puzzle as a specific channel-description signature, not by proposing new interpretations. $\square$

## §38 The Differential/Integral Duality — the Algebraic Channel Is the Integrated Form of the Principle, the Geometric Channel Is the Differential Form, and $dx_4/dt = ic$ Is Per-Increment Wick Rotation of Real Translation


§35 through §37 established the dual-channel architecture of $dx_4/dt = ic$ at the levels of wave-particle duality, observer-participant duality, and dual empirical signatures. Differentiating the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel's integrated coordinate label $x_4 = ict$ produces the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel's differential form $dx_4/dt = ic$; integrating the Geometric Channel produces the Algebraic Channel's coordinate label; the fundamental theorem of calculus is the operational content of the transition between the two channels. The Wick rotation is intrinsic to the Principle's differential form.

### §38.1 Theorem 38.1: The Algebraic Channel Is the Integrated Form of the McGucken Principle


**Theorem 38.1 (Algebraic-Channel-Is-Integrated-Form).** The Algebraic Channel content of $dx_4/dt = ic$ is exactly the *integrated form* of the Principle: the coordinate label $x_4 = ict$ obtained by integrating the differential equation, together with all content derived from this coordinate label by algebraic operations (squaring, applying isometries, forming null hypersurfaces, inducing causal orders). Each algebraic operation on the integrated coordinate label discards a specific piece of the differential form's content, producing an increasingly-shadow-like set of structures that are manifestly non-quantum-mechanical because the derivative-content — the per-increment $i$-rotation — has been flattened out of the mathematics.

**Proof.**

*Step 1 — Direct integration.* The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ is a first-order ordinary differential equation with the analytic solution $x_4(t) = ict + C$, where $C$ is the constant of integration. Choosing $C = 0$ at the reference event of $\mathcal{M}$ gives the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel's canonical coordinate label:
$$x_4 = ict$$
This is the integrated form of the Principle. From Theorem 1 Step B5, this coordinate label is exactly what the McGucken framework identifies as the Algebraic Channel's starting content.

*Step 2 — Squaring produces the Minkowski line element.* The squared coordinate $(x_4)^2 = (ict)^2 = -c^2 t^2$ is the timelike contribution to the Minkowski line element:
$$ds^2 = (dx_1)^2 + (dx_2)^2 + (dx_3)^2 + (dx_4)^2 = (dx_1)^2 + (dx_2)^2 + (dx_3)^2 - c^2\,dt^2$$

*Step 5 — Causal partial order induced.* The causal partial order $\prec$ is defined on $\mathcal{M}$ by $p \prec q$ iff $q \in V^+(p)$ (i.e., $q$ is in the causal future of $p$). ### §38.2 Theorem 38.2: The Geometric Channel Is the Differential Form of the McGucken Principle

**Proof.**

*Step 1 — The differential form contains the rate and direction explicitly.* The Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ has two pieces of content: (a) the *rate* $|dx_4/dt| = c$ (the fourth axis expands at the speed of light) and (b) the *direction* $\arg(dx_4/dt) = \pi/2$ (the expansion is in the $+i$ direction, perpendicular to the real axis). This is the integral curve of the Principle's differential form applied at $p_0$: the Sphere is *what expands* under the differential equation, propagating radially at rate $c$ from $p_0$. *Step 6 — All manifestly quantum-mechanical content is Geometric-Channel content.* The wavefunction, Compton clock, Schrödinger equation, uncertainty relations, Born rule, interference patterns, Brownian motion, and all downstream quantum-mechanical content are Geometric-Channel content derived from the differential form of the Principle. ### §38.3 Theorem 38.3: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus Relates the Two Channels — Differentiation Is Algebraic-to-Geometric, Integration Is Geometric-to-Algebraic


**Theorem 38.3 (Calculus-Relates-the-Channels).** The Algebraic Channel and the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel are related by the fundamental theorem of calculus applied to the McGucken Principle: differentiation of the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel's coordinate label produces the Geometric Channel's differential form; integration of the Geometric Channel's differential form produces the Algebraic Channel's coordinate label. The transition between the two channels is the operational content of differentiation and integration applied to the substrate content.

**Proof.**

*Differentiation carries Algebraic → Geometric.* Starting from the Algebraic Channel's coordinate label $x_4 = ict$, differentiation with respect to $t$ gives:
$$\frac{d x_4}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}(ict) = ic$$
This is the Geometric Channel's differential form $dx_4/dt = ic$. The differentiation recovers the derivative-content (rate $c$, direction $+i$, per-increment $i$-rotation) that the Algebraic Channel's integrated coordinate label had absorbed into a static coordinate.

*Integration carries Geometric → Algebraic.* Starting from the Geometric Channel's differential form $dx_4/dt = ic$, integration with respect to $t$ gives:
$$x_4(t) = \int dx_4 = \int ic\,dt = ict + C$$
Choosing the constant of integration $C = 0$ at the reference event, the Algebraic Channel's coordinate label $x_4 = ict$ is recovered. The integration flattens out the derivative-content into a static coordinate label; the per-increment $i$-rotation of the differential form is absorbed into the imaginary unit multiplying $ct$ in the integrated form.

*The fundamental theorem of calculus is the operational transition.* The pair of operations — differentiation $\text{Alg} \to \text{Geom}$ and integration $\text{Geom} \to \text{Alg}$ — is exactly the pair of operations relating the two channels. The fundamental theorem of calculus states that these operations are inverses of one another (up to the constant of integration); consequently, the two channels are related as differential-form-and-integrated-form of the same underlying Principle. Both channels are equivalent descriptions of the substrate content, differing only in whether the derivative-content is manifest (Geometric) or absorbed into a coordinate label (Algebraic). $\square$

*remark.* The two channels are related by differentiation and integration as literal mathematics, not by metaphor. Applying $d/dt$ to $x_4 = ict$ gives $dx_4/dt = ic$. Applying $\int dt$ to $ic$ gives $ict + C$. The two channels are the two forms of the same first-order linear ordinary differential equation.


### §38.4 Theorem 38.4: $dx_4/dt = ic$ Is Per-Increment Wick Rotation of the Real Translation $dx/dt = c$


**Theorem 38.4 (Principle-Is-Per-Increment-Wick-Rotation).** The McGucken Principle's differential form $dx_4/dt = ic$ is exactly the per-increment Wick rotation of the real translation $dx/dt = c$: applying the Wick rotation $t \to -i\tau$ to $dx/dt = c$ produces $dx/d(-i\tau) = c$, i.e., $dx/d\tau = -ic$, and equivalently, applying the inverse Wick rotation $\tau \to it$ to a real translation of $\tau$ produces the imaginary velocity $ic$ of the McGucken Principle. Each infinitesimal increment of the Principle IS an infinitesimal Wick rotation; the Wick rotation is therefore intrinsic to the Principle, not an external analytic-continuation trick applied at the level of formal manipulations of amplitudes.

**Proof.**

*The Wick rotation is a rotation by $\pi/2$ in the complex plane of time.* Standard Wick rotation is defined as the analytic continuation $t \to -i\tau$ (or equivalently $\tau \to it$), rotating the real time axis to the imaginary time axis by $\pi/2$. Under this rotation, a real velocity $v$ becomes an imaginary velocity $iv$ (or $-iv$ depending on rotation direction).

*The Principle IS such a rotation applied to a real translation.* Consider a real translation with velocity $c$: $dx/dt = c$. Applying $t \to -i\tau$ (Wick rotation) gives:
$$\frac{dx}{d(-i\tau)} = c \Rightarrow \frac{dx}{d\tau} = -ic$$
Or, equivalently, applying $\tau \to it$ to a real translation of $\tau$ gives $dx/d(it) = c$, i.e., $dx/dt = c/i = -ic$ (up to a sign convention, or $+ic$ with the opposite convention). The rotation-direction convention is a phase-orientation choice; up to this convention, the McGucken Principle's form $dx_4/dt = ic$ is exactly the Wick rotation of a real translation.

*Each infinitesimal increment of the Principle is an infinitesimal Wick rotation.* The Principle's differential form $dx_4/dt = ic$ can be integrated infinitesimally: over an infinitesimal time increment $\Delta t$, the substrate advances by $\Delta x_4 = ic\,\Delta t$. This advance runs in the imaginary direction $+i\hat x$ — corresponding to an $i$-rotation of the substrate's position by an angle $\Delta\theta = c\,\Delta t/x$ around a reference point (in the appropriate polar-decomposition sense). *Each infinitesimal $\Delta t$ therefore corresponds to an infinitesimal rotation of the substrate content in the complex plane*, and the accumulation of infinitesimal rotations over finite time gives the integrated coordinate label $x_4 = ict$. This is a compounded infinitesimal Wick rotation.

*The Wick rotation is intrinsic to the Principle.* Under this identification, the Wick rotation supplies the operational content of the Principle's own differential form. Whenever a physical calculation applies the Wick rotation $t \to -i\tau$, it is applying the McGucken Principle's own operation. The seventy years of success of Wick rotation in QFT (Wick 1954; extensive use in Euclidean path-integral methods, lattice gauge theory, and computational quantum field theory) is empirical evidence for the McGucken Principle's differential form: the Wick rotation works because it is the substrate's own operational content, not because it happens to be a convenient mathematical trick. $\square$

**Proof.**

*Step 1 — Lie algebras and Lie groups: standard mathematical background.* A Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ is a vector space equipped with a bracket operation $[\cdot, \cdot]$ satisfying antisymmetry and the Jacobi identity. A Lie group $G$ is a smooth manifold with a group structure compatible with the manifold structure. Every finite-dimensional Lie group $G$ has an associated Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g} = T_e G$ (the tangent space at the identity), and the exponential map $\exp: \mathfrak{g} \to G$ takes Lie algebra elements to Lie group elements. Concretely, for a matrix Lie group, $\exp(X) = e^X = I + X + X^2/2! + \ldots$. *Step 2 — The $i$ in $dx_4/dt = ic$ is a $\mathfrak{u}(1)$ Lie algebra element.* The Lie algebra $\mathfrak{u}(1)$ of the group $\mathrm{U}(1)$ (unit circle in the complex plane, phase-rotations) is the one-dimensional real vector space spanned by $i$ (up to a sign convention). The differential form is a differential equation with a $\mathfrak{u}(1)$-valued right-hand side; the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel is a $\mathfrak{u}(1)$-Lie-algebra-valued differential form.

*Step 4 — The dual-channel architecture is the $\mathfrak{u}(1)$ / $\mathrm{U}(1)$ duality.* Combining Steps 2 and 3: the Geometric Channel's differential form contains the $\mathfrak{u}(1)$ Lie algebra content (per-increment generator $-i\omega_C$); the Algebraic Channel's integrated form contains the $\mathrm{U}(1)$ Lie group content (unitary evolution $e^{-i\omega_C t}$). The two channels are related by the exponential map $\exp: \mathfrak{u}(1) \to \mathrm{U}(1)$, which is the specific instance of the general Lie algebra / Lie group duality that underlies all gauge theories.

*Step 5 — Gauge-theory generalization.* The identification generalizes: the $\mathrm{U}(1)$ phase invariance of the Compton clock underlies electric charge conservation (Corollary 37.4); the $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ gauge invariance of the electroweak sector underlies weak isospin; the $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ gauge invariance of QCD underlies color charge. Combining Theorems 38.1 through 38.5, the McGucken framework's architecture forms a six-step shadow hierarchy from the differential Principle down to the causal partial order of special relativity:

Under Theorems 38.1 through 38.5, the McGucken Principle's differential form provides the pure geometric content of the wavefront: rate $c$, direction $+i$, per-increment $i$-rotation, exponential expansion of the Sphere at every event.
