##### §28.8.10.3 The McGucken Sphere as the Single Geometric Source of Nonlocality, Probability, Entanglement, and Entropy: Characterizing How the McGucken Framework Goes Deeper Than the Orthodox Programs


The unification of §28.8.10.2 above can be sharpened by identifying the *single geometric object* whose properties supply all four of the primitive quantities required for the entropy–entanglement unification: *nonlocality* (the necessary condition for entanglement to exist), *probability* (the necessary condition for statistical mechanics to operate), *entanglement* (the correlation structure between spatially separated particles sharing a common past), and *entropy increase* (the strict Second Law). That single geometric object is the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p) \subset \mathcal{M}_G$ — the future null cone of velocity $c$ swept out by $dx_4/dt = ic$ from every spacetime event $p \in \mathcal{M}_G$, constructed in Theorem 3 of the present paper.


**The geometric property of the McGucken Sphere surface.** The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p, t)$ at coordinate time $t$ after the apex event $p$ (measured in the rest frame of a stationary observer at $\vec{x}(p)$) is the set of spacetime events
$$\Sigma_+(p, t) = \{q \in \mathcal{M}_G : x_4(q) - x_4(p) = ict, \quad |\vec{x}(q) - \vec{x}(p)| = ct\}.$$
Every event on this surface has the *same* $x_4$-coordinate offset from the apex: $x_4(q) - x_4(p) = ict$ for all $q \in \Sigma_+(p,t)$. The Sphere surface is therefore *local in $x_4$*: any two events $q_1, q_2 \in \Sigma_+(p,t)$ are at the same $x_4$-coordinate, separated by zero $x_4$-distance. The Sphere surface is *nonlocal in the spatial three-slice $(x_1, x_2, x_3)$*: two events $q_1, q_2 \in \Sigma_+(p,t)$ at antipodal positions on the Sphere are separated by spatial distance $|\vec{x}(q_1) - \vec{x}(q_2)| = 2ct$, which can be macroscopic or cosmological at sufficient $t$.


The single geometric property — *local in $x_4$, nonlocal in $(x_1, x_2, x_3)$* — is the geometric source of all four primitive quantities below. The same geometric structure that supplies the nonlocality required for entanglement to exist also supplies, through its $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-symmetry, the probability distribution that drives the Second Law.


**(1) Nonlocality as the property of the Sphere surface.** The Sphere surface's locality in $x_4$ combined with its nonlocality in $(x_1, x_2, x_3)$ supplies the geometric nonlocality required for entanglement to exist. Theorem 30 of the present paper (Quantum Nonlocality as McGucken-Sphere Null-Separation) makes the identification explicit: events that appear *spacelike-separated* in any 3D spatial-slice projection are *geometrically local on the 4D null surface* of their common source event $p_0$. The apparent spacelike separation between Alice's detection event $e_A$ and Bob's detection event $e_B$ in entangled-photon experiments is the 3D-slice projection of their 4D-null-locality on the common Sphere $\Sigma_+(p_0)$ of the entangled-photon-pair source event. ##### §28.8.10.4 The Dynamical Mechanism Behind the Single Geometric Source: The Born Rule as a Head-on $x_4$-Collision of Two McGucken Spheres


The identification of §28.8.10.3 supplies the *kinematic* substrate: the McGucken Sphere is the single geometric object whose properties yield nonlocality, probability, entanglement, and entropy. The Sphere's $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-Haar measure on its surface (Theorem 7) supplies the probability distribution; the spatial-projection of the Sphere's $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-isotropy under constant collision-measurement (Theorem 26) supplies the strict Second Law. What remains to be articulated is the *dynamical* mechanism by which the Sphere's geometric probability becomes the Born-rule probability density $|\psi(P)|^2$ at a measurement event $P$. The existing derivation of [Theorem 4.2]MGBornRule supplies the operator-algebraic the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel reading: the bilinearity in $(\psi, \psi^*)$ is forced by the rank-2 character of the Minkowski metric induced by $x_4 = ict$ (the integrated coordinate shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$). The present subsection supplies the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel geometric-dynamical reading: the bilinearity $\psi^*(P)\psi(P)$ at a measurement event is the rate of head-on collision between two McGucken Spheres carrying opposed $x_4$-orientations at $P$, with the collision performing the Wick rotation of Theorem 26 and depositing the participating particles' $x_4$-expansion content into spatial localization at $P$.


**The two-sphere collision picture.** Let two particles $A$ and $B$ at events $E_A$ and $E_B$ each propagate their McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(E_A)$ and $\Sigma_+(E_B)$ outward at $dx_4/dt = +ic$ in their respective rest frames (Theorem 3 of the present paper, applied independently at each event). At any spatial point $P$ where both Spheres arrive at the same coordinate time in some common reference frame, the local relative orientation of the two outgoing $x_4$-directions along the shared spatial geodesic through $P$ is *antiparallel*:


*(i) In particle $A$'s rest frame.* The Sphere $\Sigma_+(E_A)$ at $P$ has outgoing $x_4$-direction $dx_4/dt|_A = +ic$ (the principle applied to $\Sigma_+(E_A)$ in $A$'s frame). The Sphere $\Sigma_+(E_B)$, having propagated from $E_B$ to reach $P$ from the opposite side along the shared spatial geodesic, has its outgoing wavefront direction at $P$ pointing away from $E_B$ — that is, *toward* $A$'s spatial location. Viewed in $A$'s rest frame, the $x_4$-orientation of this incoming wavefront at $P$ reads $dx_4/dt|_B^{(A)} = -ic$: $B$'s Sphere is incoming with respect to $A$, hence its $x_4$-advance contribution at $P$ is the negative of $A$'s own outgoing $x_4$-advance along the shared spatial axis.


*(ii) In particle $B$'s rest frame.* The converse holds: $\Sigma_+(E_B)$'s outgoing direction at $P$ has $dx_4/dt|_B = +ic$, and $\Sigma_+(E_A)$'s incoming direction at $P$ reads $dx_4/dt|_A^{(B)} = -ic$.


The relative orientation of the two outgoing Spheres at $P$ is therefore *frame-relational, not absolute*: each particle observes its own Sphere expanding at $+ic$ and its partner's incoming Sphere as expanding at $-ic$. This is the content of complex conjugation in the Born-rule formalism. The complex conjugate $\psi^*$ of an outgoing spherical-wave amplitude $\psi$ is the same Sphere viewed as incoming from the partner's frame, with the $x_4$-orientation reversed along the shared spatial geodesic. Complex conjugation in quantum mechanics is therefore identified geometrically as the relative-frame reading of the partner's $+ic$ as $-ic$ at the collision point — the conjugate is the other branch of $\sqrt{-1}$ produced by the relative-frame reading, not an absolute primitive separate from the primary $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$.


**The $x_4$-orientation cancellation at $P$ forces three-spatial localization.** Each McGucken Sphere carries an $x_4$-advance content $+ic$ outgoing from its apex event. At the collision point $P$, the two Spheres' outgoing $x_4$-orientations are antiparallel by the frame-relational argument above: the local net $x_4$-orientation at $P$ is the sum $(+ic) + (-ic) = 0$ in either particle's rest frame along the shared spatial geodesic. The cancellation does not eliminate the underlying $x_4$-expansion of either particle; it eliminates the *projection* of the combined $x_4$-advance onto the shared spatial geodesic at $P$. By conservation of total four-content across the four dimensions of $\mathcal{M}_G$ — momentum, energy, and the $x_4$-expansion-advance read as a momenergy budget — the cancellation in the $x_4$-direction at $P$ is balanced by appearance in the spatial three-slice $(x_1, x_2, x_3)$: both particles must be present at $P$ for the collision to occur, and the $x_4$-content that cancelled at $P$ is deposited as spatial localization of both particles at $P$. The detector click — the moment at which the particle's outgoing $x_4$-expansion is converted into a spatial localization in the laboratory — is identified as this transfer of $x_4$-content into spatial three-slice content at the collision event $P$.


**The Born rule as the head-on collision rate.** The localization rate at $P$ is the head-on Sphere-collision rate, which is bilinear in the two incoming Sphere amplitudes by the standard collision-rate calculation. Let $\psi(P)$ denote the amplitude for $\Sigma_+(E_A)$ to reach $P$ and $\phi(P)$ denote the amplitude for $\Sigma_+(E_B)$ to reach $P$. The collision rate at $P$ is then
$$\mathrm{Rate}_{\rm collision}(P) \;\propto\; \phi^*(P)\,\psi(P),$$
where the conjugate factor on the $\phi$-amplitude is the frame-relational reading of $B$'s outgoing $+ic$ Sphere as incoming $-ic$ in $A$'s frame at $P$ (the $\psi \leftrightarrow \psi^*$ identification established above). For a single-particle quantum-mechanical system emitting Sphere $\Sigma_+(E_A)$ with amplitude $\psi$ at $P$, and a detector consisting of many absorber particles whose Spheres arrive at $P$ from the detector face, the rate of localization at $P$ summed over absorber states with appropriate matrix elements reduces to
$$\mathrm{Rate}_{\rm Born}(P) \;\propto\; \psi^*(P)\,\psi(P) \;=\; |\psi(P)|^2,$$
recovering the Born rule as the rate of head-on $x_4$-collisions between the emitter's outgoing Sphere and the absorber's outgoing Sphere viewed from the emitter's frame. The complex conjugate factor $\psi^*(P)$ identifies the absorber's own outgoing $x_4$-expansion appearing as inward in the emitter's frame and supplies the dynamical content of the relative-frame head-on collision. The derivation of [Theorem 4.2]MGBornRule supplies the operator-algebraic the Algebraic Channel reading of the same bilinearity (forced by the rank-2 character of the Minkowski metric induced by $x_4 = ict$); the head-on Sphere-collision mechanism of the present subsection supplies the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel geometric-dynamical reading. The two readings constitute two algebraic projections of one underlying dynamical event: head-on encounter of two McGucken Spheres in $x_4$.


**The photon as the extreme case.** A photon propagating at velocity $c$ is in the McGucken framework a Sphere $\Sigma_+(E_\gamma)$ expanding at $dx_4/dt = +ic$ from its emission event $E_\gamma$, with the photon's full momenergy budget being $x_4$-directed at every event of its worldline (a Sphere-borne reading, in which the fourth dimension physically expands at rate $c$ from the emission event and continues to expand at every event of the photon's worldline, per the McGucken Principle: the photon itself has $v_{x_4} = 0$ on its own worldline per [MGWavefront] Appendix A — stationary in $x_4$, which is what makes it move at $c$ through space — while its momenergy is carried by the $dx_4/dt = +ic$ Sphere-expansion the photon rides on; the momenergy transfer at collision comes from the Sphere-borne motion in $x_4$, which is the physical expansion of the fourth dimension itself) — the photon has no rest-frame spatial-momentum content because the photon has no rest frame; its momenergy is entirely the $x_4$-expansion of the Sphere wavefront. Detection of the photon at a spatial point $P$ — for example, blackening of a film grain at $P$ — is the head-on Sphere-collision: the photon's outgoing Sphere $\Sigma_+(E_\gamma)$ and the absorber's outgoing Sphere $\Sigma_+(E_{\rm abs})$ from a film-grain silver-halide molecule meet head-on at $P$ in the film grain's rest frame. The photon's $+ic$ $x_4$-orientation and the absorber's $-ic$ $x_4$-orientation (viewed in the photon's frame) cancel at $P$. Because the photon's entire momenergy is $x_4$-directed, the entire $x_4$-content of the photon is transferred to the spatial three-slice at $P$: the photon is *completely* knocked out of $x_4$-expansion and *fully* localized at $P$, depositing its full energy $\hbar\omega$ into the film grain's silver-halide reduction. The photographic blackening at $P$ is the spatial-three-slice receipt of the photon's entire $x_4$-momenergy. The photon is the extreme case of the head-on Sphere-collision mechanism because its initial momenergy budget is entirely $x_4$-directed; for a massive particle, only the $x_4$-projected portion of the momenergy is transferred at the collision, with the spatial-three-slice rest-frame portion redistributed by the collision dynamics.


**Connection to Theorem 26 (each inter-molecular collision is a Wick rotation).** Theorem 26 of the present paper establishes that each inter-molecular collision is a McGucken–Wick rotation that exteriorises the imaginary unit $i$ from the participating molecules' wavefunctions onto the real coordinate axis. The head-on Sphere-collision mechanism supplies the explicit dynamical content of this Wick rotation: the $x_4$-content transfer at the collision point $P$ is the geometric Wick rotation, with the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel complex-wavefunction structure carried by the imaginary $ic$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$ being deposited as the Geometric Channel real-positive ensemble-distribution structure at $P$. Each Wick rotation per collision is therefore identified as a Born-rule event in the operator-algebraic reading and a head-on Sphere-collision event in the geometric reading. The two readings are two algebraic projections of one dynamical mechanism: head-on encounter of two Spheres carrying antiparallel $x_4$-orientations at the collision point. Corollary 26.1's diagnosis of Boltzmann's Stosszahlansatz as the implicit recognition of the Wick-rotation content of inter-molecular collisions is therefore equivalently the implicit recognition that each inter-molecular collision is a head-on Sphere-collision with the Born-rule structure embedded in the collision dynamics.


**The relativistic-boost / quantum-measurement parallel.** In both special relativity and quantum mechanics, a rotation with respect to the fourth expanding dimension $x_4$ produces a physical effect on the system's motion. In special relativity, a rotation in the $x_4$-$x_i$ plane is a *Lorentz boost*, and the boosted observer's spatial velocity with respect to the original inertial frame is the rotation parameter (the standard relation $\tanh\xi = v/c$ for boost rapidity $\xi$, with the boost mixing the $x_4$ and $x_i$ axes). In quantum mechanics, a rotation in the $x_4$-$x_i$ plane is a *measurement event*: a particle previously propagating its Sphere outward at $dx_4/dt = +ic$ (surfing the $x_4$-expansion) is rotated by the head-on Sphere-collision out of pure $x_4$-expansion and localized in the spatial three-slice at $P$. The two operations — Lorentz boost and quantum measurement — are the same operation (rotation in the $x_4$-$x_i$ plane) acting on two different physical contents through the McGucken Duality of Theorem 19.5 of the present paper. The Lorentz boost is the Algebraic Channel algebraic reading: the algebraic-symmetry rotation of inertial frames preserves all measurable quantities and acts on the principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ by relabeling the $x_4$ axis in the boosted frame. The quantum measurement is the Geometric Channel geometric reading: the geometric-propagation rotation transfers $x_4$-content into spatial-three-slice content at the collision point and acts on the principle by terminating the particle's $x_4$-Sphere-expansion at the measurement event. Both operations arise from the same principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ through its Duality; the difference is which channel's reading of the rotation is operative in the specific physical context. The unity of the relativistic boost and the quantum measurement under the single principle is a deeper identification supplied by the McGucken framework and inaccessible to the orthodox tradition's separation of special relativity and quantum mechanics as distinct programs.


**Thermodynamic emergence: why the imaginary unit disappears.** Over a large ensemble of particles, head-on Sphere-collisions occur at the inter-molecular collision rate $\Gamma_{\rm coll} \sim N_{\rm int}\omega_C \sim 10^{22}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ per molecule (Theorem 26), with the cumulative effect over the $\sim 10^{23}$ degrees of freedom of any macroscopic environment being a Born-rule measurement event for each particle at every collision. Each such event exteriorises the imaginary unit $i$ from the participating wavefunctions onto the spatial three-slice via the head-on Sphere-collision mechanism above, producing a Geometric Channel real-positive ensemble distribution on the relevant Sphere surface. The thermodynamic-limit phenomenology — the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution as the equilibrium $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-Haar measure on the velocity-space Sphere; the strict Second Law $dS/dt = (3/2)k_B/t > 0$ of Theorem 9; the diffusion-equation behavior of Theorem 6; the equipartition theorem; the Boltzmann–Gibbs $\rho \propto e^{-\beta H}$ canonical distribution — emerges as the cumulative effect of trillions of head-on Sphere-collision Born-rule events per second per particle, each one exteriorising the $i$ once. The imaginary unit disappears from the thermodynamic phenomenology because every collision in the ensemble has exteriorised it once at the head-on Sphere-collision event, and the cumulative effect over $10^{22}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ collisions per particle is the complete conversion of the Algebraic Channel complex-wavefunction structure into the Geometric Channel real-positive ensemble distribution. The McGucken–Wick rotation that the orthodox tradition treats as a formal substitution $t \to -i\tau$ for technical convenience in evaluating Euclidean path integrals is, under the head-on Sphere-collision mechanism, the cumulative dynamical effect of the Born-rule events occurring at every inter-molecular collision in the ensemble: a real physical process happening trillions of times per second per particle.


**Synthesis with §28.8.10.3.** The head-on Sphere-collision mechanism unifies four operations of physics — the Born rule (rate of localization at a measurement event), the McGucken–Wick rotation (exteriorisation of $i$ at each inter-molecular collision), the Lorentz boost (the Algebraic Channel rotation in the $x_4$-$x_i$ plane), and the quantum measurement (the Geometric Channel rotation in the $x_4$-$x_i$ plane) — as four readings of one dynamical operation: rotation with respect to the fourth expanding dimension $x_4$, induced by head-on encounter of two McGucken Spheres carrying antiparallel $x_4$-orientations in the participants' relative frames. The single geometric object of §28.8.10.3 (the McGucken Sphere) supplies the kinematic substrate; the head-on Sphere-collision mechanism of the present subsection supplies the dynamics. Together they constitute the answer to the primary question of how nonlocality, probability, entanglement, and entropy arise from a single principle $dx_4/dt = ic$. The orthodox programs of Table~\ref{tab:four-quantities-comparison} have access to neither the single geometric object nor the head-on Sphere-collision dynamical mechanism that supplies the unification: Boltzmann 1872 has the SO(3)-isotropy without recognizing it as the Sphere's property; Bekenstein–Hawking 1973/1975 have the area-law without recognizing it as the Sphere's mode-count under the head-on Sphere-collision Wick rotation; Verlinde 2011/2022 has the entanglement-entropy substrate without recognizing the head-on Sphere-collision mechanism that produces it; Ryu–Takayanagi 2006 has the formula $S_{\rm EE} = A/4$ without the dynamical mechanism that explains its empirical content. The McGucken framework supplies both the geometric substrate and the dynamical mechanism, and derives the four primitive quantities (nonlocality, probability, entanglement, entropy) together with their dynamical realization (Born rule, Wick rotation, Lorentz boost, quantum measurement) from one principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$.


##### §28.8.10.5 Singularities and Infinities Across Four Sectors of Physics: How the McGucken Framework Resolves Them Through the Sphere Mode Count


The depth of the McGucken framework documented in §28.8.10.3 (the McGucken Sphere as single geometric source) and §28.8.10.4 (the head-on Sphere-collision dynamical mechanism) extends naturally to a class of problems the orthodox tradition has been engaging with for over a century: the appearance of singularities and infinities in continuum-field equations across four distinct sectors of physics. The present subsection establishes that the four classes of divergence — general-relativistic spacetime singularities, Navier–Stokes gradient blow-up, quantum-field-theoretic ultraviolet divergences, and thermodynamic critical-point singularities — share one source: the artifact of taking continuum-limit equations to scales smaller than the natural physical cutoff supplied by the McGucken Sphere mode count $A/\ell_P^2$ at the Planck scale (Theorem 21 of the present paper), with the head-on Sphere-collision dynamics of §28.8.10.4 supplying the additional molecular-scale cutoff where appropriate.


**Are there singularities in thermodynamics?** The thermodynamic sector contains three distinct species of singularity that the orthodox tradition has been engaging with for over a century.


*(i) Critical-point singularities at second-order phase transitions.* At the critical point of a second-order phase transition — water at $T = 374\,\mathrm{^\circ C}$ and $P = 22\,\mathrm{MPa}$; the ferromagnetic Curie point; the superfluid lambda transition in liquid helium-4 at $T_\lambda = 2.17\,\mathrm{K}$; the Bose–Einstein condensation transition — the correlation length $\xi$ diverges $\xi \to \infty$; the specific heat at constant volume $C_V$ diverges with critical exponent $\alpha$; the magnetic susceptibility diverges with exponent $\gamma$; the order-parameter response to a conjugate field diverges with exponent $\delta$. The Wilson renormalization-group analysis [145], developed from the Kadanoff block-spin construction [146], was the primary machinery for treating these singularities through scaling laws and critical exponents.


*(ii) Black-hole endpoint singularity.* The Hawking temperature relation $T_H = \hbar\kappa/(2\pi c k_B) = \hbar c^3/(8\pi G M k_B)$ exhibits $T_H \to \infty$ as $M \to 0$: a black hole that has Hawking-radiated to near-zero mass approaches infinite temperature. The endpoint of black-hole evaporation is therefore a singular point of the orthodox thermodynamic relation between $M$ and $T_H$, with the breakdown of the semiclassical analysis at $M \to m_P$ catalogued in the orthodox literature without identification of the source of the breakdown.


*(iii) Third-law approach to absolute zero.* As $T \to 0$, multiple thermodynamic quantities approach singular limits: the specific heats of crystalline solids approach zero with characteristic power laws set by the Debye theory; magnetic susceptibilities diverge or vanish depending on the system's frustration structure; the entropy approaches the Nernst-theorem residual entropy at a possibly non-analytic limit. The orthodox identification of these limits as "the third law of thermodynamics" treats them descriptively without supplying a mechanism.


The thermodynamic sector therefore has its own substantial singularity catalogue, with the Wilson renormalization-group machinery being the canonical orthodox response — descriptive scaling-law machinery without a substrate-level resolution.


**Are the singularities in Navier–Stokes and general relativity related to the infinities in quantum field theory?** The diagnosis is that all three classes of divergence arise from the same source: extrapolation of continuum field equations to scales smaller than the principle's natural cutoff.


*(i) Continuum extrapolation as the common source.* General relativity treats spacetime as a continuum smooth manifold $\mathcal{M}$ with metric $g_{\mu\nu}(x)$ defined at every point. As $r \to 0$ in Schwarzschild geometry or $t \to 0$ in FLRW cosmology, the Einstein tensor $G_{\mu\nu}$ diverges because the equation $G_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4)\,T_{\mu\nu}$ admits no internal mechanism preventing the divergence. The Penrose 1965 [142], Hawking 1967 [143], and Hawking–Penrose 1970 [144] singularity theorems established that the divergences are generic features of the continuum theory rather than artifacts of specific symmetric solutions, applicable under reasonable energy conditions to any globally hyperbolic Lorentzian manifold containing a trapped surface or sufficient cosmological expansion. Navier–Stokes treats fluid velocity $\vec{u}(\vec{x},t)$ as a continuum smooth field on $\mathbb{R}^3$; the Clay Millennium global-regularity problem asks whether smooth initial data necessarily yields smooth solutions for all time, with potential finite-time gradient blow-up being the open question. Tao's program [149] has identified candidate blow-up mechanisms within the continuum theory. Quantum field theory treats the field $\phi(x)$ as a continuum object with momentum modes at all wavelengths down to zero; ultraviolet divergences arise in loop integrals because the integration over high momenta has no built-in cutoff. The three sectors share one fact: the continuum field equations admit no internal mechanism preventing divergence when extrapolated to scales smaller than the principle's natural cutoff.


*(ii) The Wilson renormalization-group identification.* Wilson 1971 [145] established that quantum-field-theoretic infinities and critical-phenomena singularities share the same mathematical structure: both arise from the absence of a natural cutoff in continuum equations and respond to the same renormalization-group machinery. The Wilson–Kadanoff scaling laws were derived in the critical-phenomena context but apply equally to the QFT-divergences context under the Wick rotation between Lorentzian and Euclidean signatures (Theorem 25 of the present paper). The identification "QFT ultraviolet divergences and critical-point singularities are one phenomenon" is therefore established in the orthodox literature, with the McGucken framework supplying the source through Theorem 19 of the present paper (Universal $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel Theorem): the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel content of every dual-channel derivation is one mathematical object — iterated McGucken Sphere expansion — read in two signatures related by the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$.


*(iii) The asymptotic-safety program and effective field theory.* The orthodox response to general relativity's ultraviolet incompleteness has been the asymptotic-safety program of Weinberg 1979 [147], developed operationally by Reuter 1998 [148] and many subsequent authors. The asymptotic-safety conjecture postulates that general relativity has an ultraviolet fixed point of its renormalization-group flow at which the theory becomes scale-invariant and predictive at all scales. The conjecture acknowledges that orthodox general relativity has ultraviolet divergences and proposes a solution within the renormalization-group machinery without identifying the source of the cutoff. The effective-field-theory program treats general relativity as valid above a Planck-scale UV cutoff supplied by some yet-to-be-identified physics. Both responses presuppose a principle the orthodox tradition has not yet identified; the asymptotic-safety conjecture has produced extensive numerical evidence for a UV fixed point through the Reuter machinery, but the source of the fixed point remains an open question. The McGucken framework supplies the principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$, with the natural cutoff being the McGucken Sphere mode count $A/\ell_P^2$ at the Planck scale (Theorem 21 of the present paper).


**Does Jacobson's derivation of gravity from thermodynamics resolve gravitational singularities?** Jacobson's 1995 derivation [122] established that the Einstein equations $R_{\mu\nu} - (1/2)g_{\mu\nu}R = (8\pi G/c^4)\,T_{\mu\nu}$ follow from the Clausius relation $\delta Q = T\,dS$ applied to local Rindler horizons. This was the identification of gravity as emergent thermodynamics, ratifying the thermodynamic reading of general relativity as the Geometric Channel content of $dx_4/dt = ic$ in [3].


The Jacobson derivation does not dissolve gravitational singularities. The derivation applies at the macroscopic scale where local Rindler horizons have well-defined areas $\delta A$ and temperatures $T_U = \hbar\kappa/(2\pi c k_B)$. At the Planck scale, both $\delta A$ and $T_U$ become subject to quantum-gravitational corrections that the Jacobson derivation does not supply: the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy $S = k_B A/(4\ell_P^2)$ presupposes that the horizon area $A$ is much larger than the Planck length squared $\ell_P^2$; the Hawking temperature $T_H = \hbar c^3/(8\pi G M k_B)$ presupposes that the black-hole mass $M$ is much larger than the Planck mass $m_P \approx 2.18 \times 10^{-8}\,\mathrm{kg}$. The Jacobson derivation is therefore a low-energy thermodynamic equation of state for gravity, valid above the Planck scale, dissolving no Planck-scale singularity. The Schwarzschild singularity at $r = 0$, the FLRW Big-Bang singularity at $t = 0$, and the black-hole endpoint singularity at $M \to 0$ all persist under the Jacobson reading because the Jacobson derivation works within the same continuum-Einstein-equation framework that produces them.


The McGucken framework extends the Jacobson program by supplying the explicit Planck-scale cutoff that the Jacobson derivation implicitly presupposes but does not derive. Under Theorem 21 of the present paper (Huygens equals Holography), the mode count on any McGucken Sphere of area $A$ is $N(A) = A/\ell_P^2$, derived from $dx_4/dt = ic$ through the Bekenstein III–V chain of [33]. For $A = \ell_P^2$, $N(A) = 1$ — a single Sphere mode; for $A < \ell_P^2$, $N(A) < 1$ — no physical content. The McGucken Sphere mode count therefore supplies a cutoff at $\ell_P$ that the orthodox tradition has not derived from principles. The cutoff is the content of Theorem 21 derived from $dx_4/dt = ic$ at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$, supplied by the principle rather than introduced phenomenologically.


The Hilbert–Jacobson forced agreement at the Geometric Channel / the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel interface is one of the three forced dual-channel agreements documented in [3] (the other two being Heisenberg–Feynman on $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ and Feynman–Wiener at the QM–statistical-mechanics correspondence). The three forced agreements are the empirical signature of $dx_4/dt = ic$ as the single principle behind all four sectors of physics; the McGucken framework's extension of the Jacobson program is the explicit identification of the Planck-scale cutoff via the Sphere mode count $A/\ell_P^2$ as the content of $dx_4/dt = ic$ at the primary level.


**How does the McGucken framework resolve the singularities and infinities across all four sectors?** The answer is identical across all four sectors: the McGucken Sphere mode count $A/\ell_P^2$ supplies a natural cutoff at the Planck scale below which the continuum-limit equations cease to apply; the head-on Sphere-collision dynamics of §28.8.10.4 supplies the additional molecular-scale cutoff for fluid systems; the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel versus the Geometric Channel distinction (Theorem 19.5 of the present paper) supplies the source for critical-point singularities as projections of the Geometric Channel regular dynamics onto the Algebraic Channel bulk variables.


*(1) General-relativistic spacetime singularities.* The Schwarzschild singularity at $r = 0$ and the FLRW Big-Bang singularity at $t = 0$ arise from extrapolating the continuum Einstein equations $G_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4)\,T_{\mu\nu}$ to scales smaller than the Planck length, where the underlying McGucken Sphere mode count drops below one. At $r < \ell_P$ in Schwarzschild geometry, the available area $4\pi r^2$ contains fewer than one Sphere mode and the Einstein equations no longer describe a physical content; the curvature singularity at $r = 0$ is an artifact of continuum extrapolation below the natural cutoff. The McGucken framework predicts a Planck-scale core (one Sphere mode minimum) for any black hole; the orthodox $r = 0$ singularity is dissolved as unphysical. The FLRW Big-Bang singularity at $t = 0$ is the origin event of the McGucken manifold $\mathcal{M}_G$ at which $x_4 = 0$ but $dx_4/dt = ic$ continues to operate; the orthodox scale-factor singularity $a(t) \to 0$ is an artifact of an Algebraic Channel coordinate parameterization that vanishes at the origin, with the underlying principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ being non-singular everywhere (Theorem 13 of the present paper, Past Hypothesis dissolution). The Penrose–Hawking singularity theorems [142, 143, 144] establishing that GR singularities are generic under reasonable energy conditions apply to the continuum theory; the McGucken framework's natural Planck-scale cutoff renders the singular endpoints unphysical without requiring the energy conditions to be violated.


*(2) Navier–Stokes gradient blow-up.* The Clay Millennium problem on Navier–Stokes asks whether smooth initial data for the incompressible Navier–Stokes equation $\partial_t \vec{u} + (\vec{u}\cdot\nabla)\vec{u} = -\nabla p/\rho + \nu\nabla^2\vec{u}$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$ necessarily yields smooth solutions for all time. The potential failure mode is finite-time gradient blow-up: a smooth initial velocity field develops gradients diverging at some finite time. Tao's program [149] has identified candidate blow-up mechanisms within the continuum theory. The McGucken framework resolves the status of the Clay problem: the continuum Navier–Stokes equation is an effective field theory valid at scales above the molecular mean free path $\lambda_{\rm mfp} \sim 1/(n\sigma)$, where $n$ is the molecular number density and $\sigma$ the collision cross-section. Below $\lambda_{\rm mfp}$, the fluid is a collection of molecules undergoing head-on McGucken Sphere collisions at rate $\Gamma_{\rm coll} \sim N_{\rm int}\omega_C \sim 10^{22}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ per molecule (§28.8.10.4 of the present paper), with each head-on Sphere collision performing the Wick rotation of Theorem 26 and supplying a discrete, well-defined dynamics at the molecular scale. Physical fluids exhibit no blow-up because their molecular structure provides a natural cutoff; the mathematical continuum Navier–Stokes equation may exhibit blow-up because it lacks this cutoff. The McGucken framework reframes the Clay problem as a question about the continuum limit's range of validity, with the answer being that the molecular-scale head-on Sphere-collision dynamics replaces the continuum equation at scales below $\lambda_{\rm mfp}$.


*(3) Quantum-field-theoretic ultraviolet divergences.* The ultraviolet divergences of quantum field theory — the divergences of loop integrals $\int d^4k\,f(k)$ at $|k| \to \infty$ — arise from integrating field modes at all wavelengths down to zero. The orthodox treatment uses dimensional regularization plus renormalization: a formal substitution $d \to d - \varepsilon$ followed by analytic continuation back to $d = 4$ and absorption of the divergences into bare parameters. The McGucken framework supplies the source of the cutoff: the McGucken Sphere mode count per unit area is $1/\ell_P^2$ at the Planck scale (Theorem 21 of the present paper); the maximum physical momentum is $|k|_{\max} \sim 1/\ell_P$ (the Planck momentum); the integration $\int d^4k$ should be cut off at $|k| \sim 1/\ell_P$. The Wilson renormalization-group machinery [145] developed for treating UV-IR divergences is the operational implementation of this cutoff in the orthodox framework; the McGucken framework supplies the source for the cutoff (the Sphere mode count derived from $dx_4/dt = ic$) where the orthodox framework treats it as a parameter to be fixed phenomenologically. The asymptotic-safety conjecture of Weinberg 1979 [147] and the Reuter 1998 [148] machinery are identified in the present subsection as the orthodox response to the same question the McGucken framework answers through the Sphere mode count: the UV fixed point conjectured by asymptotic safety is the content of $dx_4/dt = ic$'s natural cutoff at the Planck scale.


*(4) Thermodynamic critical-point singularities.* The critical-point singularities of second-order phase transitions arise from coarse-graining bulk thermodynamic quantities (which are the Algebraic Channel averages over the operator algebra) onto order parameters at scales where the underlying dynamical mechanism (head-on McGucken Sphere collisions per molecule) is regular. The bulk thermodynamic quantities diverge because they are projections of the underlying mechanism onto the Algebraic Channel coarse-grained variables that lose information about the molecular substrate; the underlying dynamical mechanism (head-on Sphere collisions at rate $\Gamma_{\rm coll} \sim 10^{22}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ per molecule) does not diverge. The Wilson renormalization-group analysis [145] and Kadanoff block-spin construction [146] are the operational machinery for handling these projections, with the McGucken framework supplying the source: critical-point singularities are the Algebraic Channel projections of regular the Geometric Channel head-on Sphere-collision dynamics. The black-hole endpoint singularity at $M \to 0$ is similarly an artifact of extrapolating the Hawking temperature relation $T_H = \hbar c^3/(8\pi G M k_B)$ below the Planck mass $m_P$; for $M \to m_P$, the McGucken Sphere mode count of the horizon area $A_{\rm horizon} = 16\pi G^2 M^2/c^4$ drops below one and the orthodox thermodynamic relation ceases to apply. The third-law approach to absolute zero is the limit where the molecular kinetic energy approaches the head-on Sphere-collision threshold; below the threshold, the Sphere collisions cease to drive the random walk that produces thermal equilibrium, and the orthodox thermodynamic relations cease to apply.

#### §28.8.11 Barbour 2020: Replace Entropy with Shape Complexity, Postulate a Janus Point


Julian Barbour's *The Janus Point* (Basic Books, 2020, [203]) and the shape-dynamics program of Barbour, Koslowski, and Mercati [205] attempt a different escape route: replace entropy with a *complexity* measure derived from shape-dynamics and postulate that the universe has a minimum-complexity central state (the "Janus Point") with time flowing outward in both temporal directions from it. The arrow at our epoch comes from being in one of the two outward-flowing branches from the Janus Point.

The form is again the same. Shape complexity is a redefinition, not a derivation; the Janus Point itself is postulated rather than derived; the two-arrows-from-minimum picture replaces one mystery (why did entropy start low?) with another (why is there a Janus Point at all?). The vocabulary has shifted from entropy to shape complexity, from low-entropy initial state to Janus Point, from Past Hypothesis to two-branch shape dynamics — but the shape is identical to the previous episodes: postulate a special structure; use it to derive the arrow; appeal to the empirical record for self-justification; declare the special structure fundamental. The present paper's existing engagement with Barbour at §29.5 (Barbour's Janus Point and Shape Dynamics: The Direct Challenge to Entropy as Time's Arrow) supplies the diagnosis in detail.

#### §28.8.13 The Tautological-Substitution Pattern: How Shifting Terms Appears to Be Progress


The catalogue of nine episodes makes visible a pattern that is otherwise easy to miss because the vocabulary changes mask the equivalence. The pattern is: each new orthodox response shifts the vocabulary of the prior response while preserving the prior response's form (postulate + circular self-justification + declaration of fundamentality). The shift creates the appearance of progress because the new vocabulary speaks the language of the contemporary period — cosmological physics in Penrose's case, Humean metaphysics in Albert's case, multiverse cosmology in Carroll's case, shape dynamics in Barbour's case. The appearance of progress dissolves on examination of the form.

Five canonical tautological substitutions can be identified, with primary-source articulation of each:

*Tautology 1: Entropy increases ↔ Second Law holds.* Clausius 1865 formulates the Second Law in terms of entropy increase; subsequent literature explains entropy increase by invoking the Second Law. The circularity is at the level of definition: entropy is *defined* in terms that already smuggle the temporal direction (Clausius's $\Delta S = \int dQ/T$ requires a directionality of heat flow that is itself the empirical signature the Second Law is supposed to explain). The shift Eddington 1928 introduces — *time's arrow IS entropy increase* — removes the appearance of circularity by collapsing the two into a single identification, but the underlying problem (why does either of them have the unidirectional character?) remains.

*Tautology 2: Low-entropy initial state ↔ Past Hypothesis.* Boltzmann 1897 postulates an improbable initial state to derive entropy increase; Albert 2000 promotes the same postulate to law status under the name "Past Hypothesis." The shift from "postulated initial state" to "law of nature" is purely vocabulary; the content (an asymmetric boundary condition at $t=0$) is identical. The Past Hypothesis is the Boltzmann postulate rebranded.

*Tautology 3: Irreversibility is fundamental ↔ Non-commuting operator algebra.* Prigogine's 1970s program builds asymmetric operator algebras such that irreversibility appears as a property of the formal machinery; the asymmetry is encoded by the construction. The shift from "irreversibility is empirically observed" to "irreversibility follows from non-commuting operators" is the encoding of the empirical signature into formal machinery and the subsequent appeal to the formal machinery as the derivation. The encoding-and-appeal-to-encoding is circular.

*Tautology 4: Special cosmological initial condition ↔ Vanishing Weyl curvature ↔ Eternal inflation low-entropy patches.* Penrose 1979 specifies the Boltzmann postulate as vanishing Weyl curvature at the cosmological initial singularity; Carroll 2004 replaces this with eternal inflation generating low-entropy patches; Barbour 2020 replaces this with a Janus Point central state. The vocabulary changes from "improbable initial state" to "vanishing Weyl curvature" to "eternal inflation patch" to "Janus Point" — but the form (postulate a special cosmological structure; use it to derive the arrow; appeal to the empirical record for self-justification) is unchanged at each step.

*Tautology 5: It is the way it is because it is.* This is the underlying form of all the preceding tautologies. Boltzmann 1897 stated it explicitly: *"one should not expect to be able to deduce it from anything more fundamental."* Eddington 1928 stated it by identification (entropy = time, no further explanation needed). Reichenbach 1956 stated it by branch-system construction (the cosmic background is just unexplained). Prigogine 1970s stated it by operator encoding (the asymmetry is built into the operators). Penrose 1979 stated it by Weyl curvature hypothesis (the initial condition is just fundamental). Hawking 1988 stated it by no-boundary alignment (the three arrows just align). ### §28.9 The Deng–Hani–Ma 2024–2025 Derivation of the Boltzmann and Fluid Equations: Position Within the McGucken Framework


In August 2024, Yu Deng (University of Chicago), Zaher Hani (University of Michigan), and Xiao Ma (University of Michigan) posted [336, arXiv:2408.07818] a rigorous derivation of the Boltzmann equation on $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d \geq 2$) from Newton's laws applied to a hard-sphere particle system, valid on arbitrarily long time intervals — extending Oscar Lanford's 1975 result [314] which had been limited to very short times. In March 2025, the same authors posted a follow-up [337, arXiv:2503.01800] extending the derivation to the periodic torus $\mathbb{T}^d$ ($d \in \{2, 3\}$) and chaining it with the standard hydrodynamic limit results of Gallagher–Tristani [GallagherTristani], Caflisch [Caflisch1980], and Guo–Jang–Jiang [GuoJangJiang] to obtain the incompressible Navier–Stokes–Fourier system and the compressible Euler equation as effective equations for the macroscopic density, velocity, and temperature of the particle system. The authors state the significance directly in their abstract of [337]: *"we rigorously derive the fundamental PDEs of fluid mechanics, such as the compressible Euler and incompressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier equations, starting from the hard sphere particle systems undergoing elastic collisions. This resolves Hilbert's sixth problem, as it pertains to the program of deriving the fluid equations from Newton's laws by way of Boltzmann's kinetic theory."*

The Deng–Hani–Ma result is the most substantial recent advance on the kinetic-theory portion of Hilbert's Sixth Problem and warrants engagement with the McGucken framework developed in the present paper. The framework's position on their work is already published in [McGuckenHilbertSixth2026] §11.9 (elliotmcguckenphysics.com/2026/05/07), which establishes two theorems on the relationship between the two constructions: Theorem 47 (Position of Deng–Hani–Ma Within the Framework) and Theorem 48 (Composed Derivation Chain from $dx_4/dt = ic$ to the Fluid Equations). The present subsection restates the position in the theorem-numbering system of the present paper, with primary-source verbatim content from both Deng–Hani–Ma papers.

The framework's position is that the Deng–Hani–Ma result and the McGucken framework operate at different levels of the derivation hierarchy and are complementary. Deng–Hani–Ma rigorously execute the Newton $\to$ Boltzmann $\to$ fluid pipeline within the orthodox framework, taking the Liouville measure on phase space, the time-symmetric Newtonian dynamics, and the Maxwellian reference state as primitive inputs. The McGucken framework, by Theorems 7, 9, and 12 of the present paper, derives precisely those primitive inputs from the single principle $dx_4/dt = ic$. The two results address different layers of Hilbert's Sixth Problem: Deng–Hani–Ma complete the PDE limit-process pipeline; the McGucken framework supplies the source of the postulates that pipeline takes as input.


#### §28.9.1 The Deng–Hani–Ma Construction: Primary-Source Content


The Deng–Hani–Ma construction of [337] consists of four elements, each of which is treated in the McGucken framework at a specified derivational layer. We state each element in the authors' own formulation.

*Element (D1) — The phase-space measure.* Deng–Hani–Ma define the grand canonical ensemble in [337], Definition 1.3. The random hard-sphere configuration $\boldsymbol{z}^0 \in \mathcal{D}$ has probability law defined by the density
$$\frac{1}{N!} W_{0,N}(\boldsymbol{z}_N) := \frac{1}{\mathcal{Z}} \frac{(\alpha \cdot \varepsilon^{-(d-1)})^N}{N!} \prod_{j=1}^N n_0(z_j) \cdot \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{D}_N}(\boldsymbol{z}_N),$$
where the integration measure on state vectors $z_j = (x_j, v_j) \in \mathbb{T}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d$ is the standard Lebesgue product measure $\mathrm{d}z_j = \mathrm{d}^d x_j \, \mathrm{d}^d v_j$ ([337], their equation (1.8) with the non-overlapping domain $\mathcal{D}_N \subset \mathbb{T}^{dN} \times \mathbb{R}^{dN}$ enforcing $|x_i - x_j|_{\mathbb{T}} \geq \varepsilon$ for $i \neq j$). This is the Liouville measure restricted to the phase space of the hard-sphere system.

*Element (D2) — The microscopic dynamics.* Deng–Hani–Ma define the hard-sphere flow map $\mathcal{H}_N(t): \mathcal{D}_N \to \mathcal{D}_N$ in [337], Definition 1.1. Between collisions the particles undergo free transport at constant velocity; at contact $|x_i(t) - x_j(t)|_{\mathbb{T}} = \varepsilon$, the velocities exchange according to the elastic-collision rule ([337], their equation (1.4)):
$$v_i(t^+) = v_i(t) - \big((v_i(t) - v_j(t)) \cdot \omega\big)\omega, \quad v_j(t^+) = v_j(t) + \big((v_i(t) - v_j(t)) \cdot \omega\big)\omega,$$
where $\omega := (x_i(t) - x_j(t)) / \varepsilon \in \mathbb{S}^{d-1}$. Proposition 1.2 establishes that $\mathcal{H}_N(t)$ is a measure-preserving diffeomorphism satisfying the semigroup property. The dynamics is time-symmetric Newtonian.

*Element (D3) — The Boltzmann equation as kinetic limit.* Deng–Hani–Ma establish in [337], Theorem 1, that in the Boltzmann–Grad limit $N \to \infty$, $\varepsilon \to 0$ at $\alpha := N \varepsilon^{d-1}$ fixed (their equation (1.14): $\mathbb{E}(N) \cdot \varepsilon^{d-1} \approx \alpha$), the $s$-particle correlation functions $f_s(t)$ satisfy the $L^1$ bound (their (1.18))
$$\Big\| f_s(t, \boldsymbol{z}_s) - \prod_{j=1}^s n(t, z_j) \cdot \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{D}_s}(\boldsymbol{z}_s) \Big\|_{L^1(\mathbb{T}^{ds} \times \mathbb{R}^{ds})} \leq \varepsilon^\theta,$$
where $\theta > 0$ is an absolute dimension-dependent constant, $t \in [0, t_{\rm fin}]$ with $t_{\rm fin} \ll (\log |\log \varepsilon|)^{1/2}$, and $n(t, z)$ solves the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation ([337], Definition 1.4, their (1.15))
$$(\partial_t + v \cdot \nabla_x) n = \alpha \cdot \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \int_{\mathbb{S}^{d-1}} \big((v - v_1) \cdot \omega\big)_+ \cdot (n' n_1' - n n_1) \, \mathrm{d}\omega \, \mathrm{d}v_1.$$
The one-particle correlation function of the hard-sphere system converges to the solution of the Boltzmann equation in $L^1$ on the kinetic timescale.

*Element (D4) — The hydrodynamic limits.* Deng–Hani–Ma establish in [337], Theorems 2 and 3, that iterated limits (first $N \to \infty, \varepsilon \to 0$ with $\alpha = \delta^{-1}$ fixed, then $\alpha \to \infty$) recover the incompressible Navier–Stokes–Fourier system ([337], their equation (1.19)) with initial data of the Gallagher–Tristani well-prepared form (their (1.21)), and the compressible Euler equations ([337], their (1.40)) with initial data of the Caflisch Hilbert-expansion form (their (1.43)). Each fluid equation appears as the effective macroscopic-scale equation for the density, velocity, and temperature of the underlying particle system.

The time-asymmetry question receives explicit acknowledgment. Deng–Hani–Ma write in [337]: *"A fundamental intriguing question is the justification of the passage from the time-reversible microscopic Newton's theory to the time-irreversible mesoscopic Boltzmann theory."* And, describing the content of their Theorem 1: *"Since Theorem 1 covers the full lifespan of the Boltzmann solution, it could be viewed as a justification of the emergence of the time irreversible Boltzmann theory from the time reversible Newton's theory near Maxwellian."* The authors identify the emergence of the arrow of time as the fundamental intriguing question their result addresses at the level of a rigorous derivation, while leaving the source of the time-asymmetry itself unexplained beyond the near-Maxwellian condition on initial data.

Loschmidt's reversibility objection is dissolved by Theorem 12: the time-symmetric microscopic dynamics (Algebraic Channel) and the time-asymmetric Second Law (Geometric Channel) descend from the same single principle.*

*(P4) The Maxwellian reference state $\mathfrak{M}(t, x, v) = \rho / (2\pi T)^{d/2} \cdot e^{-|v - u|^2 / (2T)}$ that Deng–Hani–Ma take as the equilibrium state near which their initial data is prepared ([337], their equations (1.21) and (1.41)) is the local-equilibrium state of the ISO(3)-symmetric Compton-coupled Brownian motion of Theorem 4 of the present paper. #### §28.9.3 Verification of the Four Claims


We verify the four claims (P1) through (P4) of Theorem 28.9.1 directly.

*Verification of (P1).* Deng–Hani–Ma's grand canonical ensemble ([337], Definition 1.3) defines the probability density $W_{0,N}: \mathcal{D}_N \to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ on the non-overlapping domain $\mathcal{D}_N \subset \mathbb{T}^{dN} \times \mathbb{R}^{dN}$ using the integration measure $\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z}_N = \prod_{j=1}^N \mathrm{d}^d x_j \, \mathrm{d}^d v_j$ from their (1.8). This is the Liouville measure restricted to the phase space of the hard-sphere system. By Theorem 7 of the present paper, the Liouville measure on the phase space $T^*Q$ of a single particle is the unique $\mathrm{ISO}(3)$-Haar measure pushed forward via the cotangent-lift construction; the $N$-particle Liouville measure is the product Haar measure on $\mathrm{ISO}(3)^N$, with the action restricted to the non-overlapping domain via the constraint $|x_i - x_j|_{\mathbb{T}} \geq \varepsilon$. The measure used by Deng–Hani–Ma is the unique measure forced by the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via Haar's 1933 theorem, with the hard-sphere non-overlap as an additional constraint that respects the ISO(3)-symmetry.

*Verification of (P2).* Deng–Hani–Ma's hard-sphere flow map $\mathcal{H}_N(t)$ ([337], Definition 1.1(3)–(4)) evolves phase-space configurations by free transport between collisions and by the elastic-collision velocity exchange at contact (their (1.4)). Between collisions, the free-transport portion is generated by the classical Hamiltonian $H = \sum_j |v_j|^2 / 2$, with time evolution $\partial_t = \{\cdot, H\}$ given by the Poisson bracket. The classical Hamiltonian flow is the classical limit of the quantum Hamiltonian flow generated by $\hat H = i\hbar \partial_t$, which by Stone's theorem is the infinitesimal generator of the one-parameter unitary time-translation group on the Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$, descending from the Algebraic Channel temporal-translation symmetry of $dx_4/dt = ic$. The elastic-collision rule (their (1.4)) is a momentum-conserving boundary condition that respects the $\mathrm{ISO}(3)^N$ symmetry of the Algebraic Channel. The full hard-sphere dynamics is a classical-limit descendant of the McGucken Principle.

*Verification of (P3).* Deng–Hani–Ma's Theorem 1 produces the Boltzmann equation
$(\partial_t + v \cdot \nabla_x) n = \alpha \mathcal{Q}(n, n)$
as the effective equation for the one-particle correlation function in the kinetic limit ([337], their (1.15) and Theorem 1). The collision operator $\mathcal{Q}(n, n)$ satisfies the Boltzmann H-theorem: the $H$-functional $H(t) = \int n \log n \, \mathrm{d}z$ satisfies $\mathrm{d}H/\mathrm{d}t \leq 0$, equivalent to $\mathrm{d}S/\mathrm{d}t \geq 0$ for the Boltzmann entropy $S = -\kB H$. Deng–Hani–Ma explicitly frame the time-asymmetry as the question their work addresses at the level of a rigorous derivation:

> *"Since Theorem 1 covers the full lifespan of the Boltzmann solution, it could be viewed as a justification of the emergence of the time irreversible Boltzmann theory from the time reversible Newton's theory near Maxwellian."* ([337], their p. 3)

Their construction produces the Boltzmann equation rigorously; the source of the time-asymmetry itself — the reason the Boltzmann H-theorem holds forward in time rather than backward — remains outside the scope of their derivation, deferred to the "near Maxwellian" condition on initial data. In the McGucken framework, the source of the time-asymmetry is the $+ic$ orientation of $x_4$'s expansion. Theorem 9 of the present paper establishes the strict-monotonicity result $\mathrm{d}S/\mathrm{d}t = (3/2)\kB / t > 0$ for massive-particle ensembles undergoing the spherical isotropic random walk generated by the Compton-coupled Brownian motion of Theorem 4; the strict positivity of $D > 0$ in the resulting Wiener-process density is a direct geometric consequence of the $+ic$ orientation. The Boltzmann H-theorem irreversibility that Deng–Hani–Ma derive in the kinetic limit is the kinetic-theory manifestation of the same $+ic$-oriented Geometric-Channel content. Loschmidt's reversibility objection is dissolved by Theorem 12 of the present paper: time-symmetric microscopic dynamics (Algebraic Channel) and the time-asymmetric Second Law (Geometric Channel) descend from the same single principle.

*Verification of (P4).* Deng–Hani–Ma's fluid limits require initial data prepared near the Maxwellian reference state $\mathfrak{M}(t, x, v) = \rho / (2\pi T)^{d/2} \cdot e^{-|v - u|^2/(2T)}$ (their (1.41)) for the compressible Euler limit ([337], Theorem 3, their (1.43)) and near the global Maxwellian $(2\pi)^{-d/2} e^{-|v|^2/2}$ for the incompressible Navier–Stokes–Fourier limit (their (1.21)). The Maxwellian is a stationary state of the Boltzmann equation, and restricting to initial data near it allows the proof to control the kinetic limit on long time intervals. The origin of the Maxwellian as the appropriate reference state — the reason the universe of admissible initial conditions is restricted to those near a thermal-equilibrium Maxwellian — is outside the scope of the Deng–Hani–Ma derivation. The orthodox literature on the Past Hypothesis [236, 303, 237, 235] is the standard locus of attempts to address it, with Penrose's $10^{-10^{123}}$ Weyl-curvature fine-tuning as the standard quantitative measure of the required special initial condition. In the McGucken framework, the answer comes from Theorem 13 of the present paper: the lowest-entropy moment of any system participating in $x_4$'s expansion is the moment $t = 0$ of $x_4$'s origin. The Maxwellian reference state at later times is the local-equilibrium state attained by the spherical isotropic random walk starting from that origin; its geometric source is the monotonic radial growth of the McGucken Sphere from $t = 0$. No fine-tuning is required because the geometry of $x_4$-expansion selects $t = 0$ as the initial moment by construction; Penrose's $10^{-10^{123}}$ measures probability under a uniform prior that the McGucken framework does not adopt.

*(C5)*. Apply [337], Theorem 2, to the Boltzmann equation of (C4): take the iterated limit $\varepsilon \to 0$ first with $\alpha = \delta^{-1}$ fixed (which gives (C4)), then $\delta \to 0$ with initial data prepared near the Maxwellian (their (1.21)). The macroscopic fields $(u, \rho)$ on $\mathbb{T}^d$ satisfy the incompressible Navier–Stokes–Fourier system (their (1.19)):
$$\partial_t u + u \cdot \nabla u - \mu_1 \Delta u = -\nabla p, \qquad \partial_t \rho + u \cdot \nabla \rho - \mu_2 \Delta \rho = 0, \qquad \nabla \cdot u = 0.$$

*(C6)*. Apply [337], Theorem 3, to the Boltzmann equation of (C4) with initial data given by the Caflisch Hilbert expansion (their (1.43)). The macroscopic fields $(\rho, u, T)$ satisfy the compressible Euler system (their (1.40)).

*(C7)*. The Boltzmann equation in (C4) satisfies the standard H-theorem: $\mathrm{d}H/\mathrm{d}t \leq 0$ for $H = \int n \log n \, \mathrm{d}z$ along solutions, with equality only at local Maxwellians. The non-strict inequality of the standard H-theorem is the kinetic-limit content of the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel in the McGucken framework. The strict-monotonicity result $\mathrm{d}S/\mathrm{d}t = (3/2)\kB / t > 0$ of Theorem 9 of the present paper is the Boltzmann entropy production rate at fixed kinetic-limit parameters; the strictness is recovered when the system is away from local Maxwellian equilibrium and approaches it through the Geometric Channel's spherical isotropic random walk.

The composition sequence (C1) $\to$ (C2) $\to$ (C3) $\to$ (C4) $\to$ \{(C5), (C6), (C7)\} is finite and uses only the theorems of the present paper together with the cited external theorems of [55] and [337]. Therefore (C1) through (C7) are theorems of the McGucken framework composed with the Deng–Hani–Ma construction. $\Box$


#### §28.9.5 Implication for the Status of Hilbert's Sixth Problem


Theorem 28.9.2 establishes that the kinetic-theory portion of Hilbert's Sixth Problem — the *"rigorous theory of limiting processes ... which lead from the atomistic view to the laws of motion of continua"* that Hilbert specified in his 1900 address, quoted by Deng–Hani–Ma in [337], §1.1 — has a complete chain of theorems from the single principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ to the compressible Euler and incompressible Navier–Stokes–Fourier equations. The Deng–Hani–Ma 2024–2025 result supplies the rigorous PDE-level execution of the Newton $\to$ Boltzmann $\to$ fluid pipeline; the McGucken framework supplies the source of the Newtonian and probabilistic inputs. Composed, the two results yield the kinetic-theory subdivision of Hilbert's Sixth Problem in full:

$$dx_4/dt = ic \; [\text{1 principle}] \xrightarrow{\text{McGucken}} \text{Liouville + Newton's laws} \; [\text{orthodox starting point}]$$
$$\xrightarrow{\text{[337]}} \text{Boltzmann} \; [\text{kinetic theory}] \xrightarrow{\text{[337]}} \text{Navier–Stokes, Euler} \; [\text{continuum mechanics}].$$

The Scientific American framing of Deng–Hani–Ma [368] as a major stride toward grounding physics in mathematics is accurate for the kinetic-and-hydrodynamic portion of Hilbert's Sixth Problem treated within the orthodox foundation. The Quanta Magazine coverage [310], which characterizes the Deng–Hani–Ma work as illuminating why time cannot flow in reverse via a rigorous derivation of the emergence of the arrow of time from time-reversible microscopic dynamics near Maxwellian, reflects the same reading. The McGucken framework extends the grounding one level deeper: the orthodox postulates that Deng–Hani–Ma take as inputs — the Liouville measure, the time-symmetric Newtonian dynamics, the Maxwellian reference state, the near-Maxwellian condition that carries the time-asymmetry — are themselves theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$ (Theorems 7, 12, 4, and 13 of the present paper, respectively).

The four sectors Hilbert specifically named in his 1900 address and 1902 followup — probability, mechanics, quantum theory, and kinetic theory of gases — descend from the same single principle $dx_4/dt = ic$. The kinetic-theory sector is now executed rigorously through the composed chain: the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel symmetry content supplies the Liouville measure (Theorem 7); the classical-limit Hamiltonian dynamics supplies the Newtonian flow (Theorem 12); the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel geometric-propagation content supplies the time-asymmetry of the H-theorem (Theorems 9 and 11); the Deng–Hani–Ma kinetic-and-hydrodynamic limits supply the Boltzmann equation, the Navier–Stokes–Fourier system, and the compressible Euler equation. The completed chain is the empirical validation, at the highest level of PDE rigor available in the current literature, of the McGucken framework's claim: the four historically separated sectors of Hilbert's Sixth Problem are one framework, with the single principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ as the primary source and the orthodox postulates recovered as derived theorems.

The framework's own position — that the Deng–Hani–Ma work and the McGucken derivation are complementary, at different levels of the derivation hierarchy — is the position published in [McGuckenHilbertSixth2026] §11.9 (elliotmcguckenphysics.com/2026/05/07). The present subsection restates that position in the theorem-numbering system of the thermodynamics paper, with primary-source verbatim content from both Deng–Hani–Ma papers. **Rigor grade: G1 for the composed chain (C1)–(C7) treating the external theorems [337, Thms 1–3] as verified; the primary-source content quoted here is verbatim from [336, 337] with page and equation locators.**



### §28.9.6 Where the Time-Asymmetry Is Injected in the Deng–Hani–Ma Construction: Three Concealed Sites and the Critical Consensus


The catalog of §28.8.1–§28.8.15 documented ten historical episodes (Clausius 1865 through Barbour 2020) in which the arrow of time was moved from one location in the theoretical apparatus to another while being described as *derived* rather than *postulated*. Table 1 of §28.8.12 summarized the pattern. The present subsection examines Deng–Hani–Ma 2024–2025 [336, 337] against the same diagnostic and finds that the pattern continues. The Deng–Hani–Ma construction migrates Boltzmann's Stosszahlansatz from every-collision imposition (Boltzmann 1872) to initial-time-only factorization (following Lanford 1975 [314]); it then propagates the resulting factorization forward via a partial time expansion whose asymmetry is forced by the specific direction from which the cumulants are expanded; and it restricts the fluid-limit initial data to a neighborhood of a Maxwellian equilibrium, which itself carries the low-entropy content required for the Second Law's directionality. Each of the three sites is required for the proof to work. Each has been identified in the philosophy-of-physics and mathematical-physics literature over the past decade as the location where the time-asymmetry enters the derivation. This subsection reads the three sites in the primary-source language of Deng–Hani–Ma and matches each to the corresponding McGucken framework theorem that supplies the asymmetric content from $dx_4/dt = ic$ as a derived consequence rather than by postulate.


#### §28.9.6.1 Deng–Hani–Ma's Own Acknowledgment: The Paradox Named in Their §1.3.2


The Deng–Hani–Ma 2024 paper does not conceal the irreversibility question. The opening paragraph of §1 [336, p.\ 1] names the paradox openly: the macroscopic Boltzmann equation displays time-irreversibility with an entropy functional increasing forward in time, while the microscopic hard-sphere Newtonian dynamics remains time-reversible; the passage from one to the other the authors describe as the emergence of the arrow of time [336, p.\ 1].

Section §1.3.2 of [336], titled ``The cumulant ansatz'', contains the authors' own analysis of why the propagation of their cumulant estimate cannot proceed by any Banach-norm-based inductive scheme. Their argument, in the primary source, runs by contradiction: they assume such a scheme existed, then observe that any Banach norm on the cumulants $E_H(\ell\tau)$ remains invariant under the velocity-flip operation $v_j \mapsto -v_j$; under the time-reversibility of the hard-sphere Newtonian dynamics [336, Def.\ 1.1], the same scheme would then propagate backward in time from time $\tau$ to time $0$ as effectively as it propagates forward from time $\tau$ to time $2\tau$; this would produce a factorized description of $f_s(0,\bm{z}_s)$ in terms of the one-particle function $f(2\tau,\cdot)$, contradicting the initial factorization in terms of $f(0,\cdot)$. Their own conclusion, summarized in their §1.3.2, attributes the failure to the time irreversibility of the target Boltzmann equation.

The authors then introduce a partial time expansion as the resolution. The partial time expansion propagates cumulants backward from time $\ell\tau$ toward time $0$ (where the cumulants vanish by the initial-data assumption of Definition 1.3), while holding the leading factorized term $f^{\mathcal{A}}((\ell-1)\tau)$ fixed rather than expanding it backward. The forward-in-time direction receives asymmetric embedding in this construction: the leading term is transported forward, the cumulants are expanded backward toward the initial-condition asymmetry, and the two are combined to produce a forward-only propagation. The authors' own summary of the method's significance, in the closing sentence of §1.3.3 [336, §1.3.3], describes the partial expansion as ``crucial in obtaining a time irreversible equation from time reversible dynamics''. That sentence supplies the authors' own acknowledgment that the time-asymmetric output descends from the combination of the time-reversible dynamics with the partial expansion construction, which selects a direction.

The v2 version of [336] sharpens the language of §1.3.2. The v2 text [336, v2, §1.3.2, verified-read from arXiv:2408.07818v2, p.\ 10] states directly:

> ``In this way, we see the creation of the distinction between going forward and backward in time.''

The v2 sentence names the distinction as *created* by the cumulant-ansatz construction rather than *identified* within a pre-existing time-asymmetry of the underlying Newtonian dynamics. The passage sits within the v2 worked example $\ell = s = 2$, $H = \{1,2\}$, in which the cumulant $E_H(\tau, z_1, z_2)$ behaves as the indicator function of a set of two-particle collision states, and the change of variables $v_j \mapsto -v_j$ produces a different set whose contribution to the one-point density does not vanish. The v3 version rewrites §1.3.2 and drops this specific sentence, though the underlying observation about the failure of Banach-norm induction is preserved and sharpened in v3 §1.3.3 (below). The v2 sentence is retained in the record as the sharpest primary-source acknowledgment of the constructive origin of the arrow-of-time distinction within the proof architecture.

The v2 §2.1 discussion of the cumulant ansatz, in its point (1) after the schematic eq.\ (1.26), states the cumulant-memorization content in the verified-read primary source [336, v2, §2.1, point (1), verified-read from arXiv:2408.07818v2 via full-text PDF fetch]:

> ``This ansatz retains all the structural information of $E_H(\ell\tau)$ by memorizing the full collision history that contributes to this cumulant (see the precise formulas in Propositions 4.17 and 4.21).''

The v2 wording locates the memory content in a specific proof-mechanism object: the cumulant expression $E_H(\ell\tau)$ that carries the record of past collisions to time $\ell\tau$. This is the property the partial expansion is designed to propagate, and the property whose forward-only accumulation from $t=0$ toward $t=\ell\tau$ makes the propagation directionally asymmetric. The v3 version retains equivalent content in v3 §1.3.4 with the phrase ``retains the ordering between different collisions of the same particle, and the layer of each collision'' [336, v3, §1.3.4, verified-read from arXiv:2408.07818v3 via full-text PDF fetch].

A note on the v1 (14 Aug 2024) preprint version. The v1 preprint reportedly contained a §1.3.5 titled ``The arrow of time, and resolution of the irreversibility paradox'' — this section title is attested by Google search-snippet excerpts of the ResearchGate mirror of the v1 PDF and by the v1 table of contents visible in that snippet, but the present writing has not directly fetched the arXiv v1 PDF (which is not currently reachable via this session's sanctioned fetch tools). The v3 version [336, v3, §1.3.3, verified-read from arXiv:2408.07818v3, titled ``The cumulant ansatz''] contains the sharpest no-go argument. The v3 primary source states:

> ``There is something deep behind this phenomenon: for any Banach space $X$, it is not possible to obtain smallness of $\|E_H(\ell\tau)\|_X$ (in the form of (1.21)) using only smallness of the same norm $\|E_H((\ell-1)\tau)\|_X$, precisely because of the time irreversibility of Boltzmann's equation.''

The argument that follows in v3 §1.3.3 uses the time reversibility of the Newtonian dynamics via velocity-sign flipping to establish that any inductive scheme based on a norm bound would work equally well forward-in-time and backward-in-time, contradicting the observed forward-only propagation of the initial-condition factorization. The v3 authors conclude:

> ``In fact, in order to prove (1.21), we need to propagate structural information (which goes beyond any Banach norms) for the cumulants $E_H(\ell\tau)$ by induction in $\ell$.''

This is the authors' own no-go argument. The argument establishes that the arrow of time in their proof cannot reside in any size estimate — any $L^p$ norm, any Banach space, any magnitude measure alone — and requires an informational content the authors call in their own v3 wording (preserved verbatim above) ``structural information.''\footnote{The v3 verbatim wording of Deng–Hani–Ma uses the noun phrase ``structural information'' in the technical sense of the information content that goes beyond a norm bound. The present-paper convention of avoiding the adjective family ``structural''/``structurally'' as filler applies to the paper's own prose, not to verbatim quotations of primary sources, which are preserved as written.}

The McGucken framework's derivation of the content the v3 authors identify: the Sphere-expansion probability content is a the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel (participant-in-$x_4$) quantity carrying the $+ic$ orientation at every event, while cumulant size estimates are the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel (observer-of-$x_4$) quantities carrying magnitude only; the framework's derivational architecture separates the two channels at the substrate level and locates the arrow of time in the Geometric Channel, per Theorem 11 of the present paper. The v3 Banach-space no-go establishes from the mathematical-physics side of the derivation that the arrow of time is a Geometric-Channel fact, which is what the McGucken framework establishes from the geometric side.
