The three concealed sites developed in the remainder of this subsection are the locations at which the asymmetric content enters the construction.


#### §28.9.6.2 Site 1: The Initial-Time-Only Factorization (The Grand Canonical Ensemble at $t=0$)


Definition 1.3 of [336] specifies the initial data for the hard-sphere system as a grand canonical ensemble with density function
$$\frac{1}{N!} W_{0,N}(\bm{z}_N) = \frac{1}{\mathcal{Z}} \frac{\varepsilon^{-(d-1)N}}{N!} \prod_{j=1}^N f_0(z_j) \cdot \mathbbm{1}_{\mathcal{D}_N}(\bm{z}_N)$$
The initial density is a product $\prod_{j=1}^N f_0(z_j)$ modified only by the non-overlap indicator $\mathbbm{1}_{\mathcal{D}_N}$ that excludes configurations where any two particles are within distance $\varepsilon$ of each other. At $t=0$, the $N$ particles are independent and identically distributed. At $t>0$, correlations arise dynamically from collisions. The cumulants $E_H(0)$ vanish at $t=0$; the cumulants $E_H(\ell\tau)$ at later times measure the departure from independence.

The asymmetric content of this specification takes the following form: the factorization holds only at $t=0$ and propagates forward only. A time-reversed configuration in which the particles are i.i.d.\ at $t = t_{\mathrm{fin}}$ and the correlations grow backward from $t_{\mathrm{fin}}$ toward $t=0$ remains equally consistent with the time-reversible Newtonian dynamics [336, Def.\ 1.1], yet violates the initial-condition postulate of [336, Def.\ 1.3]. The choice of $t=0$ as the moment of i.i.d.\ factorization, rather than $t=t_{\mathrm{fin}}$ or any intermediate time, supplies the origin of the asymmetry.

The migration from Boltzmann's original Stosszahlansatz to this initial-time-only factorization has been documented in the philosophy-of-physics literature. Ardourel's 2017 study [341] of the derivation identifies the migration explicitly. Where Boltzmann's 1872 derivation imposed the Stosszahlansatz at every collision, Lanford's 1975 derivation and its successors reduced this to ``only a factorization condition at the initial time'' [341, §2.2]. The asymmetric assumption stayed in the theory; it changed location, moving from the collision-by-collision level to the initial-condition level. Deng–Hani–Ma 2024 inherits this migration and extends it to arbitrarily long times.

Dekkers–Landsman's 2025 analysis of Deng–Hani–Ma [342, arXiv:2512.20421] states the diagnosis in unqualified terms. Their §1, item 2, observes that ``the i.i.d.\ assumption itself remains unjustified'' [342, §1]. Their reading of the Deng–Hani–Ma proof, developed in their §2, traces the irreversibility of the output to the i.i.d.-at-$t=0$ postulate combined with the convention of tracing motion forward in time from $t=0$. The i.i.d. postulate remains what Deng–Hani–Ma prove propagates; it lies outside what Deng–Hani–Ma derive.

**The McGucken framework's supply of this content.** Under Theorem 7 of the present paper, the Liouville measure on the hard-sphere phase space $\mathbb{T}^{dN} \times \mathbb{R}^{dN}$ is the unique $\mathrm{ISO}(3)$-Haar measure pushed forward to the cotangent bundle $T^*Q$, with the $N$-particle product measure on $(\mathrm{ISO}(3))^N$ providing the factorized initial density. The factorization holds at every event of the McGucken manifold $\mathcal{M}_G$ as a consequence of the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel algebraic-symmetry content of $dx_4/dt = ic$, in place of a postulate on a distinguished initial time. The distinguished moment $t=0$ is supplied by Theorem 13 of the present paper as the origin of the McGucken Sphere's radial expansion, and follows as a geometric consequence of the Sphere-starting-at-radius-zero content of the framework, in place of a postulate on the initial ensemble.


#### §28.9.6.3 Site 2: The Forward-Time Convention in the Partial Time Expansion


The partial time expansion of [336, §1.3.3] introduces an asymmetric feature into the propagation of cumulants across time layers $[(\ell-1)\tau, \ell\tau]$ with $1 \leq \ell \leq \mathfrak{L}$. The construction expands the cumulants $E_H((\ell-1)\tau)$ backward in time toward $t=0$, where they vanish by the initial-data assumption, while the leading factorized term $f^{\mathcal{A}}((\ell-1)\tau)$ remains fixed and receives approximation by the Boltzmann solution rather than backward expansion. The asymmetry between the treatment of the two terms allows the estimate to close: the cumulants receive small-parameter gains $\varepsilon^{\alpha|H|}$ that offset the $t^n$ divergence of the time-series expansion, while the leading term is transported forward layer-by-layer without accumulating divergence.

Under time reversal $t \mapsto -t$ combined with velocity reversal $v_j \mapsto -v_j$, the Newtonian dynamics remains invariant [336, Def.\ 1.1] and every trajectory has a time-reversed partner. The partial time expansion, however, loses invariance under this operation. Reversing the expansion direction would require expanding the leading term $f^{\mathcal{A}}$ backward and holding the cumulants $E_H$ fixed, which reverses the roles of the two terms in the estimate closure. The proof does not survive this role reversal, because the cumulant gains that offset the divergence come from the initial-data factorization at $t=0$, and expanding backward from $t=0$ toward $t_{\mathrm{fin}}$ has no analogous small-parameter source at $t_{\mathrm{fin}}$.

Dekkers–Landsman [342, §1, item 5] identify this convention as the second component of the injection. Their analysis develops the argument through the theory of algorithmic randomness applied to microscopic trajectories, and concludes that the time-asymmetry of the derived Boltzmann equation traces to the time-asymmetry of the randomness condition relative to a probability measure that makes the particles i.i.d.\ at $t=0$ specifically, rather than at any other time. The forward-time convention thus operates as the specific direction in which the partial expansion propagates the initial-condition factorization, rather than as a passive descriptive choice.

Uffink–Valente 2015 [338, *Foundations of Physics* 45] had reached the corresponding conclusion for the earlier Lanford 1975 short-time result. Their analysis of Lanford's proof led them to the diagnosis that the derivation contains ``no time-asymmetric ingredient at all'' [338] at the level of the microscopic dynamics — which entails, by their argument, that whatever irreversibility appears in the output arrived through the initial-condition and expansion-direction conventions rather than through derivation. Deng–Hani–Ma 2024 extends the Lanford framework to arbitrarily long times but inherits the same feature.

**A fine-grained locus within Site 2: the left-continuity convention at collision instants (Ardourel-relocated).** Deng–Hani–Ma implement the incoming-versus-outgoing distinction through a left-continuity convention on velocities at collision instants. Definition 1.1(3b) of [336, v3, verified-read from arXiv:2408.07818v3] specifies: at a collision time $t$, position remains continuous $x_i(t^+) = x_i(t)$, and velocity updates $v_i(t^+) = v_i(t) - ((v_i(t) - v_j(t)) \cdot \omega)\omega$, ``where $t^+$ indicates right limit at time $t$'' [336, v3, Def.\ 1.1(3b), verified-read]. The definition then imposes the convention [336, v3, Def.\ 1.1(3b), verified-read from arXiv PDF v3]:

> ``in this definition (and similarly for all the modified dynamics below) we also always require $v_j(t)$ to be left continuous in $t$, so $v_j(t) = v_j(t^-)$.''

Figure 1 of [336, v3, verified-read caption] states the same convention pictorially: $(v_i(t), v_j(t)) = (v_i(t^-), v_j(t^-))$ are the incoming velocities and $(v_i(t^+), v_j(t^+))$ are the outgoing velocities. The convention selects the incoming velocity state as the value the flow map returns at the collision instant, while the outgoing state is reached only in the right-limit.

The Ardourel 2017 objection [341, engaged at §28.9.6.5(b) below] lands on the Deng–Hani–Ma construction in relocated form. Where Ardourel's diagnosis in *Foundations of Physics* 47 targeted the Lanford proof's explicit choice of ``incoming, rather than outgoing, configurations for collision points,'' the Deng–Hani–Ma construction absorbs the same choice into the left-continuity convention of the flow definition. The choice migrated from a proof-time decision to a definitional convention on continuity, and the asymmetric content — selection of incoming velocities as the value the flow returns at the collision instant, in preference to outgoing velocities — remains present in the mathematics.

*Rigor grade.* The identification of the left-continuity convention as a relocated form of the Ardourel injection site is a G2 grade result. The verbatim primary-source content of Definition 1.1(3b) and Figure 1 caption is verified-read from arXiv:2408.07818v3 (G1 evidence). The interpretation of this convention as the relocated site of the Ardourel 2017 objection is a reading of the definition against Ardourel's prior-art critique — a reading the Deng–Hani–Ma authors do not make in the paper, where the left-continuity convention is presented as a technical continuity requirement rather than as an asymmetric assumption. The G2 grade reflects the interpretive component: the injection is present in the mathematics with verified-read primary-source content, and the identification of it as an injection site requires reading the definition against Ardourel's framework.

**The McGucken framework's supply of this content.** Under Theorem 11 of the present paper, the $+ic$ orientation of the fourth-dimension expansion at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$ supplies the forward-time direction as a geometric fact rather than a proof-technique convention. The five arrows of time (thermodynamic, cosmological, radiation, quantum-measurement, psychological) descend as parallel projections of the same $+ic$ orientation. No forward-time convention receives imposition on the proof; the direction of time is the direction of $x_4$-expansion at every event.


#### §28.9.6.4 Site 3: The Near-Maxwellian Restriction in the Hydrodynamic Limit


The companion paper [337, arXiv:2503.01800] extends the kinetic-limit result of [336] to the fluid limit, obtaining the incompressible Navier–Stokes–Fourier system and the compressible Euler equation. The hydrodynamic-limit portion of the derivation requires the initial data to be prepared near a Maxwellian equilibrium. The Maxwellian form, in the notation of [336, §1.4.1, eq.\ (1.26)], is
$$f(t,x,v) = \frac{\rho(t,x)}{(2\pi T(t,x))^{d/2}} \exp\!\left(-\frac{|v-u(t,x)|^2}{2T(t,x)}\right)$$
This is the maximum-entropy distribution at fixed local $(\rho, u, T)$. Restricting the fluid-limit initial data to a neighborhood of a global Maxwellian restricts initial data to configurations already close to thermal equilibrium.

The asymmetric content of this restriction is subtle but present. The Maxwellian is the fixed point of the Boltzmann collision operator; it is the state at which $dH/dt = 0$. Perturbations away from the Maxwellian evolve back toward it under the Boltzmann equation, with the direction of the evolution set by the H-theorem. The near-Maxwellian restriction selects initial data for which the subsequent evolution is a relaxation toward the equilibrium fixed point, rather than data for which the evolution is arbitrary. The direction of relaxation — toward equilibrium as $t$ increases — carries the Second Law's directionality in the fluid limit.

An initial condition prepared far from any Maxwellian would lack this property. The Boltzmann equation for such data might have no global smooth solution; the fluid limit might not be well-defined; the relaxation toward equilibrium might occur in an unobserved direction. The near-Maxwellian restriction is what makes the Deng–Hani–Ma fluid-limit derivation reproduce the observed Second Law directionality. The restriction lacks derivation from anything upstream in the construction; it is a choice of the neighborhood in initial-data space, and the choice is asymmetric in the sense that the neighborhood of the Maxwellian is a distinguished region.

**The McGucken framework's supply of this content.** Under Theorem 13 of the present paper, the lowest-entropy moment of any system participating in $x_4$-expansion is the moment $t=0$ of the McGucken Sphere's origin. The Maxwellian reference state at later times is the local-equilibrium state attained by the spherical isotropic random walk of Theorem 8, whose source is the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel monotonic radial growth of the McGucken Sphere from $t=0$. No fine-tuning of a neighborhood in initial-data space is required, because the geometry of $x_4$-expansion selects $t=0$ as the moment of lowest entropy by the framework's own convention on the $+ic$ orientation (Convention $\kappa$, Theorem 11). Penrose's $10^{-10^{123}}$ fine-tuning [235] measures the probability of the low-entropy initial state under a uniform prior on phase space; the McGucken framework does not adopt this prior, and the low-entropy initial state is a geometric consequence of the Sphere-radius-zero starting condition rather than a fine-tuned selection.


#### §28.9.6.5 The Critical Consensus: A Decade of Literature Across Four Communities on This Question


The three injection sites developed above restate identifications appearing in four distinct research communities over the past decade: (a) the mathematical-physics community around Deng–Hani–Ma's own predecessors, (b) the philosophy-of-physics community, (c) the alternative-kinetic-theory community developing time-reversal-invariant formulations, and (d) the physics-community critics who identify the dilute-gas restriction as the physical limitation of the derivation. The convergence across these communities on the same set of injection sites — while differing in emphasis and in the framework offered as replacement — is the empirical content of the diagnosis developed in §28.9.6.2 through §28.9.6.4.


##### (a) Deng–Hani–Ma's own mathematical-physics predecessors: the one-sided-chaos literature


The technical predecessors of Deng–Hani–Ma — Bodineau, Gallagher, Saint-Raymond, Simonella — wrote in 2016 a dedicated paper analyzing exactly where irreversibility appears in the Boltzmann-Grad limit process:

**Bodineau–Gallagher–Saint-Raymond–Simonella 2016/2018** [340, arXiv:1612.03722, ``One-sided convergence in the 101-Grad limit'', published as *Ann.\ Fac.\ Sci.\ Toulouse Math.* (6) **27** (2018), no.\ 5, pp.\ 985–1022, abstract verified via arXiv:1612.03722 abstract page and Numdam publisher page item AFST\_2018\_6\_27\_5\_985\_0; full-text PDF not directly fetched in this writing] gave a dedicated technical review of Lanford's theorem focused on the initial data. The verbatim published-journal-version abstract [340, abstract only, verified from arXiv:1612.03722 abstract page and from Numdam publisher metadata; full-paper text not directly fetched]:

> ``We review various contributions on the fundamental work of Lanford [21] deriving the Boltzmann equation from (reversible) hard-sphere dynamics in the low density limit. We focus especially on the assumptions made on the initial data and on how they encode irreversibility. The impossibility to reverse time in the Boltzmann equation (expressed for instance by Boltzmann's H-theorem) is related to the lack of convergence of higher order marginals on some singular sets. Explicit counterexamples single out the microscopic sets where the initial data should converge in order to produce the Boltzmann dynamics.''

Two features of the primary-source abstract merit attention. First, the four authors — Deng–Hani–Ma's own technical predecessors and the Bourbaki reviewers of the Deng–Hani–Ma proof (see the 2026 Bourbaki entry below) — identify the initial data as encoding the irreversibility, in the exact wording ``how they encode irreversibility.'' The word ``encode'' places the arrow of time content within the initial-condition specification rather than within the dynamics. Second, the abstract signals that explicit counterexamples single out the microscopic sets on which the initial data must converge to produce Boltzmann dynamics. The claims of the full paper concerning the specific counterexample sets are not directly verified in the present writing (only the abstract is verified-read); the abstract's high-level diagnosis is the primary-source content engaged here.

The 2016 paper predates Deng–Hani–Ma's long-time proof by eight years, and the diagnosis its abstract states applies to the long-time proof without modification, because Deng–Hani–Ma preserve the same initial-time factorization (their Definition 1.3, engaged at §28.9.6.2 above) and forward-time-of-limit convention (their §1.3.3, engaged at §28.9.6.3 above) that the 2016 abstract identifies as the carriers of the asymmetry. The published journal version at *Ann.\ Fac.\ Sci.\ Toulouse* is the referee-cleared restatement of the same diagnosis and is the citation form used by the mathematical-physics community that continues to develop this line, including in the 2026 Bourbaki review below.

**Denlinger 2016 and 2017** [Denlinger2016, arXiv:1605.00589, ``The propagation of chaos for a rarefied gas of hard spheres in the whole space''; Denlinger2017, arXiv:1706.09961, ``Observables and Strong One-Sided Chaos in the Boltzmann-Grad Limit''] developed the concept of strong one-sided chaos, which he identifies as the property Lanford's proof actually propagates (as opposed to the two-sided chaos that would be time-symmetric). From Denlinger 2017, abstract: the strength of convergence proven at positive times was much weaker than that which had to be assumed at the initial time, which is at odds with the standard propagation-of-chaos idea. Denlinger's framework is one of several proposals in the mathematical-physics literature for the notion of one-sided chaos as the property that captures the emergence of irreversibility. The Deng–Hani–Ma proof extends the Lanford result to longer times while retaining the underlying one-sided character; the one-sided-chaos literature therefore identifies the same asymmetric ingredient in Deng–Hani–Ma as in Lanford.

**Bodineau–Gallagher–Saint-Raymond–Simonella 2026** [Bourbaki2026, arXiv:2602.04407, Séminaire BOURBAKI n°1247, January 2026, ``Derivation of the Boltzmann equation from hard-sphere dynamics [after Y. Deng, Z. Hani, and X. Ma]''] gave the official Bourbaki seminar review of Deng–Hani–Ma. The seminar was delivered by the same four mathematicians who authored the 2016 one-sided-convergence paper — Deng–Hani–Ma's own predecessors and the most authoritative technical readers of the work. Their review devotes §1.3 to the Loschmidt paradox and the loss of information, framing the irreversibility question as a matter of gradual loss of microscopic detail encoded by the entropy production. The Bourbaki review confirms that the injection sites identified in the 2016 one-sided-convergence paper remain present in the Deng–Hani–Ma proof and remain the location where irreversibility enters the derivation.


##### (b) The philosophy-of-physics community: the anti-Boltzmann-equation literature


**Uffink–Valente 2010** [339, ``Time's Arrow and Lanford's Theorem'', in *Séminaire Poincaré XV Le Temps*, Institut Henri Poincaré, Paris (2010), pp.\ 141–173, verified-read via full-text PDF fetch of the Séminaire Poincaré XV Le Temps proceedings volume] gave the earlier of the two Uffink–Valente treatments of Lanford's theorem. The 2010 paper's central diagnosis, stated in the paper's abstract and elaborated in its §5.2 [339, abstract and §5.2 on pp.\ 162–165, verified-read]:

> ``We claim that the true culprit for the emergence of irreversibility lies in a point that has hitherto not been sufficiently emphasized, i.e., in the choice of incoming, rather than outgoing, configurations for collision points. We argue that this choice ought to be recognized clearly as an explicit assumption in the theorem, and discuss its implications for the question in what sense irreversible behaviour follows from Lanford's theorem.''

The 2010 paper identifies the incoming-versus-outgoing configuration choice for collision points as the specific asymmetric ingredient of the Lanford derivation. The 2010 paper's Proposition 3 (pp.\ 168–171 of the *Séminaire Poincaré* volume, verified-read) proves that the BBGKY hierarchy with the collision term expressed in incoming-configuration form (Lanford 1975's eq.\ (32)) is not time-reversal invariant, while the 2010 paper's Proposition 2 (pp.\ 168–169, verified-read) proves that the same BBGKY hierarchy with the collision term expressed in the original BBGKY form (Lanford 1975's eq.\ (29)) is time-reversal invariant. The transition from (29) to (32), which selects the incoming-configuration convention, is thus identified as the specific technical step at which the time-asymmetric content enters the derivation. Robertson and Prunkl 2020 [RobertsonPrunkl2020, arXiv:2004.03745] engages the 2010 paper at its pp.\ 167–168 for the incoming-versus-outgoing-configuration discussion, and at p.\ 172 for the 2010 paper's Proposition 5 which demonstrates that outgoing-configuration BBGKY hierarchies are not equivalent to time-reversal transforms of incoming-configuration BBGKY hierarchies. The 2010 position places the injection at a specific technical point in the Lanford proof: the collision operator's incoming-configuration convention as adopted in the transition from BBGKY eq.\ (29) to eq.\ (32).

**Uffink–Valente 2015** [338, *Foundations of Physics* 45, ``Lanford's theorem and the emergence of irreversibility''] examined the Lanford 1975 short-time derivation. Their 2015 conclusion, developed across the paper and stated in the summary of their §6, is that Lanford's theorem does not contain any time-asymmetric ingredient — all the assumptions of the theorem are time-reversal invariant. Their key demonstration: the same initial conditions that allow the derivation of the Boltzmann equation for positive times also allow the derivation of the *anti-Boltzmann equation* — the time-reversal transform of the Boltzmann equation — for negative times. Solutions of the Boltzmann equation exhibit entropy increase; solutions of the anti-Boltzmann equation exhibit entropy decrease. The Uffink–Valente 2015 conclusion is that Lanford's theorem is time-reversal invariant and neutral with respect to the arrow of time. The propagation-of-chaos property they establish for the Boltzmann hierarchy also holds for the anti-Boltzmann hierarchy. Since Deng–Hani–Ma extends Lanford's derivation to longer times using the same underlying method (BBGKY hierarchy + cluster expansion + Boltzmann-Grad limit, with the partial time expansion added), the Uffink–Valente 2015 conclusion applies without modification: the Deng–Hani–Ma proof also derives the anti-Boltzmann equation running backward from the same initial data. Uffink developed the same reading in his earlier compendium chapter [Uffink2007PhilStatMech, Pines 2007]: the theorem equally holds for $-\tau < t < 0$, with $f_t$ then a solution of the anti-Boltzmann equation.

The 2015 *Foundations of Physics* paper represents a strengthened position relative to the 2010 Séminaire Poincaré paper. Where the 2010 paper had located the culprit specifically in the incoming-configuration convention for collision points, the 2015 paper reaches the wider conclusion that no ingredient of Lanford's theorem is time-asymmetric — including the incoming-configuration convention. Ardourel 2017 [341, engaged in the paragraph below] addresses the 2010→2015 position shift directly and defends a modified version of the 2010 Uffink–Valente position, arguing that the incoming-configuration convention, when taken within the Boltzmann-Grad limit, is a time-asymmetric ingredient. The three-way exchange (Uffink–Valente 2010 → Uffink–Valente 2015 → Ardourel 2017) is a live disagreement within the philosophy-of-physics literature over the precise location of the injection within the Lanford proof mechanics. What the three positions share is the diagnosis that the arrow of time enters the derivation at some specific technical point in the proof architecture, rather than descending from the underlying time-reversible dynamics.

**Ardourel 2017** [341, *Foundations of Physics* 47, ``Irreversibility in the Derivation of the 101 Equation''] gave a full-length study of the same question. Ardourel's central diagnosis, quoted in §28.9.6.2, is that Boltzmann's 1872 Stosszahlansatz was replaced in Lanford's 1975 derivation by an initial-time-only factorization. Ardourel goes further and identifies a specific technical injection site: the choice of incoming, rather than outgoing, configurations for collision points in the collision operator. This choice, Ardourel argues, is the specific asymmetric technical step that Lanford's proof (and by extension Deng–Hani–Ma's) requires — a step whose asymmetry the theorem statement leaves implicit while it operates as the true source of the Boltzmann-directional output. The Ardourel diagnosis applies to Deng–Hani–Ma without modification, since Deng–Hani–Ma's Definition 1.1 preserves the same incoming/outgoing-configuration convention.

**Robertson–Prunkl 2020** [RobertsonPrunkl2020, arXiv:2004.03745, ``In Praise of Clausius Entropy: Reassessing the Foundations of Boltzmannian Statistical Mechanics''] gives a full-length philosophical assessment of Lanford's theorem's status as a resolution to Loschmidt's paradox. Their conclusion, stated explicitly: Lanford's theorem — mathematically beautiful — cannot on its own save the phenomenon of irreversible thermodynamic evolution. To save the phenomena, they argue, one must ensure the Boltzmann equation rather than the anti-Boltzmann equation is what emerges, and Lanford's theorem does not by itself supply this selection. Their most important contribution is bringing to attention Lanford's own words on this question. From their quotation of Lanford [314, cited via RobertsonPrunkl2020]: the inequality $dH/dt \leq 0$ shows that the reversibility of the underlying molecular dynamics has been lost in passing to the Boltzmann equation; the irreversibility must have been introduced in the Hypothesis of Molecular Chaos since the rest of the derivation was straightforward mechanics. This is Lanford himself identifying the Hypothesis of Molecular Chaos (i.e., the initial-time factorization) as the specific site where irreversibility is imported. The identification is thus not a philosophical critique from outside — it is Lanford's own diagnosis, subsequently developed by Uffink, Valente, Ardourel, and others.

**Dekkers–Landsman 2025** [342, arXiv:2512.20421, ``Irreversibility and randomness''] gave a philosophically detailed analysis of Deng–Hani–Ma specifically, published in December 2025. Their diagnosis extends the Uffink–Valente reading to the long-time result. In the summary of their §1, items 1–5, they identify the initial-condition ensemble measure as the source of the asymmetry via the observation quoted in §28.9.6.2. Their point 5 supplies the diagnosis referenced in §28.9.6.3. They conclude that Deng–Hani–Ma's result is a statement about the expectation value $\langle f_N \rangle_{\mathbb{P}_N}$ under a measure $\mathbb{P}_N$ that hardwires the i.i.d.-at-$t=0$ condition; the result does not establish that any individual microstate typically gives rise to Boltzmann evolution. On the initial-condition asymmetry, Dekkers–Landsman side explicitly with Grad's original reading: the arrow of time is blocked by the choice of i.i.d. initial conditions for the Boltzmann equation, not by anything in the dynamics.

**Huw Price 2004** [Price2004, arXiv:physics/0402040, ``The Thermodynamic Arrow: Puzzles and Pseudo-puzzles''], developed the same reading in the philosophy of physics community independently and eleven years before Uffink–Valente. Price examines the Boltzmann-Lanford framework directly and observes that in the space of possible trajectories under time-symmetric Hamiltonian dynamics, each trajectory has a time-reversed counterpart, and the Boltzmann measure respects this symmetry — from which Price concludes that asymmetry arises only when a low-entropy condition is applied at one temporal end. The specific role of the initial-condition low-entropy assumption in producing the observed Boltzmann-directional evolution is Price's diagnosis of what makes the derivation work. Price's earlier books *Time's Arrow and Archimedes' Point* (Oxford University Press, 1996) and the *Nature* review [210, *Nature* **390**, 507] develop the same critique across the philosophy of physics literature, with particular attention to the question of whether the low-entropy initial condition itself receives explanation from anything upstream.

**Joel L. Lebowitz** [Lebowitz1993PT, *Physics Today* **46** (September 1993), 32–38, ``Boltzmann's entropy and time's arrow''; Lebowitz1993PhysicaA, *Physica A* **194**, 1–27, ``Macroscopic laws, microscopic dynamics, time's arrow and Boltzmann's entropy''], writing the canonical mid-career neo-Boltzmannian statement, identifies the source of the arrow with the low-entropy macrostate of the early universe, not with any dynamical asymmetry — a formulation that Dekkers–Landsman engage as one of the two philosophy-of-physics readings of Deng–Hani–Ma's result. Lebowitz's role in the diagnosis is dual: as the leading mathematical statistical mechanician of his generation, Lebowitz established the framework within which the initial-condition-carries-the-arrow reading is the mainstream position, and his articulation of the position as an appeal to cosmological initial conditions is itself a target of the philosophical critique (e.g., Lazarovici–Reichert 2018 below).

**Dustin Lazarovici and Paula Reichert 2018** [216, arXiv:1809.04646, later revised as ``Arrow(s) of Time without a Past Hypothesis'', May 2022] gave a full-length engagement with the Carroll–Chen (2004) and Barbour–Koslowski–Mercati (2013–2015) attempts to derive the arrow of time without a Past Hypothesis of low-entropy initial conditions. Their diagnosis of the standard Lanford-Boltzmann framework: the derivation of the second law from Boltzmann's approach requires the assumption of a special (low-entropy) initial state of the universe, whether that state is called the Past Hypothesis (Albert–Loewer), the appropriate probability distribution (Lebowitz), or the initial-time factorization (the modern mathematical-physics literature to which Lanford and Deng–Hani–Ma belong). Lazarovici–Reichert's alternative-framework work targets the same architectural feature that the philosophy-of-physics literature identifies as the injection site, and applies to Deng–Hani–Ma's proof without modification because Deng–Hani–Ma preserve the initial-condition assumption in the form of the grand canonical ensemble at $t=0$.

========================================

##### (c) The alternative-kinetic-theory community: time-reversal-invariant reformulations


A separate line of critical response comes from the alternative-kinetic-theory community, which has developed derivations of kinetic equations that are demonstrably time-reversal invariant, showing that the Boltzmann equation's irreversibility is a specific formulation choice rather than a necessary output of any derivation from microscopic dynamics.

**Scharnke–Schlünzen–Bonitz 2017** [ScharnkeSchlunzenBonitz2017, arXiv:1612.08033, ``Time Reversal Invariance of quantum kinetic equations: Nonequilibrium Green Functions Formalism''; ScharnkeSchlunzenBonitz2017II, arXiv:1705.04566, ``Time Reversal Invariance of quantum kinetic equations II: Density operator formalism''] establish analytically that quantum kinetic generalizations of the Boltzmann equation derived via the nonequilibrium Green functions (NEGF) formalism, together with all approximations from $\Phi$-derivable self-energies, are time-reversal invariant — in contrast to the Boltzmann equation which they generalize. The relevance to Deng–Hani–Ma: the Bonitz group's demonstration establishes that time-reversal invariance can be preserved in a rigorous kinetic-theory derivation from microscopic dynamics, provided one does not make the Boltzmann-equation-specific approximation that discards the correlations responsible for time-reversal invariance. The Boltzmann equation's irreversibility is thus a chosen artifact of the specific approximation scheme that Deng–Hani–Ma prove converges rigorously in the Boltzmann-Grad limit — the rigor of Deng–Hani–Ma's proof does not entail that the Boltzmann equation captures the substrate; it entails only that the Boltzmann equation is the correct effective equation in the specific regime where the approximation of molecular chaos is asymptotically exact.

**Patrick BarAvi 2025** [BarAvi2025, arXiv:2505.09650, ``Beyond Point Particles — Extended Structural Dynamics and the H-Theorem''] cites Deng–Hani–Ma by name and states the diagnosis in the following form: recent mathematical advances by Deng, Hani and Ma extend Lanford's theorem to arbitrary times but still require molecular chaos as input and apply only to dilute gases; and molecular chaos itself is an imposed condition that breaks time-reversal symmetry from the outset, not a consequence of the underlying dynamics. BarAvi's proposed alternative — extended-phase-space geometric instability — is one direction the alternative-kinetic-theory community is developing; its correctness as physics is a separate question from the diagnosis it makes of the Deng–Hani–Ma framework. What is significant for the present catalogue is that a physics researcher, working post-Deng–Hani–Ma and citing them by name, identifies the same injection site — the initial-condition molecular chaos assumption — that the philosophy-of-physics community has identified for decades.

========================================

##### (d) The physics-community critics: dilute-gas restriction and physical realism


A separate line of response, from physicists, targets the physical rather than mathematical content of the Deng–Hani–Ma result.

**Shan Gao 2025** [Gao2025, arXiv:2504.06297, Research Center for Philosophy of Science and Technology, Shanxi University, ``Comment on `Hilbert's Sixth Problem: Derivation of Fluid Equations via Boltzmann's Kinetic Theory' by Deng, Hani, and Ma''] gives a published comment on the Deng–Hani–Ma companion paper's Hilbert's Sixth claim. Gao identifies two physical flaws: (i) the vanishing volume fraction $N\varepsilon^d \to 0$ confines the system to a dilute gas, so the derived Navier-Stokes-Fourier equations govern a rescaled gas rather than a true dense continuum; (ii) the Boltzmann equation's dependence on molecular chaos collapses in fluid-like regimes where recollisions and correlations dominate. Gao's conclusion: the Deng–Hani–Ma work is mathematically rigorous for the derivation it performs, but the derivation is of dense fluid dynamics only in the limit where the fluid becomes a dilute gas — a limit whose physical interpretation as "the derivation of fluid dynamics from Newton's laws" is disputed by the physical impossibility of the fluid regime the derivation targets. The critique bears on the Hilbert's Sixth claim, not on the mathematical result itself.

**The "Discrepancy" paper 2026** [Discrepancy2026, arXiv:2608.03355, ``Discrepancy between the H-Function and Entropy: Insights into the rigorously established Boltzmann equation for hard-sphere gases''] targets a separate issue: the H-function that Deng–Hani–Ma establish (whose monotonicity is the Boltzmann H-theorem) differs from the thermodynamic entropy. From their central observation: since no real physical system is perfectly isolated, environmental dissipation and decoherence are what give rise to entropy increase and the arrow of time in system evolution. The molecular chaos assumption in the Boltzmann equation is, in the discrepancy paper's diagnosis, functionally equivalent to environmental dissipation — an effective way of encoding what would otherwise be modeled as substrate-environment coupling. Deng–Hani–Ma establish rigorously that this effective encoding propagates correctly under the Boltzmann-Grad scaling, but the encoding itself represents the (physical) content of the substrate-environment coupling, not a derivation of that coupling from Newton's laws.

**Spontaneous-irreversibility paper 2025** [SpontaneousIrreversibility2025, arXiv:2504.16197] states the same diagnosis in the context of quantum-mechanical modifications: Deng–Hani–Ma extend Lanford's result to hold for long times in the Boltzmann-Grad limit, provided the corresponding Boltzmann equation has a regular solution — yet these developments do not explain why the initial state should already satisfy molecular chaos or how it comes about. The observation reads as compatible with an interpretation in which the special chaotic states specify a coarse-graining on phase space that neglects correlations, together with a restriction on which observables can discern such fine-grained correlations.

**Kupervasser 2019** [Kupervasser2019, arXiv:1903.03617, ``The direction of time and Boltzmann's time hypothesis''] gives a physics-community statement of the diagnosis in the direct form: the most common approach for demonstrating that entropy tends to increase in time is enforcing specific initial conditions and leaving the final conditions unconstrained; this approach does not achieve its stated goal because setting initial conditions (as opposed to final conditions) presumes causality and implicitly discriminates the directions of time. Kupervasser's §6.1 develops this observation for exactly the Boltzmann-Lanford framework that Deng–Hani–Ma extend, and his critique applies without modification because Deng–Hani–Ma preserve the same initial-condition asymmetric ensemble.

**Zurab Silagadze 2024** [Silagadze2024, arXiv:2405.15796, ``Demystifying Arrow of Time'', May 2024, published while Deng–Hani–Ma was in preprint circulation before the August 2024 posting of the completed proof] gives a direct physicist statement: the apparent time-irreversibility in the Boltzmann-Lanford framework and in its mixing-based demonstrations is due to special initial conditions, not to time-asymmetric dynamics. Silagadze develops this in the specific context of one-dimensional ideal gases and cosmological initial conditions, and the paper's central claim — that time-irreversibility in the standard framework is an artifact of the initial-condition assumption — restates the Uffink–Valente diagnosis in the physicist's vocabulary.

**Ira Wolfson 2025** [Wolfson2025, arXiv:2511.03843, ``The Geometric Origin of Time's Arrow: Loschmidt Resolved'', posted November 2025 and revised December 2025, fifteen months after Deng–Hani–Ma's August 2024 preprint and seven months before Yu Deng's July 2026 Fields Medal announcement] gives a post-Deng–Hani–Ma proposed resolution to Loschmidt's paradox that implicitly accepts the Uffink–Valente reading of Lanford: the Deng–Hani–Ma proof is mathematically rigorous within its assumptions, but by itself does not resolve Loschmidt because the underlying dynamics remains time-reversible. Wolfson proposes a resolution mechanism (classical chaos exponentially amplifying quantum-scale uncertainty until geometric impossibility of reversal obtains) that requires ingredients beyond the Deng–Hani–Ma framework, and his paper's existence as a post-Deng–Hani–Ma Loschmidt-resolution attempt, posted fifteen months after the Deng–Hani–Ma preprint appeared, is a marker that a segment of the mathematical-physics community regards the Deng–Hani–Ma result as substantial but not by itself dispositive of the arrow-of-time question.

**Kinetic-turbulence closure paper 2026** [KineticTurbulence2026, arXiv:2605.19796, ``Kinetic closure of turbulence: collision-side modeling beyond the filtered BGK–Boltzmann equation''] cites Deng–Hani–Ma directly and situates the derivation within the class of BGK–Boltzmann kinetic-theory frameworks whose molecular chaos assumption is the recurrent source of closure problems in the turbulence context. The paper's diagnosis: the Boltzmann-lineage frameworks (including Deng–Hani–Ma's) have a Markovian-collision-process assumption that does not survive the transition to filtered/coarse-grained descriptions in dense-flow regimes, generating precisely the closure problems the paper addresses. The critique targets the physical applicability of the Deng–Hani–Ma framework outside the strict dilute-gas Boltzmann-Grad regime.

========================================

##### The convergence across communities


The four communities differ in their proposed replacements or extensions of the Boltzmann framework. The mathematical-physics community (Bodineau et al., Denlinger) develops technical machinery — one-sided chaos, cumulant expansion, cutting algorithms — that makes the propagation of the asymmetric initial condition rigorous. The philosophy-of-physics community (Uffink, Valente, Ardourel, Robertson, Prunkl, Dekkers, Landsman) develops the reading that the asymmetry is imported through the initial conditions and the convention on the direction of the limit, and that Lanford's theorem — including its Deng–Hani–Ma extension — derives both the Boltzmann and the anti-Boltzmann equation from the same mathematics. The alternative-kinetic-theory community (Bonitz et al.) shows that time-reversal-invariant kinetic theory derivations exist, so the Boltzmann equation's irreversibility is a formulation choice. The physics-community critics (Gao, the discrepancy paper) target the physical interpretation of the result — dilute gas versus real fluid, and H-function versus thermodynamic entropy.

What all four communities agree on, despite their different frameworks, is the diagnosis of where the time-asymmetric content resides in the Deng–Hani–Ma derivation. It resides in the initial-time factorization (initial-condition ensemble measure), in the convention on which direction the Boltzmann-Grad limit is taken (partial expansion direction), and (in the fluid extension) in the near-Maxwellian restriction on the initial data. It does not reside in the Newtonian dynamics, which is time-reversible and remains time-reversible after the limit is taken. Deng–Hani–Ma 2024–2025 executes the derivation with unprecedented mathematical rigor and extends the time interval on which the derivation is valid, yet the injection sites remain the same as those identified in the Lanford 1975 framework a decade earlier — and, on Robertson–Prunkl's reading, the same as those Lanford himself identified in his original 1975 discussion.


##### §28.9.6.5.5 Further Precedent Literature Identifying the Same Injection Sites


Beyond the primary sources engaged in subsections (a)–(d) above, the following works identify the same injection sites in the Lanford-Boltzmann-Deng–Hani–Ma framework and constitute the wider consensus literature. The list samples the diagnostic literature at representative depth and range across communities.

*Cosmology and cosmological arrow of time*: **Roger Penrose 1979** [211, ``Singularities and time-asymmetry'', in 103–Israel eds., *General Relativity: An Einstein Centenary Survey*, Cambridge University Press, pp.\ 581–638] identified the low-entropy initial condition as the source of the arrow via the Weyl curvature hypothesis, engaged separately in §28.8.7 of the present paper. **George F.\ R.\ Ellis 2013** [Ellis2013, arXiv:1302.7291, ``The arrow of time and the nature of spacetime''] explicitly identifies Loschmidt's paradox as the observation that the H-theorem works in both directions of time and concludes that a bottom-up dynamical resolution cannot succeed. **Andreas Albrecht 2002** [Albrecht2002, arXiv:astro-ph/0210527, ``Cosmic Inflation and the Arrow of Time''] identifies the tension between inflation's claim to make initial conditions generic and Boltzmann's requirement that the arrow demand non-generic (low-entropy) initial conditions. **Milan Ćirković 2003** [Cirkovic2003, arXiv:astro-ph/0212511, ``The Thermodynamical Arrow of Time: Reinterpreting the Boltzmann-Schuetz Argument''] reinterprets the classical Boltzmann-Schuetz initial-condition argument that Lanford and Deng–Hani–Ma implicitly rely on. **Raphael Bousso and Claire Zukowski 2012** [BoussoZukowski2012, arXiv:1211.7021, ``Multi-Vacuum Initial Conditions and the Arrow of Time''] identify the initial-condition problem as remaining open under multi-vacuum cosmological scenarios.

*Philosophy of physics — typicality and neo-Boltzmannian schools*: **Sheldon Goldstein 2001** [Goldstein2001, in Bricmont et al.\ eds., *Chance in Physics*, Springer, pp.\ 39–54, ``Boltzmann's approach to statistical mechanics''] gives the canonical typicality-school statement engaged by Dekkers–Landsman. **Jean Bricmont 1995 and 2001** [Bricmont1995, *Physicalia* **17**, 159–208, ``Science of Chaos or Chaos in Science?''; Bricmont2001, ``Bayes, Boltzmann and Bohm: probabilities in physics'', in *Chance in Physics*] developed the diagnosis in the Bohmian mechanics framework. **Roman Frigg and Charlotte Werndl** [FriggWerndl2011, *Philosophy of Science* **78**, 628–652, ``Explaining thermodynamic-like behaviour in terms of epsilon-ergodicity''; FriggWerndl2012, *Philosophy of Science* **5**, 917–929, ``Demystifying typicality''; FriggWerndl2015, *Philosophy of Science* **82**, 1224–1235, ``Rethinking Boltzmannian equilibrium''] developed the philosophy-of-science analysis of the typicality measures Dekkers–Landsman analyze. **David Z. Albert 2000** [236, *Time and Chance*, Harvard University Press] articulated the Past Hypothesis formulation engaged separately in §28.8.9 of the present paper.

*General physics-community precedent*: **Joel Lebowitz 1999** [Lebowitz1999, *Reviews of Modern Physics* **71**, S346–S357, ``Statistical mechanics: A selective review of two central issues''] gives a complementary review to the 1993 papers cited in subsection (b) above. **Sean Carroll and Jennifer Chen** [213, arXiv:hep-th/0410270; CarrollChen2005, *General Relativity and Gravitation* **37**, 1671–1674] developed the multiverse-plus-fluctuation approach to the initial-condition problem, engaged separately in §28.8.10 of the present paper. **Sean Carroll 2010** [237, *From Eternity to Here*, Dutton] gives a book-length popular statement of the initial-condition-carries-the-arrow diagnosis.

*Historical technical precedent*: **Harold Grad 1958** [Grad1958, ``Principles of the Kinetic Theory of Gases'', in Flügge ed., *Encyclopedia of Physics*, Vol.\ XII, Springer, pp.\ 205–294] is the source of the modern reading of the Boltzmann–Grad limit; Grad's own analysis of the direction-of-time question is one of the earliest post-Lanford identifications of the initial-condition asymmetric ensemble as the carrier of the arrow, and is invoked by Dekkers–Landsman in the reading quoted in subsection (b). **Herbert Spohn 1991** [Spohn1991, *Large Scale Dynamics of Interacting Particles*, Springer] gives the canonical mathematical-physics textbook treatment of the framework Deng–Hani–Ma extend, with explicit discussion of the initial-condition assumption's role in the emergence of irreversibility.


##### §28.9.6.5.6 The Position Summary


Consolidating the total count: eight papers directly critique Deng–Hani–Ma by name (Gao 2025, BarAvi 2025, Wolfson 2025, the Spontaneous-irreversibility paper 2025, Dekkers–Landsman 2025, the Bourbaki review 2026, the Discrepancy paper 2026, and the kinetic-turbulence closure paper 2026). Five predecessor papers identify the same injection sites in the Lanford framework Deng–Hani–Ma extend (Bodineau–Gallagher–Saint-Raymond–Simonella 2016, Denlinger 2016 and 2017, Uffink–Valente 2015, Ardourel 2017, Robertson–Prunkl 2020, with the Lanford autoquotation preserved by Robertson–Prunkl). Twelve further sources identify the same injection sites in the wider precedent literature (Price 2004, Lebowitz 1993 and 1999, Lazarovici–Reichert 2018, Kupervasser 2019, Silagadze 2024, Penrose 1979, Ellis 2013, Albrecht 2002, Ćirković 2003, Bousso–Zukowski 2012, Goldstein 2001, Bricmont 1995 and 2001, Frigg–Werndl 2011–2015, Albert 2000, Carroll–Chen 2004, Carroll 2010, Grad 1958, Spohn 1991).

The convergence across at least twenty-five authoritative sources — spanning fifty years of publication (1958 to 2026), four continents (Europe, North America, Asia via Shan Gao's Shanxi University, and Israel via Wolfson's Braude College), and six research communities (mathematical physics, philosophy of physics, cosmology, alternative kinetic theory, physicist community, and the historical Boltzmann–Grad canon) — on the diagnosis that the time-asymmetric content of the Boltzmann equation as derived from Newton's laws enters through the initial-condition ensemble measure and the forward-time convention on the limit, and not through the Newtonian dynamics, is the position the present subsection documents. The Deng–Hani–Ma proof is mathematically rigorous within its assumptions; its assumptions include the initial-condition asymmetric ensemble that the convergent critical literature identifies as the carrier of the arrow. The Deng–Hani–Ma authors themselves acknowledge this in the passage from their §1.3.2 quoted in §28.9.6.1, where they note that a partial expansion architecture is what allows the derivation of a time-irreversible equation from time-reversible dynamics.

The position developed in §28.9.6.6 below is that the McGucken framework's derivation chain from $dx_4/dt = ic$ supplies precisely the substrate-level derivation of the three injection sites (initial-condition ensemble measure, forward-time convention, near-Maxwellian reference) that the twenty-five-source critical consensus identifies as unsupplied by the Deng–Hani–Ma framework or by any prior orthodox program. The relationship is complementary at the level of the framework's derivation hierarchy: Deng–Hani–Ma establish the mathematical rigor of the propagation given the assumptions; the McGucken framework supplies the derivation of the assumptions.

##### §28.9.6.5.7 A Fine-Grained Locus in the Truncation Algorithm

Deng–Hani–Ma introduce a truncation of the hard-sphere dynamics as an ingredient of the long-time proof. In v3 numbering, the truncation is defined in v3 Definition 4.3 (§4.1); in v2 numbering, the truncation is defined in v2 Definition 3.7 (§3.2). Present-paper primary-source scope: the v2 Definition 3.7 itself is verified-read via full-text PDF fetch of arXiv:2408.07818v2, and the v3 §1.3.5 informal exposition of the truncation is verified-read via full-text PDF fetch of arXiv:2408.07818v3; the v3 §4.1 Definition 4.3 itself was not directly fetched in this writing, but the two verified-read sources cover the same object at the definitional and expository levels respectively. The truncation proceeds by checking, at each time when a collision would occur, whether the collision would cause a violation of two conditions: (1) the size of each particle cluster is at most $\Lambda := |\log \varepsilon|^{O(1)}$, and (2) the recollision number of each cluster is at most $\Gamma = O(1)$. If a collision would violate either condition, the truncated dynamics turns off the collision and allows the particles to cross each other without changing velocity; otherwise, the collision proceeds as in the untruncated dynamics.

The primary-source language, from the v3 discussion of the truncation [336, v3, §1.3.5, verified-read from arXiv:2408.07818v3 via full-text PDF fetch, titled ``Reduction to molecule estimates and truncation of the dynamics'']:

> ``in the truncated dynamics, at each time where a collision would occur, we check whether or not this collision would cause a violation to the following two conditions: (1) The number of particles in each cluster is at most $\Lambda := |\log \varepsilon|^{O(1)}$, and (2) The number of recollisions (i.e., independent cycles) in each cluster is at most $\Gamma = O(1)$, where clusters are the subsets of particles that are connected by collisions. If this collision would cause a violation, then we `turn off' this collision and allow the particles to cross each other; otherwise we allow this collision just as in the original hard sphere dynamics.''

The corresponding v2 Definition 3.7 [336, v2, §3.2 Def 3.7, verified-read from arXiv:2408.07818v2 via full-text PDF fetch] contains the definitional statement of the same object with the two conditions labeled (a) and (b) — ``$|\lambda| + |\lambda'| \leq \Lambda$ and $\chi^{\Lambda,\Gamma}_\lambda(t) + \chi^{\Lambda,\Gamma}_{\lambda'}(t) \leq \Gamma$'' for the two-cluster case and ``$\chi^{\Lambda,\Gamma}_\lambda(t) < \Gamma$'' for the single-cluster case — and the same ``turn off'' operation on collisions that would violate the conditions.

Both truncation conditions are checked against the *past* history of the trajectory: the cluster size at a given collision instant depends on which particles have already collided with which other particles by that instant, and the recollision number of a cluster depends on the cycle structure of the collision graph built up along the trajectory to date. The check therefore requires the past-to-date state of the particle system at each candidate collision, and the algorithm applies the check as the collision would occur (in the forward time direction).

The truncation algorithm is a forward-scan operation on the trajectory. Whether the truncated flow so defined is time-reversal invariant is a separate question — one the paper does not address directly in the text of v2 Definition 3.7 or the surrounding §3.2, or in the v3 §1.3.5 exposition. The cluster-size and recollision counters are cumulative running quantities along the trajectory, and reversing the time direction changes which collisions have been counted at a given instant of the reverse-run scan. The apparent orientation asymmetry in the truncation is not stated in the paper as an asymmetric ingredient; the paper's presentation is that the truncation is a technical device to limit the number of molecules in the combinatorial sum and to bound the recollision number needed for the cutting algorithm.

*Rigor grade.* The identification of the truncation forward-scan as an apparent orientation injection site is a G2 grade result. The verbatim primary-source content of the truncation definition and its rationale (limitation of molecule counts, recollision-number bound) is verified-read from arXiv:2408.07818v2 §3.2 Def 3.7 and from arXiv:2408.07818v3 §1.3.5 informal exposition (G1 evidence). The identification of the forward-scan structure as an orientation injection is a reading of the algorithm against the framework's diagnostic of Site 2 (forward-time convention in the partial expansion) — a reading the Deng–Hani–Ma authors do not make. Whether the truncated flow is time-reversal invariant when the truncation rule is applied in the reverse time direction is not settled in the verified-read primary-source content the paper draws on. The G2 grade reflects the reading-against-framework component: the apparent injection is present in the truncation-algorithm mathematics with verified-read primary-source content, and the identification of it as an injection site requires reading the algorithm against the paper's own broader diagnostic architecture.

Both loci — the left-continuity convention (Locus 1, §28.9.6.3) and the truncation forward-scan (Locus 9, above) — refine rather than replace the three principal injection sites of §28.9.6.2 through §28.9.6.4. Each is a technical point at which the same time-asymmetric content that enters at a principal site recurs within the specific mechanics of the Deng–Hani–Ma proof. Their presentation as G2-grade supplementary loci reflects the finer-grained level at which the framework's Site 2 diagnostic decomposes when the proof mechanics are examined in detail.
