### 22.5.19 The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ Reading of the No-Signaling Theorem — Nonlocality and Quantum Probability as Two Faces of the Same $dx_4/dt = ic$ Sphere Mechanism, with the McGucken No-Signaling Theorem Establishing that the Very Sphere Expansion at Rate $c$ that Supplies Nonlocality Also Supplies the SO(3)-Invariant Haar-Measure Born Rule that Cloaks the Instantaneous Nonlocal Influences in Probability, and Diagnostic Case 11 (Al-Khalili 2026, Maudlin 2026) Reading Al-Khalili's "Tough Luck We Can't Signal" Position and Maudlin's "Theoretically You Can Signal" Position as Formal Reconstructions of the Sphere-Born-Rule Physical Unity that the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ Framework Supplies Directly

The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ states that the fourth dimension is expanding at the invariant velocity of light $c$ in a spherically symmetric manner from every spacetime event, with the imaginary unit $i$ marking perpendicularity to the three ordinary spatial dimensions. The two Channels of the McGucken Duality read this Principle in two aspects: the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel reads the real-rate-at-$c$ aspect (the physically-real spherically-symmetric wavefront's spatial spreading, the physical carrier of nonlocality); the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel reads the perpendicularity-marker-$i$ aspect (the operator-algebra apparatus generating quantum probability through the SO(3)-invariant Haar measure on the McGucken Sphere). This subsection establishes the McGucken No-Signaling Theorem as the physical theorem tying nonlocality and quantum probability together as two faces of the same $dx_4/dt = ic$ Sphere mechanism, and applies it as Diagnostic Case 11 to Jim Al-Khalili's 2026 podcast interview position (*"tough luck we can't signal"*) and Tim Maudlin's 2026 podcast interview position (*"theoretically you can signal"*).

**Theorem 22.5.19.1 (The McGucken No-Signaling Theorem — Statement).** *Let two spatially-separated measurement events $A$ (at spacetime point $q_A$) and $B$ (at spacetime point $q_B$) be performed on the two members of an entangled pair created at a common local origin event $p_{\text{pair}}$, with $q_A$ and $q_B$ spacelike-separated. Under the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$:*

*(i) The two measurement events $A$ and $B$ share the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma^+_M(p_{\text{pair}})$ expanding at rate $c$ in the $+ic$ direction from the common pair-creation event $p_{\text{pair}}$, and their measurement outcomes are correlated through the shared McGucken-Sphere identity via the CHSH singlet correlation $E(\hat a, \hat b) = -\cos\theta_{\hat a\hat b}$ established at Theorem 22.5.17.5 (McGucken Nonlocality Theorem) — a real physical correlation carried by the shared nonlocal Sphere surface at rate $c$ from $p_{\text{pair}}$.*

*(ii) The individual measurement outcome at event $A$ is Born-rule distributed on the SO(3)-invariant Haar measure of the shared McGucken Sphere at event $A$, per Theorem 22.5.17.4 (Born Rule from McGucken Sphere Intensity via SO(3) Haar-Measure Uniqueness), giving each individual outcome a random character with probability $|\psi_i|^2$ for outcome $i$; the same holds for the individual outcome at event $B$.*

*(iii) The correlation of clause (i) and the individual randomness of clause (ii) descend from the same physical mechanism — the McGucken Sphere expanding at rate $c$ in the $+ic$ direction from $p_{\text{pair}}$ — with the correlation carried by the shared Sphere identity across the two events and the individual randomness carried by the Sphere's SO(3)-invariant Haar-measure mode-count at each event. Nonlocality (clause i) and quantum probability (clause ii) are two faces of the same $dx_4/dt = ic$ Sphere mechanism.*

*(iv) The individual measurement outcome at event $A$ cannot be influenced or set by any experimenter action at event $B$, because the individual outcome at $A$ is Born-rule distributed on the SO(3)-invariant Haar measure of the shared McGucken Sphere at $A$, which is a rotationally-invariant probability distribution fixed by the Sphere geometry and not by any experimenter's choice or action at any other event. Consequently, the marginal distribution of outcomes at $A$ is independent of any experimenter's choice of measurement axis at $B$, and no signaling from $B$ to $A$ (or vice versa) is possible.*

*(v) The correlation of clause (i) is empirically detectable only through the joint statistics of many entangled-pair measurement events at $A$ and $B$ compared against a shared measurement-axis record — the nonlocal correlation is "cloaked" in the individual-outcome randomness of clause (ii), and the cloak is a physical consequence of the Sphere geometry, not a contingent empirical happenstance.*

*(vi) The two conditions — real nonlocal correlation (clause i) and individual-outcome randomness (clause ii) — are inseparable consequences of the same $dx_4/dt = ic$ Sphere mechanism, so no-signaling is forced, not "tough luck." No experimental modification, technological development, or hidden-variable extension of the framework can produce signaling while preserving the McGucken Sphere as the physical carrier of both the nonlocal correlation and the SO(3)-invariant Haar-measure Born rule.*

*Proof of Theorem 22.5.19.1.*

*Proof of (i) — the shared McGucken-Sphere identity from the common pair-creation event.* By Theorem 22.5.17.1 (McGucken Sphere from the axiom), the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma^+_M(p_{\text{pair}})$ at the common pair-creation event $p_{\text{pair}}$ expands at rate $c$ in the $+ic$ direction from $p_{\text{pair}}$, with spatial radius $r(t) = c(t - t_{p_{\text{pair}}})$ at coordinate time $t \geq t_{p_{\text{pair}}}$. Both measurement events $q_A$ and $q_B$ lie on the Sphere $\Sigma^+_M(p_{\text{pair}})$ at their respective coordinate times, since the Sphere expands to encompass any spacetime point reachable from $p_{\text{pair}}$ at rate $c$. The shared McGucken-Sphere identity is established by clause (i) of Theorem 22.5.17.2 (Six-Fold Locality of the McGucken Sphere) — the Sphere is a single foliation-leaf object, and both measurement events lie on this single leaf. The two-point correlation function $E(\hat a, \hat b) = -\hat a \cdot \hat b = -\cos\theta_{\hat a\hat b}$ of Theorem 22.5.17.5 (McGucken Nonlocality Theorem) supplies the specific singlet-correlation form the shared-Sphere identity generates. $\square$

*Proof of (ii) — the SO(3)-invariant Haar-measure Born rule at each event.* By Theorem 22.5.17.4 (Born Rule from McGucken Sphere Intensity via SO(3) Haar-Measure Uniqueness), the McGucken Sphere at every event supports a unique probability measure that is invariant under the SO(3) action of spherically symmetric rotations — the Haar measure on the compact group SO(3), which by the uniqueness of the Haar measure on a compact group is the uniform measure on the Sphere. The modulus operation at each measurement event registers the Sphere's SO(3)-invariant intensity through this Haar measure, giving the Born rule $P(\text{outcome } i) = |\psi_i|^2$ for the individual measurement outcome at that event. This applies independently at event $A$ (giving the individual random outcome at $A$ with probability $|\psi_i^A|^2$) and at event $B$ (giving the individual random outcome at $B$ with probability $|\psi_j^B|^2$). $\square$

*Proof of (iii) — nonlocality and probability from the same $dx_4/dt = ic$ Sphere mechanism.* Clause (i) establishes that the correlation is carried by the shared McGucken Sphere $\Sigma^+_M(p_{\text{pair}})$ expanding at rate $c$ from $p_{\text{pair}}$. Clause (ii) establishes that the individual-outcome randomness is generated by the SO(3)-invariant Haar measure on the same McGucken Sphere at each measurement event. The Sphere and its Haar measure are one physical object — the physically-real spherically symmetric expanding wavefront at rate $c$ from every event supplies both the shared-Sphere-identity nonlocal correlation and the SO(3)-invariant Haar-measure individual-outcome randomness. The correlation of clause (i) and the randomness of clause (ii) are two faces of the same $dx_4/dt = ic$ Sphere mechanism, with the primary-source statement from [5, §4.8] making this explicit: *"the McGucken Nonlocality Principle and the Born rule are two faces of one geometric fact."* $\square$

*Proof of (iv) — no signaling from $B$ to $A$.* Let $\rho_A$ denote the marginal probability distribution of measurement outcomes at event $A$ obtained by averaging over all possible measurement outcomes at event $B$. By clause (ii), the individual outcome at $A$ is Born-rule distributed via the SO(3)-invariant Haar measure on the shared McGucken Sphere at $A$. The marginal distribution $\rho_A$ is therefore the SO(3)-invariant Haar measure on the shared Sphere at $A$, which by the SO(3)-invariance is independent of any global-rotation choice — in particular, independent of the experimenter's choice of measurement axis $\hat b$ at event $B$. Formally, for the entangled singlet state, $\rho_A = \text{tr}_B(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|) = I_A/2$ (the maximally mixed single-particle state), which is manifestly independent of any measurement performed at $B$. Consequently, no signal from $B$ to $A$ can be extracted from the marginal distribution at $A$ alone; any experimenter at $A$ observing only $A$-measurements records the same statistics regardless of what any experimenter at $B$ chooses to do. The same argument applies symmetrically to $\rho_B$: no signaling from $A$ to $B$ is possible. $\square$

*Proof of (v) — the correlation is empirically detectable only through joint statistics.* The correlation $E(\hat a, \hat b) = -\cos\theta_{\hat a\hat b}$ of clause (i) is a joint expectation value $\langle \sigma_A(\hat a) \sigma_B(\hat b) \rangle$ over the entangled pair. Its empirical measurement requires the joint recording of $A$-outcomes and $B$-outcomes at their respective events, together with the record of the measurement axes $\hat a$ and $\hat b$, and the subsequent correlation of these records through classical communication of the joint outcomes at a third event (either at $A$ or $B$ or at some other spacetime point after both measurements have been performed). Without the joint record — without access to both $A$-outcomes and $B$-outcomes and their axes — no correlation can be extracted from the single-event marginal distributions of clause (iv). The correlation is therefore empirically "cloaked" in the individual-outcome randomness: any single measurement event yields Born-rule random outcomes on the SO(3)-invariant Haar measure of the local Sphere, and only the joint record across many pairs and both events reveals the underlying shared-Sphere-identity correlation. The cloak is a physical consequence of the Sphere geometry — the SO(3)-invariance forces the individual outcomes to be uniformly distributed on the Sphere at each event, which is precisely what makes them empirically random from any single-event vantage point. $\square$

*Proof of (vi) — no-signaling is forced by the shared physical mechanism.* Suppose, for contradiction, that some experimental modification, technological development, or hidden-variable extension of the framework could enable signaling from $B$ to $A$. Such signaling would require the marginal distribution $\rho_A$ at $A$ to depend on the experimenter's action at $B$, which by clause (iv) requires either (a) violating the SO(3)-invariance of the Haar measure on the shared McGucken Sphere (making $\rho_A$ non-uniform in a $B$-choice-dependent way), or (b) supplementing the Sphere with an additional physical carrier that couples $B$-actions to $A$-marginals without going through the Sphere's SO(3)-invariant Haar measure. Option (a) violates the SO(3) spherical symmetry that is baked into the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ itself (the Sphere is spherically symmetric by construction from the axiom), contradicting Theorem 22.5.17.1 (McGucken Sphere from the axiom). Option (b) introduces a physical carrier distinct from the McGucken Sphere, contradicting Theorem 22.5.17.3 (Topological McGucken Theorem — Uniqueness of the McGucken Sphere as the Submanifold Realizing All Six Locality Senses Simultaneously), which establishes the McGucken Sphere as the unique submanifold of $M^{1,3}$ realizing all six locality clauses simultaneously. Both options fail, so no experimental modification, technological development, or hidden-variable extension of the framework can enable signaling while preserving the McGucken Sphere as the physical carrier of both the nonlocal correlation and the Born rule. No-signaling is forced by the shared physical mechanism, not contingent on empirical happenstance. $\blacksquare$

#### 22.5.21.1 The Thought Experiment and Setup — Verbatim Import from [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11]

**Thought experiment (verbatim from [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11]).** *"Take the double-slit experiment and remove everything removable: the room, the glass, the screen, the thermal bath, the detector electronics. What remains is a partition with two apertures, one atom $A$ on side $M$, one atom $B$ on side $N$, and one excitation. Atom $A$ emits; the photon passes the partition; atom $B$ absorbs. Run it the other way — atom $B$ emits — and ask whether the photon retraces its path to $A$. Two readings must be separated: whether $A$ ever absorbs, and whether the forward process is run backward. It reaches $A$ with the forward interference weight (Theorem 10.12S.5) and retraces the forward wave history with probability zero. The system is minimal by construction: two degrees of freedom and one field, no ensemble, no coarse-graining, no entropy count. Whatever irreversibility survives here is present before thermodynamics begins, and the conclusion is that it is the choice of the retarded solution of a time-symmetric field equation, a sign on the time coordinate, and that $dx_4/dt = ic$ is the single statement from which that sign follows."*

**Setup (verbatim from [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11]).** *"Let side $M$ be the half-space $z < 0$, side $N$ the half-space $z > 0$, and the partition the plane $z = 0$ with aperture function $T(x, y) = 1$ on $S_1 \cup S_2$ (the two slits) and $0$ otherwise. Atom $A$ sits at $\mathbf{r}_A$ with $z_A < 0$; atom $B$ at $\mathbf{r}_B$ with $z_B > 0$. Work first with a scalar field for a monochromatic excitation, $\psi(\mathbf{r}, t) = U(\mathbf{r})\, e^{-i\omega t}$, $k = \omega/c$; the spatial part obeys the inhomogeneous Helmholtz equation with the emitting atom as source,"*
$$(\nabla^2 + k^2)\, U(\mathbf{r}) = -\delta(\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{src}}). \tag{S.1}$$
*"The analysis carries over verbatim to the vector Maxwell field and to the Schrödinger wave of a massive particle, each being time-reversal invariant in the sense of Theorem 10.12S.1 with retarded and advanced Green's functions related as in (S.3). The barrier is reflecting in the first five theorems and absorbing in Theorem 10.12S.8; the two cases differ, and the difference is part of the content."*

McGucken's contribution here: the thought-experiment reduction of the double-slit setup to its minimal irreducible form — one emitter atom $A$, one absorber atom $B$, one partition with two apertures, one excitation, no ensemble, no coarse-graining, no thermal bath — as the empirical scale at which time irreversibility can be exhibited without statistical averaging; identification of the resulting non-retracing behavior as the empirical content of the sign $+$ in the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$; the setup fixing the Helmholtz equation (S.1) as the governing wave equation and specifying that the analysis carries over verbatim to Maxwell fields and Schrödinger waves of massive particles.

#### 22.5.21.2 Consolidated Theorems 22.5.21.1 and 22.5.21.2 — the Wave Equation Admits Both $G_{\mathrm{ret}}$ and $G_{\mathrm{adv}}$; the Sign $+$ of $dx_4/dt = +ic$ Selects $\Sigma_+$ and Excludes $\Sigma_-$

**Theorem 22.5.21.1 (The Wave Equation Admits Both Retarded and Advanced Green's Functions as Fundamental Solutions).** *The wave equation $\square \psi = 0$ derived at Theorem 1 of [MG-Time] and Theorem 1 of the present paper's §22.5.4 has two independent fundamental solutions on Minkowski spacetime: the retarded Green's function*
$$G_{\mathrm{ret}}(\mathbf{x}, t) = \frac{\delta(t - r/c)}{4\pi r}, \qquad r = |\mathbf{x}|, \quad t \geq 0$$
*supported on the forward null cone $r = +c(t - t_0)$ for $t > t_0$, and the advanced Green's function*
$$G_{\mathrm{adv}}(\mathbf{x}, t) = \frac{\delta(t + r/c)}{4\pi r}, \qquad r = |\mathbf{x}|, \quad t \leq 0$$
*supported on the backward null cone $r = -c(t - t_0)$ for $t < t_0$. Both $G_{\mathrm{ret}}$ and $G_{\mathrm{adv}}$ satisfy the inhomogeneous wave equation $\square G_\pm = -\delta^{(4)}(x - x_0)$ and are related by the parity-time reversal $G_{\mathrm{adv}}(\mathbf{x}, t) = G_{\mathrm{ret}}(\mathbf{x}, -t)$; both are mathematically permitted by the wave equation alone; the empirical selection of $G_{\mathrm{ret}}$ over $G_{\mathrm{adv}}$ in every observed radiation process requires an additional principle beyond the wave equation.*

*Proof.* Direct substitution of $G_{\mathrm{ret}}$ and $G_{\mathrm{adv}}$ into $\square G_\pm = -\delta^{(4)}(x - x_0)$ verifies both as fundamental solutions of the inhomogeneous wave equation; the derivation follows Jackson, *Classical Electrodynamics*, 3rd ed. (Wiley, 1999), §6.4 and Morse and Feshbach, *Methods of Theoretical Physics* (McGraw-Hill, 1953), §7.3. The parity-time reversal $G_{\mathrm{adv}}(\mathbf{x}, t) = G_{\mathrm{ret}}(\mathbf{x}, -t)$ follows from the invariance of the wave operator $\square = \partial_t^2/c^2 - \nabla^2$ under $t \mapsto -t$. Both solutions are mathematically permitted by the wave equation; the empirical selection of $G_{\mathrm{ret}}$ over $G_{\mathrm{adv}}$ requires an additional principle beyond the wave equation itself, as noted in Jackson (§6.4) — the standard textbook treatment adopts $G_{\mathrm{ret}}$ as a boundary condition matching observed radiation asymptotics, without deriving the selection from a physical principle. $\blacksquare$

**Theorem 22.5.21.2 ($\Sigma_+$ Realized, $\Sigma_-$ Excluded by the Sign $+$ of $dx_4/dt = +ic$).** *Under the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$, the McGucken Sphere at every source event $p_0$ is $\Sigma_+(p_0)$ with radius $r = +c(t - t_0)$ for $t > t_0$, corresponding to the forward null cone and the retarded Green's function $G_{\mathrm{ret}}$. The time-reversed McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_-(p_0)$ with radius $r = -c(t - t_0)$ for $t < t_0$, corresponding to the backward null cone and the advanced Green's function $G_{\mathrm{adv}}$, is geometrically excluded by the sign $+$ of the principle. Physical electromagnetic radiation propagates on $\Sigma_+$ (retarded); no physical process propagates on $\Sigma_-$ (advanced). The empirical selection of the retarded Green's function over the advanced Green's function in every observed radiation process, from Einstein 1917's spontaneous emission A-coefficients through every spectroscopy experiment ever performed to the loophole-free Bell tests, is a direct geometric consequence of the sign $+$ in the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$.*

*Proof.* By Theorem 3 property (c) of §6 of [MG-Time] and the primitive orientation of the McGucken Principle established at §2 of [MG-Time], the sign in the principle is $+$, not $-$; the sign is part of the geometric data of the principle rather than a convention chosen from symmetric alternatives. The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p_0)$ at source event $p_0$ has radius $r = +c(t - t_0)$ for $t > t_0$, corresponding to $x_4$'s forward expansion from $p_0$ at rate $c$ in the $+ic$ direction; this is the forward null cone. The time-reversed sphere $\Sigma_-(p_0)$ with radius $r = -c(t - t_0)$ for $t < t_0$ corresponds to $x_4$'s backward contraction into $p_0$ at rate $c$ in the $-ic$ direction; this contradicts the sign $+$ of the principle and is geometrically excluded. Consequently, the retarded Green's function $G_{\mathrm{ret}}$, supported on the forward null cone $\Sigma_+$, is the physically realized fundamental solution; the advanced Green's function $G_{\mathrm{adv}}$, supported on the backward null cone $\Sigma_-$, has no McGucken-Sphere realization. The empirical selection of $G_{\mathrm{ret}}$ that Theorem 22.5.21.1 records as requiring an additional principle beyond the wave equation is derived from the sign $+$ of the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$. Theorems 22.5.21.1 and 22.5.21.2 are the compact form of the derivation given in full at Theorems 10.12S.10 and 10.12S.11 (§22.5.21.5 below), where the same selection is established through the analytic-continuation route by the $+i\varepsilon$ prescription of the Fourier kernel with sign fixed by the $+$ of $+ic$. $\blacksquare$

The emitted quantum reaches $p_A$ along a null worldline of $\Sigma_+(p_E)$, with the absorption event's coordinate time $t_A$ satisfying $t_A - t_E = |\mathbf{x}_B - \mathbf{x}_A|/c$ where $\mathbf{x}_A, \mathbf{x}_B$ are the spatial positions of the two atoms in the common inertial frame. The two-atom process is the physical realization of one null worldline of $\Sigma_+(p_E)$ — the specific null geodesic connecting $p_E$ to $p_A$.

*Step 3 (Advanced Green's function absent).* The advanced Green's function $G_{\mathrm{adv}}(\mathbf{x}, t; \mathbf{x}', t') = \delta(t - t' + |\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}'|/c)/(4\pi |\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}'|)$ would support propagation from $p_E$ along $\Sigma_-(p_E)$, the backward null cone from $p_E$. By Theorem 3 property (c) of §6 of [MG-Time], no McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_-$ expands at $-ic$; the principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ has $+ic$ only, and the geometric ensemble at every event is $\Sigma_+$ only. The advanced Green's function has no physical realization as a McGucken-Sphere propagation, so the two-atom process is exclusively retarded: $G_{\mathrm{ret}}$ contributes, $G_{\mathrm{adv}}$ does not.

*Step 4 (Below-thermodynamics scale).* The two-atom emission–absorption process involves exactly two atoms — the emitter and the absorber. No ensemble average is taken. No coarse-graining is performed. No thermodynamic limit is invoked. The $+ic$-monotonic advance of $x_4$ between $p_E$ and $p_A$ is a geometric fact about the single two-atom process, exhibited at the scale of one Compton-cycle of the emitted quantum (or fewer, depending on the emission process). This scale is below the level at which any statistical-mechanical or thermodynamic quantity can be defined (both require multi-particle ensembles); the $+ic$ orientation is exhibited at a scale where thermodynamic averaging does not yet operate. The primitive time orientation of the principle is therefore visible below thermodynamics. $\blacksquare$

But then how do we know that we're evolving into the future or that this is the past, and the Big Bang is the future, and we're just switching the arrow?' *Al-Khalili concedes:* 'Well, we don't.'*"*

Jaimungal's challenge assumes that the arrow of time enters physics only through statistical arguments about entropy, which are time-symmetric in their microscopic substrate. The two-atom emission–absorption process shows that this assumption is wrong: the $+ic$ orientation is present in one two-atom event, not only in ensemble-averaged Second-Law content. The direction from $p_E$ to $p_A$ is $+ic$, not $-ic$; this is a geometric fact about the two-atom process, exhibited without any ensemble average, and it directly resolves Jaimungal's "how do we know."

Al-Khalili's fallback to Thomas Gold universes and mirror universes (which he acknowledges have "no empirical evidence") is unnecessary in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework: the primitive orientation is exhibited at every single two-atom event in every laboratory experiment ever performed on emission-absorption processes, so no cosmological-boundary stipulation is needed. **Comparison with Wheeler–Feynman absorber theory (verbatim from [MG-Time, §16.1]).** *"Wheeler–Feynman 1945 attempted to derive the retarded-over-advanced selection from a perfect-absorber boundary condition on the cosmological future, with radiation propagating as $(G_{\mathrm{ret}} + G_{\mathrm{adv}})/2$ and the absorber response producing effective retarded propagation. #### 22.5.21.4 Theorem 22.5.21.3 — the Two-Sphere First-Contact Collision Geometry Supplying Outcome Definiteness at the Modulus Boundary — Full Verbatim Import of §XI.5-bis of [MG-Philosophy]

**McGucken Principle anchor.** Under $dx_4/dt = ic$, every detection event is a physical interaction between two expanding McGucken Spheres — the emitter's Sphere $\Sigma_+(E_A)$ from source event $E_A$ and an absorbing detector's Sphere $\Sigma_+(E_B)$ from source event $E_B$ — both expanding at rate $c$ in the $+ic$ direction from their respective source events. The pointlike character of the detection event is derived from the geometry of expansion-from-zero, rather than postulated as a stochastic reduction.

**Theorem 22.5.21.3 (Two-Sphere First-Contact Collision Geometry — Full Verbatim Import of §XI.5-bis of [MG-Philosophy]).** *A detection event is a physical interaction between the measured system's McGucken Sphere and an absorbing detector constituent's McGucken Sphere — a photographic-emulsion grain, a photomultiplier electron, a CCD potential well. Both Spheres expand at $dx_4/dt = ic$ from their respective source events; the detection is the event at which they meet. This is the physical content of the modulus operation of Proposition II.1.2 of [MG-Philosophy]: the meeting of the forward wavefront $\psi$ with the absorber's wavefront, read in the emitter's frame as the conjugate $\psi^*$, supplies the real Born-rule intensity $\psi^* \psi$ at the meeting event (Proposition III.1 of [MG-Philosophy]).*

*First contact of two expanding wavefronts is one point.* *"The two Spheres are wavefronts expanding from zero at rate $c$ from separated source events $E_A, E_B$ at spatial separation $d = |E_B - E_A|$; their radii $R_A(t), R_B(t)$ increase from zero. Two such Spheres make first contact at the instant the radii first satisfy"*
$$R_A(t^*) + R_B(t^*) = d$$
*"— the external-tangency configuration, a single point on the line $\overline{E_A E_B}$. Before $t^*$ the Spheres do not meet; at $t^*$ they meet at exactly one point; only for $t > t^*$ is the intersection the circle of radius $\sqrt{R_A(t)^2 - x(t)^2}$ on the radical plane $x(t) = (R_A^2 - R_B^2 + d^2)/(2d)$. For the co-emitted equal-rate case $R_A = R_B = ct$, first contact is at $t^* = d/(2c)$ at the midpoint, the intersection radius $\sqrt{(ct)^2 - (d/2)^2}$ vanishing at $t^*$ and opening to a circle thereafter. The collision — the first meeting of the two expanding wavefronts — is therefore a single point as a matter of the geometry of expansion-from-zero: every pair of wavefronts expanding from separated events passes through the one-point external-tangency instant before any extended intersection can form. The detection event, being the first contact, is pointlike."*

*Definiteness derived (verbatim from §XI.5-bis of [MG-Philosophy]).* *"Two facts combine to fix single-outcome definiteness. First, the collision occurs at one spacetime point (first contact, above). Second, at that point the two Spheres' $x_4$-momentum components are antiparallel in a common frame — the emitter's $+ic$ and the absorber's $+ic$-in-its-own-frame reading as $-ic$ along the shared axis in the emitter's frame — so the $x_4$-momentum sum vanishes, and four-momentum conservation (translation invariance of the derived Lorentzian metric) requires the cancelled $x_4$-momenergy to reappear in the spatial components $x_1 x_2 x_3$, rotating both participants out of $x_4$-dominated advance and localizing them at the point. The outcome is a single localized event because the first meeting of two expanding Spheres is one point and momentum cancellation there deposits the localization. This is the geometric content of the collapse Step 3–4: the observer's branch is realized as a definite localized event, not because a stochastic reduction acts, but because the detection interaction is a pointlike first-contact collision at which conservation localizes the participants. Definiteness of localization is a consequence of the expansion geometry, read off the first-contact structure rather than postulated as (R)."*

*What remains open — the seed, not the definiteness (verbatim from §XI.5-bis of [MG-Philosophy]).* *"The geometry fixes that the outcome is one point and that its probability is the Born intensity (Proposition III.1, recovered as the collision rate). What it does not fix is which first-contact point is realized on a given trial — equivalently, which pair of secondary Huygens sources on the two wavefronts, across the dense population of source pairs whose sub-spheres can reach mutual first-contact, constitutes the collision. The distribution over which point is realized is the SO(3)-invariant Sphere measure of Proposition III.1; the selection of one point on one trial is the seed. Whether the seed is fixed by sub-wavefront configuration not tracked in $\psi$ (a hidden-variable completion the secondary-source hierarchy could in principle support) or is irreducibly chancy is not determined by the geometry stated here, and the framework forces neither — consistent with §V.6's statement that the framework supplies Born probabilities without deterministic prediction of individual outcomes and is not a hidden-variable theory."*

McGucken's contribution here: Theorem 22.5.21.3 consolidating and importing verbatim §XI.5-bis of [MG-Philosophy] establishing that a detection event is the first-contact collision of two expanding McGucken Spheres at a single point on the line between the two source events, with the pointlike character of the collision derived from the geometry of expansion-from-zero rather than postulated as stochastic reduction; identification of the $x_4$-momentum cancellation at the collision as the mechanism by which four-momentum conservation deposits the localization at the collision point, supplying outcome definiteness at the modulus boundary as a geometric consequence rather than as a postulated projection; the sharp separation between what the geometry fixes (single-outcome definiteness plus the SO(3)-invariant Sphere measure over which point is realized) and what remains open (the seed's determinism status), narrowing the measurement problem's outcome-definiteness half to a derived geometric fact and leaving only the seed as the interpretation-independent residue.

#### 22.5.21.5 Full Verbatim Import of the Fifteen Theorems and Propositions 10.12S.1 through 10.12S.19 of the Two-Atom Double-Slit Corpus Paper [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11] and Its Flagship Treatment [MG-Minkowski-Hilbert, §10.12septies]

The following fifteen theorems and propositions are the full content of the two-atom double-slit derivation as transcribed in [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11] from the companion corpus paper [MG-TwoAtom] and its flagship treatment [MG-Minkowski-Hilbert, §10.12septies]. Numbering 10.12S.1 through 10.12S.19 is preserved from the source to avoid collision with the flagship's numbering. Equation labels (S.1) through (S.6) are local to this transcribed block. The barrier is reflecting in Theorems 10.12S.1 through 10.12S.6 and absorbing in Theorem 10.12S.8; both cases are part of the content.

**Theorem 10.12S.1 (T-invariance — Full Verbatim Import from [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11]).** *The wave equation $\square\, \psi = -4\pi\rho$, the source-free Maxwell equations, and the Schrödinger equation with real potential are each invariant under time reversal: if $\psi(\mathbf{r}, t)$ is a solution, so is $\psi(\mathbf{r}, -t)$ (wave; Maxwell with $\mathbf{B} \to -\mathbf{B}$) or $\psi^*(\mathbf{r}, -t)$ (Schrödinger).*

*Proof.* *"For the wave equation $\partial_t^2$ is even in $t$. For Maxwell, the substitution $t \to -t$, $\mathbf{E} \to \mathbf{E}$, $\mathbf{B} \to -\mathbf{B}$, $\mathbf{j} \to -\mathbf{j}$ maps the equations to themselves. For Schrödinger, complex conjugation of $i \partial_t \psi = H \psi$ with $H$ real gives $-i \partial_t \psi^* = H \psi^*$, the original equation in $-t$."* $\blacksquare$

*Textbook anchor.* *"This is standard (Jackson §6.10; Sakurai §4.4); it is stated because the rest turns on it — the equation does not orient time, so whatever orients time is added to it."*

*The two Green's functions.* *"The Helmholtz equation (S.1) has two Green's functions,"*
$$G_\pm(\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{r}') = \frac{e^{\pm i k |\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{r}'|}}{4\pi |\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{r}'|}, \tag{S.2}$$
*"which with the time factor $e^{-i\omega t}$ are the retarded (outgoing, $G_+$) and advanced (incoming, $G_-$) solutions, related by"*
$$G_-(\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{r}') = G_+(\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{r}')^*. \tag{S.3}$$
*"Both satisfy (S.1); the equation is indifferent between them. This is the Ritz–Einstein point of 1909."*

**Proposition 10.12S.2 (Forward Amplitude — Full Verbatim Import from [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11]).** *Atom $A$ emits the retarded solution $U_A(\mathbf{r}) = G_+(\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{r}_A)$. With a reflecting barrier, the field on side $N$ is given by the Rayleigh–Sommerfeld integral over the aperture plane,*
$$U_A(\mathbf{r}_N) = \frac{1}{2\pi} \iint T(x, y)\, U_A(x, y, 0^-)\, \frac{\partial}{\partial z}\!\left(\frac{e^{i k L_N}}{L_N}\right) dx\, dy, \qquad L_N = |\mathbf{r}_N - (x, y, 0)|, \tag{S.4}$$
*and the probability that $B$ absorbs is proportional to $|U_A(\mathbf{r}_B)|^2$, the two-slit interference weight at $\mathbf{r}_B$.*

*Proof.* *"Kirchhoff–Rayleigh–Sommerfeld diffraction for an aperture in a plane screen (Born and Wolf §8.3); the restriction to $S_1 \cup S_2$ is the two-source coherence producing interference at $\mathbf{r}_B$."* $\blacksquare$

*Notation.* *"Denote the forward field on all of side $N$ by $U_A|_N$; it is an extended field determined on the entire half-space by the aperture data, and $U_A(\mathbf{r}_B)$ is one value of it."*

**Theorem 10.12S.3 (Exact Reversal Requires the Advanced Solution — Full Verbatim Import from [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11]).** *The time-reverse of the forward process is the solution $U_A^*$. On side $N$ it is the incoming, phase-conjugate field $U_A^*|_N$, which converges through the apertures onto $\mathbf{r}_A$; it is the advanced solution $G_-(\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{r}_A)$ restricted to the two-slit geometry.*

*Proof.* *"Apply Theorem 10.12S.1 to the forward solution: $\psi_A(\mathbf{r}, t) = U_A(\mathbf{r}) e^{-i\omega t}$ maps to $\psi_A(\mathbf{r}, -t)$, spatial part $U_A^*(\mathbf{r})$; by (S.3), $U_A^* = G_-(\cdot, \mathbf{r}_A)$ filtered by $T$, incoming on $\mathbf{r}_A$."* $\blacksquare$

**Theorem 10.12S.4 (A Point Emitter Produces the Retarded Solution — Full Verbatim Import from [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11]).** *Atom $B$ re-emitting produces $U_B(\mathbf{r}) = G_+(\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{r}_B)$, the outgoing spherical wave centered on $\mathbf{r}_B$, its restriction to the aperture plane $z = 0^+$ having phase fixed by the distance from $\mathbf{r}_B$ to each point of $S_1 \cup S_2$.* *"Which of $G_\pm$ describes emission is a property of the emitter, and it is the retarded one."*

**Theorem 10.12S.5 (Non-Retracing — Full Verbatim Import from [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11]).** *With a reflecting barrier, the re-emission from $B$ does not retrace the forward path. The field on side $M$ is*
$$U_B(\mathbf{r}_M) = \frac{1}{2\pi} \iint T(x, y)\, U_B(x, y, 0^+)\, \frac{\partial}{\partial z}\!\left(\frac{e^{i k L_M}}{L_M}\right) dx\, dy, \tag{S.5}$$
*an extended diffraction pattern over side $M$. The probability that $A$ absorbs is proportional to $|U_B(\mathbf{r}_A)|^2$, and by Helmholtz reciprocity $U_B(\mathbf{r}_A) = U_A(\mathbf{r}_B)$, so the return probability equals the forward interference weight at $B$, which is strictly less than the total weight over side $M$.*

*Proof.* *"By Theorem 10.12S.3, exact retracing requires the boundary data $U_A^*|_{z = 0^+}$, the conjugate of the forward field, an extended converging wavefront. By Theorem 10.12S.4, $B$ supplies $U_B|_{z = 0^+}$, the restriction of an outgoing spherical wave. The two agree at no point in general; the overlap of $U_B|_N$ with $U_A^*|_N$ is the single complex number $\langle U_A^*, U_B \rangle \propto U_A(\mathbf{r}_B)^*$, one component of the continuum exact reversal requires. The remainder of $U_B$ diffracts afresh through the apertures and spreads over side $M$ by (S.5); reciprocity $G_+(\mathbf{r}_A, \mathbf{r}_B) = G_+(\mathbf{r}_B, \mathbf{r}_A)$ gives the return amplitude."* $\blacksquare$

**Corollary 10.12S.6 (The Asymmetry Is Not Geometric — Full Verbatim Import from [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11]).** *The map from the field on side $M$ to the field on side $N$ through a reflecting two-slit partition is unitary on the transmitted subspace and is inverted exactly by the conjugate boundary data of Theorem 10.12S.3. The double-slit geometry therefore does not produce the irreversibility; its role is to spread the boundary data exact reversal requires over an extended aperture, so the mismatch between the required incoming wavefront and the outgoing wavefront a point atom supplies is visible at every point of the aperture plane.*

*Proof.* *"The reflecting barrier conserves the field norm; transmitted and reflected components are orthogonal projections. Phase conjugation of the transmitted field, propagated back, reconstructs $U_A$ on side $M$ (Theorem 10.12S.3); this is realized experimentally by time-reversal mirrors (Fink 1992)."* $\blacksquare$

*Interpretive consequence (verbatim from [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11]).* *"The reading in which the partition 'discards information' so that geometry alone forbids reversal is therefore wrong: with a reflecting barrier nothing is discarded, the blocked component returns into side $M$ and remains in the system, and reversal fails for one reason only — the emitter is oriented."*

**Theorem 10.12S.8 (Absorption Adds Non-Unitarity — Full Verbatim Import from [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11]).** *If the barrier absorbs, the blocked component $U_A [1 - T]$ leaves the two-atom-plus-field system. The forward evolution restricted to that system is non-unitary, and the reverse process initiated by $B$ has no access to the absorbed component; exact reversal then fails even with conjugate boundary data on side $N$.*

*Proof.* *"The absorbed component is transferred to barrier degrees of freedom outside the system; a reversal prepared on side $N$ alone reconstructs at most the transmitted component $U_A\, T$, and the reconstructed field on side $M$ differs from $U_A$ by the back-propagation of $U_A [1 - T]$."* $\blacksquare$

*Independence of Theorems 10.12S.5 and 10.12S.8 (verbatim).* *"Theorems 10.12S.5 and 10.12S.8 are independent: the first holds with a reflecting barrier and no absorption, the second with conjugate boundary data and no point-emitter restriction. Only the first survives when everything removable is removed, and it is the one the thought experiment isolates."*

**Theorem 10.12S.10 (Retarded Selection Is a Sign Choice — Full Verbatim Import from [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11]).** *The retarded and advanced Green's functions of the wave operator are the two boundary values of the same analytic function,*
$$\tilde G(\mathbf{k}, \omega) = \frac{1}{k^2 - \omega^2/c^2}, \qquad G_{\mathrm{ret}} \leftrightarrow \omega \to \omega + i\varepsilon, \quad G_{\mathrm{adv}} \leftrightarrow \omega \to \omega - i\varepsilon, \tag{S.6}$$
*and the choice between them is the sign of the infinitesimal imaginary displacement of the frequency, equivalently the sign of the imaginary part of the time coordinate in the Fourier kernel $e^{-i\omega t}$.*

*Proof.* *"The poles of (S.6) at $\omega = \pm c k$ are displaced into the lower half $\omega$-plane by $+i\varepsilon$, so the inverse transform vanishes for $t < 0$ (retarded); the opposite displacement gives vanishing for $t > 0$ (advanced)."* $\blacksquare$

*Location of the asymmetry (verbatim from [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11]).* *"This is the exact location of the asymmetry: the equation is symmetric (Theorem 10.12S.1), emission is oriented (Theorem 10.12S.4), and the orientation is the sign in (S.6). Every account of irreversibility at the level of a single emission event must supply that sign, and the accounts differ in what they add to the field equation to supply it — Ritz (1908–1909) adds a rule, use $G_+$; Wheeler–Feynman (1945) adds a perfect-absorber boundary condition on the totality of absorbers; the standard thermodynamic account adds a low-entropy initial condition. None derives the sign from a prior kinematic fact about events."*

**Theorem 10.12S.11 (The Principle Selects the Retarded Propagator — Full Verbatim Import from [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11]).** *Under $dx_4/dt = ic$, the Fourier kernel of time evolution acquires the imaginary displacement of Theorem 10.12S.10 with the sign fixed by the $+$ of $+ic$, so that the Green's function selected is $G_{\mathrm{ret}}$. Emission from a point atom is therefore outgoing as a consequence of the Principle.*

*Derivation.* *"The Principle identifies the direction of advance in $x_4$ with the direction of increasing $t$ through $x_4 = ict$: as $t$ increases, $x_4$ moves in the $+i$ direction. The Wick substitution $t \to -i\tau$, $\tau = x_4/c$, is under the Principle the coordinate identification between $t$ and the advance in $x_4$ rather than an analytic continuation (Theorem 6 of the Wick-necessity companion [MG-Wick]). The $+i\varepsilon$ prescription of (S.6) is the infinitesimal form of that identification: displacing $\omega$ by $+i\varepsilon$ is equivalent to giving $t$ a small imaginary part of sign fixed by the orientation of $x_4$-advance, and $+ic$ fixes that orientation as $+$. With the displacement sign fixed, Theorem 10.12S.10 yields $G_{\mathrm{ret}}$, and a point source then emits the outgoing wave $G_+$, which is Theorem 10.12S.4."* $\blacksquare$

**Corollary 10.12S.12 (The Two-Atom Double Slit Exhibits the Principle's Orientation — Full Verbatim Import from [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11]).** *In the two-atom experiment, non-retracing (10.12S.5) follows from point emission being outgoing (10.12S.4), which follows from 10.12S.11, which follows from $dx_4/dt = ic$. The experiment therefore exhibits, in a single emission event with no environment and no statistics, the time orientation that the Principle yields.* *"Under the Principle the same $+ic$ that orients emission generates the expanding McGucken Sphere from every event, and the interference weight $|U_A(\mathbf{r}_B)|^2$ of Proposition 10.12S.2 is the Born weight carried by the SO(3)-Haar measure on that Sphere (Remark 7.17), so in this system the orientation of emission and the interference weight at $B$ have a common origin."*

**Table 22.5.21.A (Four Accounts of Retardation, by What Each Adds to the Time-Symmetric Field Equation — Full Verbatim Import of Table 10.12S.A from [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11], McGucken far-left).**

| Account | What is added | Level | Sign origin | In two-atom system |

| McGucken, $dx_4/dt = ic$ | The physical expansion of $x_4$ at every event, with the Sphere's wavelength setting $h$ | Prior to Green's functions | The $+$ in $+ic$ | Yes (Theorem 10.12S.11) |
| Ritz, retarded-only | A rule: use $G_+$ | Green's-function level | Postulated | Yes, as postulate |

*Table 10.12S.A caption (verbatim from [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11]).* Accounts of retardation, by what each adds to the time-symmetric field equation.

*Unitarity: the operator and the realized process (verbatim from [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11]).* *"The system separates two claims the word 'unitary' usually joins."*

**Proposition 10.12S.15 (The Evolution Is Unitary — Full Verbatim Import from [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11]).** *With a reflecting barrier, the field evolution from any state on side $M$ to the corresponding state on side $N$ is norm-preserving and invertible (Corollary 10.12S.6).*

**Proposition 10.12S.16 (The Realized Process Is Not the Unitary Inverse of the Forward Process — Full Verbatim Import from [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11]).** *The forward process ends with the excitation localized on $B$. The reverse process, initiated by $B$, ends with the excitation localized on $A$ with probability $|U_A(\mathbf{r}_B)|^2$ and elsewhere on side $M$ otherwise. In neither direction is the final state the image of the initial state under $U$ or $U^{-1}$: each process ends in a definite absorption, and the step from the extended field $U_B|_M$ to the excitation on one atom is a projection, not a unitary map.*

*Proof.* *"$U_B|_M$ is an extended field with support over side $M$ (S.5); absorption by a single atom takes it to a state supported on one atom, a projection onto that atom's excited state with weight $|U_B(\mathbf{r}_A)|^2$, and a projection is not norm-preserving on the full field."* $\blacksquare$

*Compatibility of Propositions 10.12S.15 and 10.12S.16 (verbatim from [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11]).* *"Both propositions hold, and they are compatible: unitarity is a property of the evolution operator between emission and absorption, while the realized process contains two further steps, the oriented emission (Theorem 10.12S.4) and the localized absorption (Proposition 10.12S.16), neither of which is an instance of the unitary operator. Two quantities present at the start of the reverse process are absent at its end: the extended field $U_B|_M$ with its value at every point of side $M$ (after $A$ absorbs, those values are gone), and the advanced solution $G_-$ (of the two solutions the equation permits, one is realized and the other discarded before propagation begins). The two-atom system contains no environment into which to defer the projection: either the projection occurs and the field values on the rest of side $M$ are lost, or the excitation remains spread over side $M$ and $A$ has not absorbed."*

**Proposition 10.12S.19 (The Measured Event Is What Exists — Full Verbatim Import from [MG-TwoAtom] via [MG-Philosophy, §XI.3.11]).** *In the two-atom system the measurement is absorption at $A$. That event is oriented (Theorem 10.12S.4), definite (Proposition 10.12S.16), and not the reverse of the forward event (Theorem 10.12S.5); information is lost when it occurs. The unitary operator predicts the weight of the event and contains no orientation and no outcome. Under $dx_4/dt = ic$ the orientation of every event is fixed by law, and the measured orientation is a theorem (Theorem 10.12S.11).* *"Physics being defined by what is measured, and the measured event here being oriented, definite, and irreversible, the operator-level statement that evolution is unitary between emission and absorption holds of the operator and does not transfer to the realized process — the reversibility is a property of the mathematics, the irreversibility of the outcome is the physics. This is the minimal system in which the three components — unitary evolution, oriented emission, localized absorption — can be separated and named, and it exhibits the $+ic$ orientation with two atoms, one partition, one excitation, and one measurement."*

Where Cramer needs an advanced confirmation wave returning from the detector to the source to enforce that only one detection occurs, the McGucken framework needs only that the wavefront is one $x_4$-coincident object and that its registration is a single first-contact event — both forward, neither retrocausal."*

#### 22.5.21.9 Diagnostic Case 13 — Wheeler–Feynman Absorber Theory and Cramer's Transactional Interpretation as Formal Reconstructions of the McGucken Sphere's Forward Expansion at Rate $c$ in the $+ic$ Direction

**McGucken Principle anchor.** Under $dx_4/dt = +ic$, the retarded-over-advanced Green's-function selection is a local geometric fact of the McGucken Sphere at every event — the sign $+$ of the principle at each emission event $p_E$ selects $\Sigma_+(p_E)$ and excludes $\Sigma_-(p_E)$ (Theorem 22.5.21.2, Theorem 10.12S.11). **Wheeler–Feynman absorber theory (1945, 1949) as formal reconstruction.** John Wheeler and Richard Feynman [J. A. Wheeler and R. P. Feynman, "Interaction with the Absorber as the Mechanism of Radiation," *Reviews of Modern Physics* 17, 157–181 (1945); "Classical Electrodynamics in Terms of Direct Interparticle Action," *Reviews of Modern Physics* 21, 425–433 (1949)] proposed the absorber theory of radiation as an explanation for the retarded-over-advanced Green's-function selection: the classical action $S = \sum_{i < j} \int \delta(s_{ij}^2)\, \dot{x}_i^\mu\, \dot{x}_j^\nu\, \eta_{\mu\nu}\, d\tau_i\, d\tau_j$ is time-symmetric (uses half-retarded plus half-advanced Green's functions symmetrically), and the observed retarded-only radiation is derived as a consequence of a future absorber's collective advanced wave from all future absorbers cancelling the emitter's advanced wave while reinforcing the emitter's retarded wave — supplying the retarded-only radiation observed empirically. Hogarth 1962 [J. E. Hogarth, "Cosmological Considerations of the Absorber Theory of Radiation," *Proceedings of the Royal Society A* 267, 365–383 (1962)] generalized the argument to FLRW cosmology, requiring specific cosmological topology with perfect absorption.

Under the McGucken $dx_4/dt = +ic$ framework, the Wheeler-Feynman derivation is a formal reconstruction of the local geometric fact supplied by the sign $+$ of the principle. The Wheeler-Feynman absorber's collective advanced wave from all future absorbers is a cosmological-scale device that reproduces the local retarded-only selection which the sign $+$ of $dx_4/dt = +ic$ at every event supplies directly (Theorem 22.5.21.2, Theorem 10.12S.11). Table 22.5.21.A records this: the Wheeler-Feynman account operates at the cosmological level with sign origin "absorber response" and requires absorbers beyond the two atoms; the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ account operates prior to Green's functions with sign origin "the $+$ in $+ic$" and is realized entirely within the two-atom system without cosmological input. The Wheeler-Feynman intuition — that classical electrodynamics is time-symmetric and the observed retarded-only radiation requires an additional principle — is correct and is preserved in the McGucken framework; the additional principle Wheeler-Feynman located in the collective advanced wave from all future absorbers is replaced by the local sign $+$ of the principle at each emission event, which supplies the same retarded-only selection without requiring cosmological-scale absorption or perfect absorption conditions on the future.

**Cramer's Transactional Interpretation (1986, 2016) as formal reconstruction.** John Cramer [John G. Cramer, "The transactional interpretation of quantum mechanics," *Reviews of Modern Physics* 58, 647–687 (1986); John G. Cramer, *The Quantum Handshake: Entanglement, Nonlocality and Transactions* (Springer, 2016), Ch. 1] extended Wheeler-Feynman absorber theory to quantum mechanics in the Transactional Interpretation, retaining the time-symmetric formal machinery of advanced and retarded waves and interpreting quantum-mechanical wavefunctions and their complex conjugates as offer and confirmation waves respectively. ### 22.5.22 The Einsteinian Methodological Frame — $dx_4/dt = ic$ as One Universal Elementary Law from Which the §22.5 Arc is Built up by Pure Deduction, in the Shared Simplicity-and-Unification Tradition of Newton, Maxwell, Einstein, Dirac, Weinberg, Feynman, and Wheeler

Under the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ — the fourth dimension physically expanding at rate $c$ from every spacetime event — the arc developed at §§22.5.1–22.5.10 realizes the methodological standard for physics that Einstein set in the 1933 Herbert Spencer Lecture and that Newton, Maxwell, Dirac, Weinberg, Feynman, and Wheeler upheld in their own contributions to the tradition. The standard is that a foundation is measured by two ratios: how few independent premises are posited, and how much of the cosmos is built up from them by pure deduction. §22.5 exhibits these ratios explicitly for $dx_4/dt = ic$ in the thermodynamic, relativistic-geometric, quantum-geometric, and quantum-measurement domains, with every descent given as a theorem with proof referenced in the corpus. This subsection makes the methodology explicit, grounds it in the tradition, and states the standard against which the §22.5 arc — and the whole McGucken corpus — is offered.

**The Einsteinian supreme task.** Einstein stated the standard in the 1933 Herbert Spencer Lecture at Oxford (verbatim):

> *"The supreme task of the physicist is to arrive at those universal elementary laws from which the cosmos can be built up by pure deduction. There is no logical path to these laws; only intuition, resting on sympathetic understanding of experience, can reach them."*
> — Albert Einstein, *On the Method of Theoretical Physics*, Herbert Spencer Lecture, Oxford, 10 June 1933.

Einstein's own practice enacted the standard. Special Relativity (1905) descended from two premises (invariance of physical laws across inertial frames, constancy of $c$) to a rewriting of space, time, and mass–energy. General Relativity (1915) descended from one premise (the Equivalence Principle) to spacetime curvature as the physical account of gravity. The unified field theory Einstein pursued in the last decades of his life was the same enterprise sought at a further level.

**The shared simplicity-and-unification tradition.** The standard Einstein articulated was already the standard of the tradition:

*Isaac Newton, Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica (1687), Book III, Rule I of Reasoning in Philosophy (verbatim):*

> *"Nature is pleased with simplicity, and affects not the pomp of superfluous causes."*

Newton unified terrestrial and celestial mechanics under three laws of motion plus one law of universal gravitation. The falling apple and the orbiting Moon descend from the same premise.

*James Clerk Maxwell, A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field (1865):* Maxwell unified electricity, magnetism, and light into four differential equations, proving that seemingly disparate physical phenomena can be different faces of a single underlying field. His work established that unification-by-deduction is a physical outcome, not a philosophical aspiration.

*Paul Dirac, "The Evolution of the Physicist's Picture of Nature," Scientific American (May 1963), verbatim:*

> *"It is more important to have beauty in one's equations than to have them fit experiment."*

Dirac's own practice: the mathematical elegance of a first-order relativistic wave equation forced the existence of antimatter as a theorem, confirmed experimentally by Anderson in 1932.

*Richard Feynman, The Character of Physical Law (1965), verbatim:*

> *"You can recognize truth by its beauty and simplicity... When you get it right, it is obvious that it is right — primarily because it turns out that it is more beautiful than it was expected to be, and more simple."*

*Steven Weinberg, Dreams of a Final Theory (1992):* Weinberg's Nobel-recognized unification of the electromagnetic and weak forces embodied the tradition; his subsequent writing identifies a theory's beauty with its inevitability — the sense that no simple premise or constant could be altered without collapsing the whole logical framework.

*John Archibald Wheeler (verbatim):*

> *"Behind it all is surely an idea so simple, so beautiful, so compelling that when — in a decade, a century, or a millennium — we grasp it, we will all say to each other, 'Oh, how could it have been otherwise! How could we have been so blind for so long?'"*

Wheeler's "it from bit" thesis carried the enterprise one step further: the ultimate premise of the universe is information-theoretic, with physical reality descending from binary answers to yes-no questions.

**The Wheeler lineage of $dx_4/dt = ic$.** The McGucken Principle traces to Wheeler's Princeton mentorship of Elliot McGucken in 1989–1990, documented in the Historical Note of [494]. Wheeler's own directive in those conversations — that the closure of the quantum–gravity gap must come not from quantizing gravity but from finding a deeper physical principle that supplies both the geometry and the quantum — is the directive $dx_4/dt = ic$ enacts. Wheeler's "it from bit" reads in the McGucken framework as descending itself from a deeper physical layer: the stepped $x_4$-advance at rate $ic$ supplies the "it" (the physical quantized expansion) beneath the "bit" (the measurement outcome). Wheeler's optimism that the ultimate premise would be "an idea so simple, so beautiful, so compelling" is the standard the McGucken framework offers its answer against: one premise, $dx_4/dt = ic$, from which the four pillars of physics descend by pure deduction.

**How §22.5 exhibits the Einsteinian ratios.** The §22.5 arc gives six deductive descents from the single premise $dx_4/dt = ic$, each a theorem with proof in the corpus:

### D.2 The Quanta Magazine article, December 13, 2024 — verbatim record of the six sub-theses

Zack Savitsky, *"What Is Entropy? A Measure of Just How Little We Really Know,"* Quanta Magazine, December 13, 2024, https://www.quantamagazine.org/what-is-entropy-a-measure-of-just-how-little-we-really-know-20241213/. The article organises the discourse into six positions.

**Sub-thesis 1 (observer-relativity).** Verbatim: "entropy, as it's currently understood, is less a fact about the world than a reflection of our growing ignorance." And: "Entropy is seen not as a property intrinsic to a system but as one that's relative to an observer who interacts with that system." Anchored to Rovelli, Jaynes, Aguirre, Renner.

**Sub-thesis 2 (probabilistic Second Law).** Verbatim: "The heat in Carnot's engine flows from hot to cold because it's more probable for the gas particles to be all mixed up rather than segregated by speed... The second law becomes an intuitive probabilistic statement: There are more ways for something to look messy than clean." Anchored to Boltzmann 1877, Gibbs 1902.

**Sub-thesis 3 (Past Hypothesis).** Verbatim: "The Second Law $dS/dt > 0$ requires an extraordinarily low-entropy past as an unexplained boundary condition — the Past Hypothesis — which Penrose estimates requires one part in $10^{10^{123}}$ ... fine-tuning of the early-universe Weyl curvature." Anchored to Penrose 1979, Albrecht, Carroll.

**Sub-thesis 4 (observational entropy).** Verbatim: "Aguirre and collaborators have devised a new measure they call observational entropy. It offers a way of specifying which properties a given observer has access to by adjusting how those properties blur, or 'coarse-grain,' the observer's view of reality. It then attributes equal probability to all microstates compatible with those observed properties, just as Jaynes proposed." Anchored to Šafránek, Deutsch, Aguirre 2020; Strasberg 2024.

**Sub-thesis 5 (information IS entropy).** Verbatim: "It's a very beautiful interlocking picture of information and entropy. Entropy is information we don't know; information is information we do know." Anchored to Shannon 1948, Landauer 1961, Bennett 1982, Lloyd.

**Sub-thesis 6 (entropy as anthropocentric quantity).** Verbatim, from Jaynes as the article quotes him: "entropy is an anthropomorphic concept, not only in the well-known statistical sense that it measures the extent of human ignorance as to the microstate. Even at the purely phenomenological level, entropy is an anthropomorphic concept. For it is a property, not of the physical system, but of the particular experiments you or I choose to perform on it." And the article's closing: "Entropy, in other words, is what makes us human."

### D.3 The reader response, Hacker News thread December 14, 2024 — verbatim record of the physical objections

Discussion at https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42415386, 158 comments as of retrieval date. The thread contains a sustained set of objections from physics-educated commenters against the article's central sub-theses. The objections are physical, not rhetorical, and the article does not answer any of them.

**Objection O1 (Kergonath, Dec 14 2024, reply to kqr).** Verbatim: "It is not mundane, and it is also not right, at least for entropy in Physics and Thermodynamics... But entropy is also something that we can get from experimental measurements. In this case, the experimental setup does not care about microstates and macrostates, it just has properties like enthalpy, heat capacity and temperature... Fundamentally, entropy depends on the probability distribution, not the observer."

**Objection O2 (tsimionescu, Dec 15 2024, reply to BenoitEssiambre).** Verbatim: "Maxwell's demon is a thought experiment that involves a magical being. It's an interesting thought experiment, and it provides some insights about the relationship between macro states and micro states, but it's not actually a refutation of anything, and it doesn't describe any physically realizable system, even in theory... This is obviously visible in the observer-independence of many phenomena linked to temperature. A piece of ice will melt in a large enough bath of hot water regardless of whether you know the microstates of every atom in the bath and the ice crystal."

**Objection O3 (tsimionescu, Dec 15 2024, on the whifnium example).** Verbatim: "if two people had access to the same gas tank, and one knew that there were two types of argon and the other didn't, so they would compute different entropies, one of them would still be wrong about how much work could be extracted out of the system. If whifnium did exist, but it was completely unobtainable, then both physicists would still not be able to extract any work out of the system... this also proves that the system had the same entropy even before humanity existed, and so the knowledge of the existence of whifnium is irrelevant to the entropy of the system."

**Objection O4 (goatlover, Dec 15 2024, on the Big Bang).** Verbatim: "the arrow of time depends on the universe being in a high entropy state when the Big Bang happened. There were no observers then. Also, the 2nd law of thermodynamics doesn't depend on observers. The universe overall will continue to evolve into a higher entropy state without any intelligent observers making measurements."

**Objection O5 (daoboy, Dec 14 2024, on the interactive graphic).** Verbatim: "The interactive graphic that tries to show entropy is subjective doesn't sit right for me. They fail to properly define the macrostate of the system under consideration, then show two different observed entropies for two different macrostates (Colors for Alice and Shapes for Bob). That doesn't show entropy is subjective, it shows that defining the system is subjective. The same two macrostates would still have the same entropy."

**Objection O6 (Serenade, Dec 14 2024).** Verbatim: "They are confusing defining the system with defining the entropy of a system and then saying it's the entropy that is subjective. That isn't the case at all. Entropy is just a measurement."

**Objection O7 (pixl97, Dec 15 2024).** Verbatim: "an even more limiting measure of entropy shows that entropy isn't subjective. That is entropy is the ability to extract useful work from a system by moving the system from a state of lower entropy to a state of higher entropy (in a closed system). No subjective measure of entropy can allow you to create a perpetual motion machine. The measurements of any two separate closed systems could be arbitrary, but when said systems are compared with each other units and measurements standardize."

**Objection O8 (Jensson, Dec 15 2024, on Maxwell's demon).** Verbatim: "The ice cube would melt, it would just take longer, heat does transfer through vacuum via radiation. And no, you can't control the positions of the electrons to stop that radiation from happening, it is a quantum effect not something you can control."

**Objection O9 (tsoukase, Dec 14 2024, on tautology).** Verbatim: "the Second thermodynamic law is a tautology: 'every system tends to higher entropy state because it is more common' becomes 'the more common is the more common'."

**Objection O10 (rwoerz, Dec 15 2024, on discretisation).** Verbatim: "I don't get the example under 'What is entropy?'. This works only under the assumption that reality (phase space in particular) is somehow 'pixelated'. If reality is continuous, 9 particles that are clumped together can already be in uncountably many states."

**Objection O11 (kergonath, Dec 14 2024, on subjectivity of Jaynes's programme).** Verbatim: "By the look of it, it is another misguided attempt to apply information theory concepts to thermodynamics. Entropy as information is seductive because that way we think we can understand it better, and it looks like it works. But we need to be careful because even though we can get useful insights from it (like Hawking radiation) it's easy to reach unphysical conclusions."

These eleven objections make up the physical objectivist case that the article does not address. Their common structure: entropy has an observer-independent physical grounding (a calorimeter reading, the melting of ice, the work extractable from a heat bath, the Big Bang before observers, the Sackur–Tetrode gas-mixing measurement) that no relabeling as ignorance dissolves. The Quanta piece answers none of these, in part because the piece has no physical mechanism to point to — it can only cite Jaynes, who cast entropy as anthropomorphic, and Aguirre, who parameterises the coarse-graining without deriving it.

### D.4 The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ reading, point-by-point

#### D.4.1 The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ reading of Sub-thesis 1 (observer-relativity)

The McGucken Principle — the fourth dimension physically expanding at rate $c$ from every spacetime event, $dx_4/dt = ic$ — is universal at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$. That universality has two supports: the coordinate identity in the $x_4 = ict$ convention (the integrated coordinate shadow of the Principle), and the physical fact that the shadow's rate takes the same value at every event, including events near horizons and along photon worldlines. The rate is worldline-independent, matter-independent (GR Theorem 2, the McGucken-Invariance Lemma: $\partial(dx_4/dt)/\partial g_{\mu\nu} = 0$), and frame-independent in the sense that every observer's local reading of the rate is the full $ic$ (Lemma 4.7).

What varies from observer to observer is the observer's *share* in the expansion, quantified by the Sphere-tangent velocity component $v_{x_4} = \sqrt{c^2 - v^2} = c \cdot d\tau/dt = c/\gamma$ on timelike worldlines, with the direct evaluation $v_{x_4} = 0$ on null worldlines (photons at rest in $x_4$). This resolves the article's central sub-thesis on physical grounds. The subjectivists (Rovelli, Jaynes, Aguirre) are correct that a finite observer resolves only a coarse-grained view of a physical system, and that the specific coarse-graining choice determines the numerical entropy. The objectivists in the comment thread (Kergonath O1, tsimionescu O2 and O3, Serenade O6, pixl97 O7) are correct that the underlying physical process is observer-independent. The McGucken Principle supplies what neither side names: the physical process is $dx_4/dt = ic$, universal at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$; the observer's finite resolution is a fact about the observer, not about the physics; and the Cloaking Theorem (Theorem 39, Chapter 20) closes the loop by explaining why local ruler-and-clock metrology cannot detect the preferred foliation the Principle induces, since local metrology is built from $c$ itself and cannot resolve the rate that generates $c$.

McGucken's contribution here: an ontological grounding for entropy that neither Boltzmann (who used probability without physical mechanism) nor Jaynes (who used epistemic-ignorance without physical mechanism) nor Aguirre (who parameterises coarse-graining without deriving it) could provide. The physical rate is the Principle; observer-relative entropies are what finite observers record of it.

### D.5 Historical framing — two centuries of deferring the physical mechanism

The Quanta article organises its narrative as a chronological progression from Carnot (1824) through Boltzmann and Gibbs (1877, 1902) through Shannon (1948) and Jaynes (1957) to Aguirre and Rovelli (2020s). The article presents this progression as the maturation of physics. The McGucken Principle reads the same chronology as two centuries of deferring the physical mechanism.

**Carnot 1824 (*Réflexions sur la puissance motrice du feu*, Bachelier, Paris).** Carnot derived the efficiency bound for heat engines from the caloric theory. He identified a quantity whose non-decrease sets the efficiency limit. He did not derive the quantity from a mechanical principle; he inferred it from the empirical impossibility of extracting more work than the temperature difference supports. The physical mechanism is deferred.

**Clausius 1865 (*Über verschiedene für die Anwendung bequeme Formen der Hauptgleichungen der mechanischen Wärmetheorie*, Ann. Phys. 125:353).** Clausius named the quantity "entropy" ($\eta\tau\rho o\pi\dot{\eta}$, transformation), gave it the algebraic form $dS = \delta Q_{\text{rev}}/T$, and stated the Second Law as "the entropy of the universe tends to a maximum." He supplied the phenomenological definition without the underlying mechanism. The physical mechanism is deferred.

**Boltzmann 1877 (*Über die Beziehung zwischen dem zweiten Hauptsatz und der Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung*, Wiener Berichte 76:373).** Boltzmann proposed $S = k_B \ln W$, identifying entropy with the logarithm of the number of microstates compatible with a macrostate. This required the Stosszahlansatz (the assumption of molecular chaos) to derive the H-theorem. Loschmidt (1876) and Zermelo (1896) raised objections that Boltzmann's mechanical derivation cannot answer without an additional postulate about initial conditions. Boltzmann's retreat: from mechanical determinism to probabilistic averaging. The physical mechanism is replaced by a statistical postulate.

**Gibbs 1902 (*Elementary Principles in Statistical Mechanics*, Yale University Press).** Gibbs supplied the ensemble formalism and the principle of equal *a priori* probabilities. The formalism is mathematically elegant; the *a priori* postulate is not derived. The physical mechanism is displaced by an axiomatic choice of measure.

**Shannon 1948 (*A Mathematical Theory of Communication*, Bell System Technical Journal 27:379).** Shannon derived his information-entropy formula $H = -\sum p_i \log p_i$ from communication-channel axioms. Von Neumann's suggestion to Shannon that he call the quantity "entropy" was made on the observation of formal similarity, not physical identity. The information-entropy identification is a formal analogy; the physical mechanism is not addressed.

**Jaynes 1957 (*Information Theory and Statistical Mechanics*, Physical Review 106:620 and 108:171).** Jaynes cast thermodynamics as a species of statistical inference. Given constraints, assign the probability distribution of maximum entropy compatible with them. The physical mechanism is replaced by an epistemic principle. Jaynes was explicit about this: entropy is anthropomorphic, a property of the experimenter's choice of variables and not of the physical system.

**Rovelli 1996 onward (*Relational Quantum Mechanics*, International Journal of Theoretical Physics 35:1637; and later work on relational thermodynamics).** Rovelli generalises the relational reading of quantum mechanics to entropy: quantities are relative to the observer with whom the system interacts. The physical mechanism is replaced by a relational structure.

**Aguirre, Šafránek, Deutsch 2020 (*Observational entropy and thermodynamics*, Physical Review Letters 125:190602 and later).** Observational entropy parameterises the coarse-graining and computes the Shannon entropy of the coarse-grained distribution. The physical mechanism is not derived; the coarse-graining is a free parameter fixed by observer capabilities.

**McGucken 2008 onward ([186], [12], [30], and the present paper).** The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ supplies the physical mechanism that every step in the above chronology defers. The Sphere at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$ carries the Haar measure that Gibbs postulated. The $+ic$ chirality supplies the mechanical asymmetry that Boltzmann needed the Stosszahlansatz to smuggle in. The Compton coupling of Theorem 4 supplies the physical realisation of the chirality break at every event of the massive-particle sector. The strict Second Law $dS/dt > 0$ of Theorem 9 is a derived theorem, replacing the probabilistic tendency of Boltzmann–Gibbs. The FRW cosmology of Theorem 18 supplies the low-entropy early universe as a derived consequence, replacing the Past Hypothesis. The observational-entropy framework of Aguirre is preserved as a valid epistemic account of what a finite observer resolves of the same underlying process.

The two-century pattern: at each step, the discourse deferred the physical mechanism and moved to an epistemic or postulational replacement. The McGucken Principle reverses the pattern at its root by supplying the physical mechanism that generates the Haar measure, the chirality, the low-entropy past, and the coarse-graining structure as derived consequences of a single physical fact about the geometry of spacetime.

### D.6 Philosophical framing — the two-level reading

The Quanta article celebrates a single-level reading of entropy: entropy is observer-dependent, information is entropy, and the maturation of physics is the acknowledgement of this dependence. The comment thread objections (O1–O11) are one-level rebuttals from the opposite side: entropy is observer-independent, calorimeter readings are physical, and the article's reading is wrong.

The McGucken Principle supplies a two-level reading that reconciles both sides at their strongest.

**Level 1 (physical, universal, observer-independent).** The Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ holds at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$. The Sphere at every event carries the Haar measure. The Compton coupling of Theorem 4 realises the $+ic$ chirality in the massive-particle sector. The strict Second Law $dS/dt > 0$ of Theorem 9 is a derived rate. The FRW cosmology of Theorem 18 is a derived solution. None of this depends on observers.

**Level 2 (epistemic, finite, observer-relative).** Every finite observer resolves only a coarse-grained view of the underlying physical process. The observer's choice of state variables (temperature and pressure, or partial pressures of components, or particle-by-particle microstates) determines the numerical entropy they record. The Cloaking Theorem (Theorem 39, Chapter 20) explains why local metrology cannot detect the preferred foliation the Sphere induces, and why finite observers therefore resolve the same class of coarse-grainings up to their measurement precision.

Both levels are correct at what they describe. The comment-thread objectivists (O1, O2, O3, O4, O6, O7, O8) are right about Level 1: the physical mechanism is observer-independent, calorimeter readings are physical, the Big Bang was low-entropy before observers existed, ice melts whether or not one knows the microstates. The article's subjectivists (Jaynes, Rovelli, Aguirre) are right about Level 2: finite observers with finite computational resources resolve coarse-grained macrostates and the numerical entropy they record depends on their coarse-graining choice. The two levels are compatible because they describe different things: Level 1 describes the physical process (the McGucken Sphere's expansion at every event), Level 2 describes the observer's finite resolution of that process (the coarse-graining the observer's capabilities permit).

The McGucken Principle supplies Level 1. Level 2 is a valid epistemic account of what a finite observer records of Level 1. Neither the article nor the comment thread has both levels together, because neither has a physical mechanism for Level 1 to point to.

336. **[DengHaniMa2024]** Deng, Y., Hani, Z., \& Ma, X.\ (2024). *Hilbert's sixth problem: derivation of the Boltzmann equation from Newton's laws.* arXiv:2408.07818 [math.AP]. Rigorous derivation of Boltzmann's equation on $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $d \geq 2$ from Newton's laws applied to a hard-sphere particle system, valid on arbitrarily long time intervals up to the maximal lifespan of the strong solution of the Boltzmann equation. Extends Lanford's 1975 short-time result to the long-time regime through a layered cluster forest expansion and molecule analysis with new estimates on collision histories. The authors describe their result as* "a justification of the emergence of the time irreversible Boltzmann theory from the time reversible Newton's theory near Maxwellian" *and identify the passage from time-reversible microscopic to time-irreversible mesoscopic descriptions as a* "fundamental intriguing question." *Engaged in Theorem 28.9.1 of the present paper as the primary source for the kinetic-limit half of the Newton-to-fluid pipeline, with the framework's position on the structural relationship to $dx_4/dt = ic$ published in [McGuckenHilbertSixth2026, §11.9].)

(Follow-up paper of the Deng--Hani--Ma pair. Extends the Boltzmann derivation of [DengHaniMa2024] to the periodic torus $\mathbb{T}^d$ for $d \in \{2, 3\}$ (Theorem 1, their Definitions 1.1--1.4) and chains it with the hydrodynamic limit results of Gallagher--Tristani [GallagherTristani] and Caflisch [Caflisch1980]/Guo--Jang--Jiang [GuoJangJiang] to derive the incompressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system (Theorem 2, their (1.19)) and the compressible Euler equation (Theorem 3, their (1.40)) as effective equations for the macroscopic density, velocity, and temperature of the particle system. The authors' own summary of the contribution:* "we rigorously derive the fundamental PDEs of fluid mechanics, such as the compressible Euler and incompressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier equations, starting from the hard sphere particle systems undergoing elastic collisions.
